# The Story of Micah and the Tribe of Dan

## Micah’s Shrine and the Levite

...to the Lord. And his mother said regarding the eleven hundred pieces of silver <note>original: "arguriou" — silver pieces, likely shekels, a very large sum of money</note> about which you swore and spoke in my ears: "Behold, the silver is with me; I took it."

And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by the Lord." And he returned the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother. And his mother said, "I have truly dedicated <note>original: "agiasmō hēgnika" — I have set apart as holy or consecrated</note> the silver to the Lord from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image <term>carved and cast image — "glypton kai chōneuton," a cultic object involving a wooden core covered in molten metal, strictly forbidden by the Law of Moses</term>. And now I will give it back to you."

And he returned the silver to his mother; and his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to the silversmith, and he made it into a carved and cast image, and it was in the house of Micah. 

And the man Micah had a house of God <note>original: "oikos theou" — here referring to a private shrine or chapel rather than the central Tabernacle</note>, and he made an ephod and teraphim <term>ephod and teraphim — an "ephod" was a ritual vestment and "teraphim" were household idols, both used in this period for seeking oracles</term>, and he ordained <note>original: "eplērōsen tēn cheira" — literally "filled the hand," a technical term for priestly ordination</note> one of his sons, and he became a priest for him. **In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did what was pleasing in his own eyes.**

And there was a young man from Bethlehem of the family of Judah, a Levite <note>term: Levite — a member of the tribe of Levi, traditionally designated for religious service, though this young man is wandering for work</note>, and he was staying there. And the man departed from the city of Bethlehem to live wherever he might find a place, and he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, as he went on his way. 

And Micah said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to live wherever I may find a place." And Micah said to him, "Stay with me, and be a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten pieces of silver per year, and a suit of clothes <note>original: "zeugos imatiōn" — literally a "yoke" or pair of garments</note>, and your living expenses." 

And the Levite went in and began to live with the man, and the young man was to him like one of his sons. And Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest and stayed in the house of Micah. Then Micah said, "Now I know that the Lord will do me good, because I have a Levite as my priest."

<margin>18:1</margin> **In those days there was no king in Israel.** And in those days the tribe of Dan was seeking an inheritance for themselves to live in, for an inheritance had not fallen to them <note>This refers to the tribe's failure to fully secure the territory originally allotted to them near the Philistine border</note> among the tribes of Israel until that day.

<column-break/>

And the sons of Dan sent five men from their clan, from their whole number—men of valor from Zorah and from Eshtaol <note>original: "Araa kai Esthaol" — the same region where Samson lived</note>—to scout the land and to track it out. And they said to them, "Go and explore the land." 

And they came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and they lodged there. While they were at the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young Levite, and they turned aside there. 

And they said to him, "Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? What do you have here?" And he said to them, "Thus and so Micah has done for me; he has hired me and I have become his priest." And they said to him, "Inquire of God <note>original: "eperōtēson dē en tō theō" — a request for an oracle or divine guidance</note>, so that we may know if the way on which we are traveling will be successful."

Now the sons of **Eli** the priest were worthless sons <note>original: "υιοι λοιμοι" — literally "pestilent sons," often translated as "sons of Belial."</note>; they did not know the **Lord**. And the custom of the priest from all the people who were sacrificing was this: the priest’s servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged meat-hook <note>original: "κρεαγρα τριοδου"</note> in his hand. And he would thrust it into the basin, or into the kettle, or into the pot, or into the cauldron; and everything that the meat-hook brought up, the priest took for himself. Also, before the fat was burned, the priest’s servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give meat to roast for the priest; for I will not take boiled meat from you out of the kettle." ### The Rise of Samuel and the War with the Philistines

<columns>
And you shall set forth his <note>original: "ΑΠΟΘΗΣΝΩΠΟΝ" — This word is likely a transcription error in the original manuscript or the OCR, perhaps referring to a "hidden thing" or "revelation."</note> as he did for **Moses**.

And the **Lord** continued to appear in **Shiloh**, because the **Lord** revealed himself to **Samuel**. and **Samuel** was trusted to be a prophet to the **Lord** for all **Israel**, from one end of the land to the other.

And **Eli** was very old; and his sons continued in their ways, and their path was evil before the **Lord**.

And it happened in those days that the **Foreigners** <term>original: "Αλλόφυλοι" (Allophyloi) — This is the standard Greek term used in the Septuagint to refer to the Philistines.</term> gathered for war against **Israel**. And **Israel** went out to meet them in battle; and they camped at **Ebenezer**, while the **Foreigners** camped at **Aphek**. And the **Foreigners** drew up their battle lines against **Israel**, and the battle spread. And the men of **Israel** were defeated before the **Foreigners**; and four thousand men were struck down in the ranks in the open field.

And the people came back into the camp, and the elders of **Israel** said: "Why has the **Lord** defeated us today before the **Foreigners**? Let us take the **Ark of the Covenant** of our **God** from **Shiloh** to be with us, so that it may come and save us from the hand of our enemies."

So the people sent to **Shiloh**, and they carried from there the **Ark of the Covenant** of the **Lord of Hosts** <note>original: "Σαβαώθ" (Sabaoth) — A Hebrew title for God meaning "of armies" or "of hosts."</note> who sits upon the **Cherubim**. And the two sons of **Eli**, **Hophni** and **Phinehas**, were there with the **Ark of the Covenant** of **God**.

<column-break/>

### The Victory at Mizpah and the Ebenezer Stone

...to the **Lord** <note>original: "κν" (κύριον) — a shorthand for "Lord" used in sacred texts.</note> your **God** <note>original: "θν" (θεόν) — shorthand for "God."</note>, and he will save us from the hand of the **Foreigners** <term>original: "αλλοφύλων" (Allophyloi) — the standard Greek term for the Philistines.</term>.

## Chapter 16

And the lords <note>original: CΑΤΡΑΠΑΙ (satraps), meaning governors or rulers.</note> of the **Philistines** came up to her and said to her, "Deceive him, and see wherein his great strength lies, and by what means we may overpower him and bind him to humble him. And **Delilah** said to **Samson**, "Please tell me wherein your great strength lies, and with what you might be bound to be humbled."

And **Samson** said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings <note>original: ΝΕYΡΑΙC (neurais), referring to cords made of animal sinew or gut.</note> that have not been dried, then I shall become weak

<column-break/>

and be like any other man."

And he snapped the bowstrings as a strand of flax <note>original: CΤYΠΠΙΟY, the coarse part of flax or hemp.</note> might be snapped when it smells the **fire** <term>fire</term> <gloss>pyr</gloss>. And the secret of his strength was not known.

And **Delilah** took new ropes and bound him with them. And the ambush was waiting in the inner chamber. And she said to him, "The **Philistines** are upon you, **Samson**!" And he snapped them off his arms like a thread.

And **Delilah** said to **Samson**, "Behold, you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me now with what you might be bound."

And she said, "The **Philistines** are upon you, **Samson**!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom from the wall.

# 1 KINGDOMS (1 SAMUEL)
## Chapter 25

And David’s young men came and spoke to **Nabal** <note>original: ΝΑΒΑΛ</note> according to all these words in the name of **David** <note>original: ΔΑΔ, abbreviation for Δαυίδ</note>. And **Nabal** jumped up and said to **David’s** servants, answering, “Who is **David**? And who is the son of **Jesse** <note>original: ΙΕΣCΑΙ</note>? And shall I take my bread, my wine, and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers <note>term: shearers — workers who cut the wool from sheep; a time of harvest and celebration</note> and give them to men when I do not know where they are from?”

And **David’s** young men turned back on their way and returned, and they came and reported to him all these words. And **David** said to his men, “Let every man gird on his sword!” And each man girded on his sword, and **David** also girded on his own sword. And about four hundred men went up after **David**, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.

And one of the servants reported to **Abigail** <note>original: ΑΒΙΓΑΙΑ</note>, **Nabal’s** wife, saying, “Behold, **David** sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our lord, but he turned away from them. Yet the men were very good to us; they did not hinder us, nor did they demand anything from us all the days we were with them. Now **David** had said, “Surely in vain I have guarded all that belongs to this man in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that he had; and he has repaid me evil for good. And when **Abigail** saw **David**, she hurried and jumped down from her donkey, and fell before **David** on her face and bowed down to the ground. She fell at his feet and said, “Upon me, my lord, let the iniquity be. Please let your servant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your servant. Let not my lord set his heart against this worthless man, against **Nabal**; for as his name is, so is his folly. **Nabal** <note>The name Nabal literally means "foolish" or "senseless" in Hebrew</note> is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your servant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent. And now, my lord, as the **Lord** <note>original: KC, abbreviation for Κύριος</note> lives and as your soul lives, the **Lord** has withheld you from coming to shed innocent blood and from saving with your own hand. And now, let your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord become like **Nabal**.”

# The King’s Return and the Reconciliation of his Subjects

And Mephibosheth <note>original: Μεπφιβοσθε (Mephibosthe), the son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul</note>, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his nails <note>original: ωρωνυχισεν (ōrōnychisen), a specific term for nail-care</note>, nor trimmed his mustache, nor washed his clothes from the day the king departed until the day he arrived back in peace.

And it happened, when he entered Jerusalem <note>original: ΙΛΗΜ (Ierousalēm), written as a sacred name with an overline</note> to meet the king, that the king said to him: "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"

And Mephibosheth said to him: "My lord, O King, my servant deceived me <note>original: παρηκουσε (parēkouse), literally 'disobeyed' or 'ignored,' here implying a betrayal by his servant Ziba</note>. And Mephibosheth said to the king: "Let him even take it all, now that my lord the king has come home in peace to his own house."

This is a title for a prophet or messenger of God.</note> had done on that day in **Bethel**, and the words which he had spoken to the king. And they turned the face of their father <note>An idiomatic way of saying they got his attention or changed his mind.</note>, and their father spoke to them, saying: "Which way did he go?" And his sons showed him the path that the **man of God** who came from **Judah** had taken. And he said to his sons: "Saddle the donkey for me." And they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.

And he went after the **man of God** and found him sitting under an **oak tree** <note>original: "δρυν" (dryn). While often translated as oak, it refers generally to a large, sturdy tree providing shade.</note>. And he said to him: "Are you the **man of God** who came from **Judah**?" And he said: "**I am**." And he said to him: "Come with me and eat bread." But he said: "I will not be able to return with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place. For it was commanded to me by the <term>word of the Lord</term> <note>original: "εν λογω κυ" (en logo kyriou). And he said to him: "**I also am a prophet like you**, and an angel spoke to me by the **word of the Lord**, saying: 'Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.'" **But he lied to him.** So he returned with him, and he ate bread in his house and drank water.

<column-break/>

And it happened, as they were sitting at the table, that the **word of the Lord** came to the prophet who had brought him back. And he cried out to the **man of God** who had come from **Judah**, saying:

"Thus says the **Lord**: Because you provoked the **word of the Lord** <note>The Greek term suggests a bitter rebellion or disobedience.</note> and did not keep the commandment which the **Lord your God** commanded you, but you returned and ate bread and drank water in this place of which He spoke to you, saying: 'You shall not eat bread and you shall not drink water'—**your body shall not enter into the tomb of your fathers.**"

And it happened, after he had eaten bread and drunk water, that he [the old prophet] saddled the donkey for him—for the prophet whom he had brought back. And he [the man of God] returned and departed. And a **lion** found him on the road and killed him. And his body was cast aside on the road, and the donkey stood beside the body, and the **lion** also stood beside the body.

And behold, men were passing by and they saw the body cast aside on the road, with the **lion** standing next to the body. And they went in and spoke of it in the city where the **old prophet** lived.

And the one who had brought him back from the road heard it and said: "**This is the man of God** who provoked the **word of the Lord**; and the **Lord** gave him over to the **lion**, and it crushed him and killed him, according to the **word of the Lord** which He spoke." And he spoke to his sons, saying: "Saddle the donkey for me." And they saddled it. And he went and found his body cast aside on the road, and the donkey and the **lion** were standing beside the body; the **lion** had not eaten the body, nor had it crushed the donkey.

And he said to her, "Go, ask for vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors—empty vessels—and do not gather just a few. And when you have come in, close the door behind you and your sons, and pour [the oil] into all these vessels; and as they are filled, set them aside."

And she went away from him and closed the door behind her and her sons; they were bringing [the vessels] to her, and she was pouring. And it happened, when the vessels were full, she said to her sons, "Bring me yet another vessel." And they said to her, "There is not another vessel." And the oil stopped [flowing].

And it happened on a certain day that **Elisha** passed through to **Shunem** <note>original: "ΣΩΜΑΝ" (Sōman)</note>. And a great woman was there, and she urged him to eat bread. And so it was, as often as he passed by, he would turn in there to eat.

# THE CONSPIRACY OF JEHU AND THE DEATH OF JORAM

And **Jehu** <note>original: ΙΗΟΥ — the newly anointed king of Israel</note> son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against **Joram**. Now Joram was guarding **Ramoth-Gilead**, he and all of Israel, against **Hazael** king of Syria. But King Joram had returned to be healed in **Jezreel** from the wounds which the Syrians had inflicted on him during his battle with Hazael, king of Syria.

And Jehu said: “If it is your mind <note>i.e., if you support my claim to the throne</note>, let no one escape or leave the city to go and report this in Jezreel.” Then Jehu mounted his chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram king of Israel was lying there recovering from his wounds—for the archers had wounded him at **Ramoth** in the war against Hazael king of Syria—as he had found it a place of rest for his strength; he was sleeping there.

And **Ahaziah** king of Judah had come down to see Joram. Now the **watchman** <note>original: ΟCΚΟΠΟC — the sentinel</note> stood on the tower in Jezreel and saw the dust cloud of Jehu as he approached. He said, “I see a dust cloud!” And Joram said, “Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him ask: ‘Is it peace?’”

So the horseman went to meet him and said, “Thus says the king: ‘Is it peace?’” And Jehu replied, “What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me.”

And the watchman reported, saying, “The messenger reached them, but he is not returning.” 

Then he sent out a second horseman, who came to them and said, “Thus says the king: ‘Is it peace?’” And Jehu replied, “What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me.” 

And the watchman reported, saying, “He reached them, but he is not returning. And the driving is like that of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives with madness!” <note>original: ΠΑΡΑΛΛΑΓΗ — meaning in a strange or furious manner</note> And Joram said, “Yoke the chariot!” And they yoked his chariot.

<column-break/>

And Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his own chariot, to meet Jehu. They found him at the property of **Naboth the Jezreelite** <note>this location is significant because Ahab had Naboth murdered to steal this vineyard; it is the site of the family's curse</note>.

And it happened that when Joram saw Jehu, he said, “Is it peace, Jehu?” But Jehu answered, “What peace can there be, so long as the harlotries of your mother **Jezebel** and her many witchcrafts continue?”

Then Joram turned his hands <note>meaning he turned his horses to flee</note> and cried out to Ahaziah, “Treachery, Ahaziah!” But Jehu drew his bow with full strength and struck Joram between his arms <note>in the back between the shoulder blades</note>, and the arrow went through his heart; and he collapsed in his chariot.

Then Jehu said to **Bidkar** <note>original: ΒΑΔΕΚΑΡ</note>, his captain, “Pick him up and throw him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. For I remember when you and I were riding together in pairs behind Ahab his father, that the **Lord** <note>original: KC — abbreviation for Kyrios</note> took up this oracle against him: ‘Surely I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday,’ says the **Lord**, ‘and I will repay you on this very plot of ground,’ says the **Lord**. Now therefore, pick him up and throw him into the field, according to the word of the Lord.”

When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled by way of **Beth-haggan** <note>original: ΚΑΙΠΑΘΑΝ — likely a transliteration of the Hebrew for "the garden house"</note>. Jehu pursued him and said, “Strike him too!” And they struck him in his chariot at the ascent of **Gur**, which is by **Ibleam** <note>original: ΙΕΒΛΑΑΜ</note>. And he fled to **Megiddo** <note>original: ΜΑΚΕΔΔΩ</note> and died there. 

His servants carried him in a chariot to **Jerusalem** and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the **City of David**.

In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had begun to reign over Judah.

<margin>—</margin>And Jehu had stationed for himself eighty <note>The Greek text here reads ΟΚΤΩ (eight), though standard versions usually say eighty</note> men outside and said, “The man who lets escape any of the men whom I give into your hands—his life shall be for that man’s life.” 

<margin>—</margin>And it happened that as soon as he had finished making the burnt offering, Jehu said to the guards <note>original: ΠΑΡΑΤΡΕΧΟΥCΙ — literally 'those who run alongside,' the royal bodyguards</note> and to the officers <note>original: ΤΡΙCΤΑΤΑΙC — high-ranking military commanders</note>, “Go in and strike them down; let no man go out!” 

And they struck them with the edge of the sword, and the guards and officers threw them out. And they went as far as the inner shrine <note>original: ΠΟΛΕΩC ΟΙΚΟΥ — literally 'the city of the house,' referring to the inner sanctuary</note> of the house of **Baal**. And they brought out the pillar <note>original: CΤΟΛΗΝ — literally 'robe' or 'garment,' though usually interpreted as a cultic object or pillar in this context</note> of the house of **Baal** and burned it. And they broke down the pillars of **Baal**, and they demolished the house of **Baal** and turned it into latrines to this day. 

<margin>—</margin>Thus **Jehu** wiped out **Baal** from **Israel**. However, as for the sins of **Jeroboam** son of **Nebat**, which he made Israel to sin, Jehu did not depart from following them—the golden calves that were in **Bethel** and in **Dan**. 

<margin>—</margin>And the **Lord** <note>original: KC — abbreviation for 'Kyrios'</note> said to **Jehu**, “Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of **Ahab** according to all that was in my heart...”

# THE END OF JEHU’S REIGN AND THE RISE OF ATHALIAH

“...Your sons of the fourth generation shall sit upon the throne of **Israel** <note>original: ΙΣΛ — abbreviation for Israēl</note>.”

But **Jehu** did not take care to walk in the law of the **Lord** <note>original: ΚΥ — abbreviation for Kyriou</note> **God** <note>original: ΘΥ — abbreviation for Theou</note> of **Israel** with all his heart; he did not depart from the sins of **Jeroboam**, who led **Israel** into sin.

In those days, the **Lord** <note>original: ΚΣ — abbreviation for Kyrios</note> began to cut off parts of **Israel**’s territory. **Hazael** <note>The king of Aram-Damascus and a frequent enemy of Israel</note> struck them in every border of **Israel**, from the **Jordan** toward the rising of the sun: all the land of **Gilead**, the territory of **Gad**, **Reuben**, and **Manasseh**, from **Aroer** which is on the lip of the torrent **Arnon**, even **Gilead** and **Bashan**.

Now the rest of the acts of **Jehu**, and all that he did, and all his power, and his conspiracies—are these not written in the **Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel**? And **Jehu** slept with his fathers, and they buried him in **Samaria**. And **Jehoahaz** his son reigned in his place. The time that **Jehu** reigned over **Israel** in **Samaria** was twenty-eight years.

<margin>P</margin> Now when **Athaliah** the mother of **Ahaziah** <note>Athaliah was the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, married into the Judaean royal line</note> saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring. But **Jehosheba**, the daughter of King **Joram** and sister of **Ahaziah**, took **Joash** the son of **Ahaziah** and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being killed; she took him and his nurse into the bedroom. They hid him from the face of **Athaliah**, so that he was not put to death. He remained with her, hidden in the **House of the Lord** <note>The Temple in Jerusalem</note> for six years, while **Athaliah** reigned over the land.

In the seventh year, **Jehoiada** <note>The high priest</note> sent and brought the captains of the **Chorri** <term>Chorri</term> <note>original: ΧΟΡΡΙ — likely the Carian mercenaries serving as royal bodyguards</note> and the **Rasim** <term>Rasim</term> <note>original: ΡΑΣΕΙΜ — likely the 'runners' or palace guards</note>, and brought them to himself in the **House of the Lord**.

<column-break/>

And he made a covenant of the **Lord** with them and made them swear an oath in the **House of the Lord**, and he showed them the king's son. Then he commanded them, saying: “This is what you must do: a third of you who come on duty on the **Sabbath** shall keep watch over the king's house at the gate; a third shall be at the **Gate of the Ways**; and a third at the gate behind the guards. You shall keep watch over the house. Two units among you, consisting of all those who go off duty on the **Sabbath**, shall keep watch over the **House of the Lord** for the king. You shall surround the king on every side, every man with his weapon in his hand. Anyone who enters within the **ranks** <term>saderoth</term> <note>original: ΣΑΔΗΡΩΘ — the rows or ranks of guards</note> shall be put to death. Stay with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.”

The captains did exactly as **Jehoiada** the priest commanded. Each man took his subordinates—those coming on duty on the **Sabbath** along with those going off duty on the **Sabbath**—and they came to **Jehoiada** the priest. The priest gave the captains the spears and the shields that had belonged to King **David**, which were kept in the **House of the Lord**. The guards stood, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and the temple, surrounding the king.

Then he brought out the king’s son and placed upon him the **crown** <term>nezer</term> <note>original: ΝΕΖΕΡ — a royal diadem or sign of consecration</note> and the **testimony** <note>The scroll of the Law</note>. They proclaimed him king and anointed him; they clapped their hands and shouted, “Long live the king!”

When **Athaliah** heard the noise of the people running, she went to the people in the **House of the Lord**. She looked, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom...

### THE FALL OF SAMARIA AND THE EXILE OF ISRAEL

...the son of Elah [reigned] in Samaria for **nine years**. And he did what was **evil** in the eyes of the Lord <note>original: ΚΥ (Kyriou) — abbreviation for "of the Lord."</note>, though not to the same extent as the kings of Israel who were before him. Against him came up **Shalmaneser** <note>original: ϹΑΛΑΜΑΝΑϹϹΑΡ (Salamanassar)</note> king of the Assyrians, and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute <note>original: ΜΑΝΑΑ (Manaa) — from the Hebrew 'minchah', meaning a gift or grain offering, here used for political tribute.</note>.

And the king of the Assyrians discovered treachery in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to **So** <note>original: ϹΩΑ (Soa)</note> king of Egypt and did not bring the tribute to the king of the Assyrians that year as he had done before. Therefore, the king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in a **prison house**. 

And the king of the Assyrians invaded the entire land; he went up to Samaria and besieged it for **three years**. In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Halah <note>original: ΑΛΛΑΕ (Allae)</note> and on the Habor <note>original: ΑΒΩΡ (Abor)</note>, the rivers of Gozan, and in the mountains of the Medes.

And this happened because the sons of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God <note>original: ΚΩ ΘΩ (Kyrio Theo)</note>, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; they feared other gods and walked in the customs of the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the face of the sons of Israel. 

The kings of Israel acted [wickedly], and the sons of Israel devised words that were not right against the Lord their God. They built for themselves **high places** in all their cities, from the watchtower to the fortified city. They set up for themselves pillars and **sacred groves** <note>original: ΑΛϹΗ (Alse) — wooden cult objects or trees associated with the goddess Asherah.</note> upon every high hill and under every shady tree. And they burned incense there in all the high places, just as the nations did whom the Lord had removed from before them.

<column-break/>

And they made themselves associates [of evil]; they practiced carvings <note>likely referring to engraved idols or occult practices</note> to provoke the Lord <note>original: ΚΝ (Kyrion)</note> to anger. They served **idols**, concerning which the Lord had said to them, "You shall not do this thing against the Lord." 

Yet the Lord testified against Israel and against Judah by the hand of all his prophets and every seer, saying: "**Turn back** from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my ordinances and all the law which I commanded your fathers, which I sent to you by the hand of my servants the prophets."

But they did not listen; they **hardened their necks** even more than the necks of their fathers, who did not trust in the Lord their God. They rejected his ordinances and his **covenant** which he made <note>original: ΕΚΟΨΕΝ (ekopsen) — literally "cut," following the ancient Near Eastern tradition of "cutting" a sacrificial animal to seal a treaty.</note> with their fathers, and the testimonies which he warned them with. 

They went after vain things and became vain themselves... following [the nations] whom the Lord had commanded them not to imitate. They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God and made for themselves cast images—**two heifers** <note>The golden calves set up by Jeroboam I.</note>—and they made sacred groves, and they bowed down to all the host of heaven and served **Baal**.

And they passed their sons and their daughters through the **fire**, and they practiced divination and sought omens. They sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord to provoke him to anger. Therefore, the Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from his presence; none was left except the **tribe of Judah** alone.

Yet even Judah did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the customs that Israel had practiced. And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel and shook them; he gave them into the hand of those who plundered them, until he cast them out from his presence. For Israel had withdrawn from the house of David <note>original: ΔΑΔ (Dad) — abbreviation for David.</note>, and they had made **Jeroboam** the son of Nebat their king.

### THE EXILE OF ISRAEL AND THE RESETTLEMENT OF SAMARIA

And Jeroboam pushed Israel away from following the Lord <note>original: ΚΥ (Kyriou) — abbreviation for "of the Lord."</note>, and he led them to commit a great sin. And the sons of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he committed; they did not depart from them, until the Lord <note>original: ΚΣ (Kyrios) — "The Lord."</note> removed Israel from before His face, just as the Lord had spoken by the hand of all His servants the prophets. And Israel was exiled from their own land to the Assyrians, remaining there until this day.

And the king of the Assyrians brought people from Babylon, and from Cutha, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim <note>original: ΣΕΦΦΑΡΟΥΑΙΜ (Seppharouaim)</note>. And they were settled in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel; they inherited Samaria and lived in its cities. 

And it happened at the beginning of their settlement there that they did not fear the Lord. Therefore, the Lord sent lions among them, which were killing them. And they spoke to the king of the Assyrians, saying: "The nations which you relocated and resettled in the cities of Samaria do not know the custom <note>original: ΚΡΙΜΑ (krima) — literally "judgment" or "ordinance," referring here to the specific religious laws required by the local God.</note> of the God <note>original: ΘΥ (Theou) — abbreviation for "of God."</note> of the land. Therefore, He has sent lions among them, and behold, they are putting them to death because they do not know the custom of the God of the land."

And the king of the Assyrians gave a command, saying: "Lead one of the priests whom you exiled from there and let them go and settle there; and they shall teach them the custom of the God of the land." And they brought one of the priests whom they had exiled from Samaria, and he settled in Bethel and taught them how they should fear the Lord. 

But each nation continued to make their own gods, and they placed them in the houses of the high places <note>The "high places" were hilltop shrines used for local worship, often condemned by biblical writers.</note> which the Samaritans had made—each nation in the cities where they lived. And the men of Babylon made **Succoth-benoth** <note>original: ΣΟΚΧΩΘΒΑΝΩΘ (Sokchothbanoth)</note>, and the men of Cutha made **Nergal** <note>original: ΕΡΓΕΛ (Ergel)</note>, and the men of Hamath made **Ashima**, and the Avvites made **Nibhaz** <note>original: ΕΒΛΑΖΕΡ (Eblazer)</note> and **Tartak**, and the Sepharvites—

<column-break/>

—and the Sepharvites were burning their sons in fire to **Adrammelech** and **Anammelech**, the gods of Sepharvaim. 

And they were fearing the Lord, yet they also settled their abominations <note>A common biblical term for idols or pagan images.</note> in the houses of the high places which they had made in Samaria—nation by nation in the cities where they lived. And they were fearing the Lord, yet they also appointed for themselves priests for the high places; and they served the Lord within the house of the high places. They feared the Lord, but they also served their own gods according to the custom of the nations from which they had been relocated. 

Until this day, they have continued to act according to their own custom. They do [not] fear <note>The Greek text here is ambiguous, but implies a half-hearted or incorrect fear of God.</note>, and they do [not] act according to His statutes and His judgments, nor according to the law and the commandment which the Lord commanded the sons of Jacob, whom He named **Israel**. 

And the Lord had made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying: "You shall not fear other gods, and you shall not bow down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them. But the Lord, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great strength and an outstretched arm—Him you shall fear, to Him you shall bow down, and to Him you shall sacrifice. And the statutes, and the judgments, and the law, and the commandments which He wrote for you, you shall be careful to do for all your days; and you shall not fear other gods. And the covenant which He made with you, you shall not forget; and you shall not fear other gods. But the Lord your God <note>original: ΘΝ (Theon) — "God."</note> you shall fear, and He shall deliver you from all your enemies." 

But they did not listen; instead, they continued to act according to their former custom.

But the <term>Chief Butcher</term> left behind some of the poor of the land to be **vinedressers** and farmers.

And the bronze pillars that were in the house of the **Lord**, and the <term>mechonoth</term> <note>original: "ΜΕΧΩΝΩΘ" — the bronze movable stands or bases for the basins</note>, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the **Lord**, the Chaldeans broke in pieces; and they carried their bronze to Babylon. And the pots, and the shovels <note>original: "ΙΑΜΑΘ" (iamath)</note>, and the bowls, and the censers, and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered, he took away. And the fire-pans and the silver bowls and the gold ones, the <term>Chief Butcher</term> took away. As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the <term>mechonoth</term> which Solomon had made for the house of the **Lord**, there was no weighing the bronze of all these vessels. The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits <note>About 27 feet</note>, and the bronze <term>capital</term> <note>original: "ΧΩΘΑΡ" (chothar) — the decorative head of the pillar</note> was upon it; and the height of the capital was three cubits. **Network** <note>original: "ΣΑΒΑΧΑ" (sabacha)</note> and pomegranates were upon the capital all around, all of bronze. And the second pillar was like these with its network.

And the <term>Chief Butcher</term> took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the priest of the second rank, and the three who kept the <unclear>threshold</unclear>...

<meta>This page concludes the book of 4 Kingdoms (2 Kings), picking up from the immediate aftermath of the fall of Jerusalem. It details the execution of Judean officials, the short-lived governorship of Gedaliah, and the eventual release of King Jehoiachin from prison in Babylon.</meta>

# The Final Days of Judah and the Mercy of Babylon

### 2 Kings 25:19–30

He took one eunuch who was in charge of the men of war, and five men from the king's advisors who were found in the city; also the scribe of the commander of the army, the one who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city. And Nabuzardan <note>original: "ΝΑΒΟΥΖΑΡΑΔΑΝ"</note> the <term>chief cook</term> <note>original: "ΑΡΧΙΜΑΓΕΙΡΟΣ" (archimageiros) - This title traditionally meant 'chief cook' but had evolved into a high-ranking military title, similar to 'Captain of the Guard' or 'Chief Executioner.'</note> took them and led them to the king of Babylon at Riblah <note>original: "ΔΕΒΛΑΘΑ" (Deblatha)</note>. And the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath <note>original: "ΑΙΜΑΘ"</note>.

And Judah was carried away into **exile** from its land. And as for the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar <note>original: "ΝΑΒΟΥΧΟΔΟΝΟΣΟΡ"</note> king of Babylon had left, he appointed over them Gedaliah <note>original: "ΓΟΔΟΛΙΑΝ"</note> son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

And all the commanders of the army, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah; and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah <note>original: "ΜΑΣΣΗΦΑ"</note>: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan son of <unclear>Kareah</unclear>, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth <unclear>the Netophathite</unclear>, and Jaazaniah son of the <unclear>Maacathite</unclear>, they and their men. And Gedaliah swore to them and their men, and <unclear>said</unclear> to them: "Do not fear the approach of the <unclear>Chaldeans</unclear> <note>The Babylonians</note>; settle in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you."

And it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal seed, came with ten men and struck Gedaliah, and he died; and the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah. And all the people, from the small to the great, and the commanders of the army, rose up and entered into **Egypt**, for they were afraid of the face of the Chaldeans.

<unclear>And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin the king</unclear>

<column-break/>

of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, **Evil-merodach** <note>original: "ΕΥΕΙΛΑΜΑΡΩΔΑΧ"</note> king of Babylon, in the year he began to reign, lifted up the head of **Jehoiachin** <note>original: "ΙΩΑΚΕΙΜ" - Though spelled similarly to his father Jehoiakim in the Greek, this refers to the exiled king.</note> king of Judah and brought him out of the prison house. And he spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

And he changed his prison garments; and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life. And his allowance, a **continual allowance**, was given to him from the king's house, a portion for each day, all the days of his life.

# THE FIRST BOOK OF THE CHRONICLES OF THE KINGS OF JUDAH
->ΑΓ<-

### 1 Chronicles 1:1–51

**Adam, Seth, Enosh,** and **Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah.** The sons of **Noah**: **Shem, Ham,** and **Japheth.**

The sons of **Japheth**: **Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Elishah, Thokel** <note>original: "ΘΟΚΕΛ" — traditionally identified as Tubal</note>, **Meshech,** and **Tiras.**

And the sons of **Gomer**: **Ashkenaz, Riphath,** and **Thorram** <note>original: "ΘΟΡΡΑΜ" — traditionally Togarmah</note>. And the sons of **Javan**: **Elishah, Tarshish,** the **Kittim,** and the **Rodanim** <note>original: "ΡΟΔΙΟΙ" (Rodians)</note>.

And the sons of **Ham**: **Cush, Mizraim** <note>original: "ΜΕΣΡΑΙΜ" — the Hebrew name for Egypt</note>, **Phut,** and **Canaan.** And the sons of **Cush**: **Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah,** and **Sabtecha.** And the sons of **Raamah**: **Sheba** and **Dedan.**

And **Cush** begat **Nimrod** <note>original: "ΝΕΒΡΩΔ" (Nebrod)</note>; he began to be a <term>giant hunter</term> <note>original: "ΓΙΓΑΣ ΚΥΝΗΓΟΣ" (gigas kynēgos) — the Septuagint often translates the Hebrew "mighty one" as "giant."</note> upon the earth.

And **Mizraim** begat the **Ludim,** the **Anamim,** the **Lehabim,** the **Naphtuhim,** the **Pathrusim,** and the **Casluhim** (from whence came the **Philistines**), and the **Caphtorim.**

And **Canaan** begat **Sidon** his firstborn, and the **Hittite,** and the **Jebusite,** and the **Amorite,** and the **Girgashite,** and the **Hivite,** and the **Arkite,** and the **Sinite,** and the **Arvadite,** and the **Zemarite,** and the **Hamathite.**

The sons of **Shem**: **Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud,** and **Aram.** And the sons of **Aram**: **Uz, Hul, Gether,** and **Meshech.**

And **Arphaxad** begat **Cainan,** and **Cainan** begat **Shelah** <note>original: "ΣΑΛΑ" (Sala) — Cainan appears in the Greek Septuagint genealogy but not in the standard Hebrew Masoretic text.</note>, and **Shelah** begat **Eber.** And to **Eber** were born two sons: the name of the one was **Peleg** <note>original: "ΦΑΛΕΚ" (Phalek)</note>, because in his days the earth was **divided**; and his brother’s name was **Joktan.**

And the sons of **Abraham**: **Isaac** and **Ishmael.** And these are their generations: the firstborn of **Ishmael, Nebaioth;** then **Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad** <note>original: "ΧΟΔΔΑΔ" (Choddad)</note>, **Tema, Jetur, Naphish,** and **Kedemah.** These are the sons of **Ishmael.**

And the sons of **Reuel**: **Nahath, Zerah, Shammah,** and **Mizzah.**

And the sons of **Esau** <note>note: the text moves to the descendants of Seir</note>: **Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer,** and **Dishan.** And the sons of **Lotan**: **Hori** and **Hemam;** and **Lotan’s** sister was **Timna.**

The sons of **Shobal**: **Alvan** <note>original: "ΓΩΛΑΜ" (Golam)</note>, **Manahath, Ebal, Shepho,** and **Onan.** The sons of **Zibeon**: **Aiah** and **Anah.**

The sons of **Anah**: **Dishon.** And **Oholibamah** <note>original: "ΗΛΙΒΕΜΑ"</note> was the daughter of **Anah.** And the sons of **Dishon**: **Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran,** and **Cheran.**

And the sons of **Ezer**: **Bilhan, Zaavan,** and **Jaakan.** The sons of **Dishan**: **Uz** and **Aran.**

And these are the **kings** who reigned in the land of **Edom** before any king reigned over the children of **Israel**: **Bela** <note>original: "ΒΑΛΑΚ"</note> the son of **Beor;** and the name of his city was **Dinhabah.**

<meta>This page continues the genealogy of the royal line of David from 1 Chronicles 3, following the sons of Josiah through the Babylonian exile and the return under Zerubbabel. It then transitions in the second half of the first column to the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4), focusing on the families of Hur, Ashhur, and the famous prayer of Jabez.</meta>

**Column 1**

And the sons of **Josiah**: the firstborn was **Johanan** <note>original: "ΙΩΑΝΑΝ"</note>, the second **Jehoiakim**, the third **Zedekiah**, the fourth **Shallum**. And the sons of **Jehoiakim**: **Jeconiah** his son, and **Zedekiah** his son.

And the sons of **Jeconiah** <note>The captive king also known as Jehoiachin</note>: **Assir**, **Shealtiel** his son, **Malchiram**, **Pedaiah**, **Shenazzar**, **Jekamiah**, **Hoshama**, and **Nedabiah** <gloss>Abadia</gloss> <note>A variant spelling for the name Nedabiah found in the margin or between lines</note>.

And the sons of **Pedaiah**: **Zerubbabel** <note>The leader who returned from the Babylonian exile</note> and **Shimei**. And the sons of **Zerubbabel**: **Meshullam** and **Hananiah**, and **Shelomith** was their sister. And **Hashubah**, **Ohel**, **Berechiah**, **Hasadiah**, and **Jushab-hesed**—five in total. And the sons of **Hananiah**: **Pelatiah** and **Jeshaiah** his son, **Rephaiah** his son, **Arnan** his son, **Obadiah** <note>original: "ΥΙΟΣ ΑΥΤΟΥ" repeated here refers to the line of descendants</note> his son, and **Shecaniah** his son.

And the son of **Shecaniah**: **Shemaiah**. And the sons of **Shemaiah**: **Hattush**, **Igal**, **Bariah**, **Neariah**, and **Shaphat**—six in total.

And the sons of **Neariah**: **Elioenai**, **Hezekiah**, and **Azrikam**—three. And the sons of **Elioenai**: **Hodaviah**, **Eliashib**, **Pelaiah**, **Akkub**, **Johanan**, **Delaiah**, and **Anani**—seven.

<margin>4</margin> The sons of **Judah**: **Perez**, **Hezron**, **Carmi**, **Hur**, and **Shobal**. And **Reaiah** <note>original: "ΡΕΙΑ"</note> the son of **Shobal** begot **Jahath**, and **Jahath** begot **Ahumai** and **Lahad**. These are the families of the **Zorathites** <note>original: "ΣΑΡΑΘΙ"</note>. <margin>CENTONAXI</margin> <note>A marginal note likely indicating a variant reading or location name</note>

And these were the sons of **Etam**: **Jezreel**, **Ishma**, and **Idbash**; and the name of their sister was **Hazzelelponi**. And **Penuel** was the father of **Gedor**, and **Ezer** the father of **Hushah**. These were the sons of **Hur**, the firstborn of **Ephrathah**, the father of **Bethlehem**.

And **Ashhur** the father of **Tekoa** had two wives: **Helah** <note>original: "ΑΛΑΑ"</note> and **Naarah**. And **Naarah** bore him **Ahuzzam**, **Hepher**, **Temeni**, and **Haahashtari**. All these were the sons of **Naarah**. And the sons of **Helah**: **Zereth**, **Izhar** <note>original: "ΣΑΑΡ"</note>, and **Ethnan**. And **Koz** begot **Anub**, **Zobebah**, and the families of **Aharhel** <note>original: "ΑΔΕΛΦΟΥ ΡΗΧΑΒ"</note> the son of **Harum**.

And **Jabez** <note>original: "ΙΑΒΗΣ"</note> was more honorable than his brothers; and his mother called his name **Jabez**, saying, "Because I bore him in pain."

And **Jabez** called upon the God of **Israel**, saying: "If you would truly bless me and enlarge my borders, and let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm <note>original: "ΓΝΩΣΙ"</note> so that I might not be brought low!"

<column-break/>

And **God** brought about all that he had asked for.

And **Chelub** <note>original: "ΧΑΛΕΒ"</note>, the father of **Shuah** <note>original: "ΑΣΧΑΣ"</note>, begot **Mehir**; he was the father of **Eshton**. And **Eshton** begot **Beth-rapha**, **Paseah**, and **Tehinnah** the father of the city of **Nahash**, the brother of **Eselon** the **Kenizzite**. These were the men of **Recab** <note>original: "ΡΗΧΑ"</note>.

And the sons of **Kenaz**: **Othniel** and **Seraiah**. And the sons of **Othniel**: **Hathath** <note>original: "ΑΟΛΑΘ"</note>. And **Meonothai** begot **Ophrah**. And **Seraiah** begot **Joab**, the father of the **Valley of Craftsmen** <note>original: "ΡΑΓΕΙΜ"</note>, for they were craftsmen.

And the sons of **Caleb** the son of **Jephunneh**: **Iru**, **Elah**, and **Naam**. And the sons of **Elah**: **Kenaz**. And the sons of **Jehallelel**: **Ziph**, **Ziphah**, **Tiria**, and **Asarel**. And the sons of **Ezrah**: **Jether**, **Mered**, **Epher**, and **Jalon**. And **Jether** begot **Miriam**, **Shammai**, and **Ishbah** the father of **Eshtemoa**. And his wife, the **Jewess** <note>original: "ΙΔΙΑ", likely a corruption of the proper name Jehudijah</note>, bore **Jered** the father of **Gedor**, **Heber** the father of **Soco**, and **Jekuthiel** the father of **Zanoah**.

And these were the sons of **Bithiah** <note>original: "ΕΣΘΩΡ"</note> the daughter of **Pharaoh**, whom **Mered** took.

And the sons of the wife of **Hodiah** <note>original: "ΙΟΥΔΑΙΑΣ"</note>, the sister of **Naham**, the father of **Keilah** the **Garmite**, and **Eshtemoa** the **Maacathite**. And the sons of **Shimon**: **Amnon**, **Rinnah**, **Ben-hanan**, and **Tilon**.

And the sons of **Shelah** the son of **Judah**: **Er** the father of **Lecah**, and **Laadah** the father of **Mareshah**, and the families of the house of those who worked in fine linen at **Beth-ashbea**. And **Jokim**, and the men of **Chozeba**, and **Joash**, and **Saraph**, who ruled in **Moab** and returned to **Bethlehem** <note>original: "ΑΠΕΚΑΨΕΝ ΣΤΡΕΨΕΝ ΑΥΤΟΥΣ"</note>. <note>The Greek text here is difficult and appears to contain a fragment regarding the return of these families</note> These were the potters and those who lived in **Netaim** and **Gederah**; they stayed there with the king for his work and were strengthened in his kingdom.

The sons of **Simeon**: **Nemuel**, **Jamin**, **Jarib**, **Zerah**, and **Shaul**. **Shallum** <note>original: "ΘΑΛΕΜ"</note> was his son, **Mibsam** his son, and **Mishma** his son. **Hammuel** <note>original: "ΑΜΟΥΗΛ"</note> his son, **Zaccur** <note>original: "ΣΑΒΟΥΛ"</note> his son, and **Shimei** his son.

And the name of **David** became known in all the earth, and the Lord put the fear of him upon all the nations.

# THE SECOND BOOK OF CHRONICLES
## (PARALEIPOMENON II)

---

And Solomon the son of David was strengthened over his kingdom; and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him to the greatest height. And Solomon spoke to all Israel—to the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, and to all the rulers before Israel, the heads of the ancestral houses. 

And Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place <note>original: "βαμα" (bama) — a hilltop sanctuary used for worship before the Temple was built</note> that was at Gibeon; for there was the tent of the testimony of God, which Moses the servant of the Lord had made in the wilderness. But David had brought up the ark of God from the city of Kiriath-jearim; for he had prepared a tent for it long ago in Jerusalem. And the bronze altar which Bezalel <note>original: "Βεσελεηλ" (Beseleel)</note> son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the tabernacle of the Lord; and Solomon and the assembly sought it out. And Solomon brought there, upon the bronze altar before the Lord in the tent, and offered upon it a thousand burnt offerings.

> In that night, God appeared to Solomon and said to him: "Ask whatever I may give to you."

And Solomon said to God:
> "You have shown great mercy toward David my father, and you have made me king in his place. And now, Lord God, let your name be confirmed toward David my father; for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth. Now give me wisdom and understanding, and I shall go out and come in before this people. For who can judge this great people of yours?"

And God said to Solomon:
> "Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for wealth, riches, or glory, nor for the life of those who oppose you, nor did you ask for many days; but you have asked for yourself wisdom and understanding so that you may judge my people over whom I have made you king. I give you wisdom and understanding; and I will give you wealth, glory, and riches such as no king who was before you has had, and after you there shall not be any such."

And Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon to Jerusalem, from before the

<column-break/>

tent of the testimony, and he reigned over Israel.

And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen; and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen; and he stationed them in the chariot cities, and the people remained with the king in Jerusalem.

And the king made gold and silver in Jerusalem as plentiful as stones; and he made cedars in Judea as abundant as the sycamore trees in the lowlands. And Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue; the king’s merchants would go and purchase them at a set price. And they would come up and export from Egypt a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver and a horse for one hundred and fifty; and in this way, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites <note>original: "Χετταιων" (Chettaioi)</note> and the kings of Syria by their own hands.

<margin>2</margin> And Solomon determined to build a house for the name of the Lord, and a house for his kingdom. 

And Solomon gathered seventy thousand men as porters and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains, with three thousand six hundred overseers over them.

And Solomon sent word to Hiram <note>original: "Χειραμ" (Cheiram)</note> the king of Tyre, saying:
> "As you did for my father David and sent him cedars to build him a house to dwell in—and behold, I, his son, am building a house for the name of the Lord my God, to sanctify it to him, to burn incense of sweet spices before him, and for the continual setting out of the showbread <note>original: "προθεσιν" (prothesin) — the 'Bread of the Presence' displayed in the sanctuary</note>, and to offer burnt offerings continually morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, and at the New Moons <note>original: "νεομηνιαις" (neomeniais) — monthly religious festivals</note>, and at the feasts of the Lord our God; this is a duty for Israel forever. 
> 
> And the house which I am building is great; for our God is great above all gods."

And who is able to build him a house? For the heaven and the heaven of heavens do not contain <note>original: "φέρουσιν" (pherousin) — literally "bear" or "carry"</note> his glory. And who am I that I should want to build him a house, except for the purpose of burning incense before him?

And now send me a wise man, and one who knows how to work in gold, and in silver, and in bronze, and in iron, and in purple, and in scarlet, and in blue <note>original: "ὑακίνθῳ" (hyakinthō) — a deep blue or violet color derived from the hyacinth flower</note>, and one skilled in engraving, together with the wise men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father prepared. 

And send me cedar wood, and pine, and juniper from Lebanon; for I know that your servants are skilled at cutting wood in Lebanon. And behold, my servants shall work with your servants to prepare for me wood in abundance, because the house which I am building is great and glorious. And behold, for the workers who cut the wood, I have given for food to your servants: twenty thousand kors <note>original: "κόρους" (korous) — a large measure equivalent to about 10-12 bushels</note> of crushed wheat, and twenty thousand kors of barley, and twenty thousand measures <note>original: "μέτρα" (metra) — likely 'baths' for liquid measurement</note> of wine, and twenty thousand measures of oil.

And Hiram, king of Tyre, spoke in writing and sent word to Solomon: "Because the Lord loves his people, he has made you king over them." And Hiram said: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who gave to King David a wise son, and one skilled in knowledge and understanding, who shall build a house for the Lord, and a house for his kingdom. 

And now I have sent to you a wise man, skilled in understanding—Hiram, my servant. His mother was of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold and silver, in bronze and iron, in stone and wood, and to weave in purple and in blue, 

<column-break/>

and in fine linen <note>original: "βύσσῳ" (byssō) — a high-quality, expensive fabric used for royal and priestly garments</note> and in scarlet, and to engrave carvings, and to devise every design that you shall give him, along with your wise men and the wise men of my lord David your father. And now, the wheat, and the barley, and the oil, and the wine, of which my lord spoke, let him send to his servants. And we will cut wood from Lebanon according to all your need, and we will bring them in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you shall bring them to Jerusalem."

And Solomon gathered all the men who were foreigners in the land of Israel, according to the census <note>original: "ἀριθμὸν" (arithmon) — numbering or counting</note> that David his father had conducted; and there were found a hundred and fifty-three thousand and six hundred. And he made of them seventy thousand burden-bearers, and eighty thousand stone-cutters in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred overseers <note>original: "ἐπιστάτας" (epistatas)</note> over the work for the people.

<margin>3</margin>
And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared to David his father, in the place which David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. And he began to build in the second month in the fourth year of his reign. 

And these are the dimensions with which Solomon began to build the house of God: the length in cubits <note>original: "πήχων" (pēchōn) — a cubit is roughly the length of a forearm, about 18 inches</note> according to the former measure was sixty cubits, and the width was twenty cubits. And the portico <note>original: "αἰλὰμ" (ailam) — the vestibule or porch</note> across the front of the house, its length was twenty cubits (matching the width of the house), and the height was one hundred and twenty cubits; and he overlaid it on the inside with pure gold. 

And the main hall <note>original: "οἶκον τὸν μείζονα" — literally "the greater house"</note> he paneled with cedar wood and overlaid it with pure gold, and he carved on it palm trees and chains. And he adorned the house with precious stones for beauty; and the gold was gold from Parvaim <note>original: "Φαρουαϊμ" (Pharouaim) — an unidentified region famous for high-quality gold</note>. And he overlaid the house—the beams, and the thresholds, and its walls, and its doors—with gold, and he carved Cherubim <note>original: "χερουβὶν" — celestial beings associated with the presence of God</note> on the walls. 

And he made the house of the Holy of Holies; its length across the front...

# The Construction of the Temple Interior

...twenty <term>cubits</term> <note>original: "πηχέων" (pēcheōn) — a unit of measurement based on the length of the forearm, roughly 18 inches or 45 centimeters</note> in length, and its width was twenty cubits. And he overlaid it with pure gold, amounting to six hundred talents <note>A talent was a massive unit of weight; 600 talents would be roughly 20 metric tons of gold</note>. He also placed <term>cherubim</term> <note>original: "χερουβείν" (cheroubein) — celestial winged beings often depicted as guardians of sacred spaces</note> within. And the weight of the nails was fifty <term>shekels</term> of gold. He also fashioned the upper rooms with gold.

And in the most holy house, he made two cherubim, a work made of wood, and he overlaid them with gold. The wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits in length: one wing of five cubits touched the wall of the house, and the other wing of five cubits touched the wing of the other cherub. Similarly, the wing of the first cherub, being five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing of five cubits touched the wing of the other cherub.

The wings of these cherubim were spread out for twenty cubits; they stood upon their feet, and their faces were turned toward the house <note>This indicates the statues faced inward toward the main hall of the temple rather than toward the back wall</note>.

And he made the veil of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and he wove cherubim into it. And in front of the house, he made two pillars thirty-five cubits in height, and the capitals on top of them were five cubits. And he made chainwork <note>original: "σερσερώθ" (serserōth) — likely a transliteration or variation referring to decorative lattice or chains</note> in the inner sanctuary <note>original: "δαβείρ" (dabeir) — the Holy of Holies</note> and placed it on the heads of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates and placed them on the chainwork. 

And he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He called the name of the one on the right "Straightness" <note>original: "Κατόρθωσις" (Katorthōsis) — representing the Hebrew 'Jachin', meaning 'He shall establish'</note> and the name of the one on the left "Strength" <note>original: "Ἰσχύς" (Ischys) — representing the Hebrew 'Boaz', meaning 'In Him is strength'</note>.

<margin>60</margin> And he made the bronze altar, twenty cubits in length and ten cubits in width. 

And he made the "Sea" <note>A massive bronze basin used for ritual washing</note> of cast metal, ten cubits in diameter, being circular all around; its height was five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference. And the likeness of calves <note>original: "μόσχων" (moschōn) — oxen or young bulls</note> was underneath it, encircling it all around; ten cubits of them surrounded the washing

<column-break/>

basin all around in two rows. These figures were cast in one piece with the basin itself. It stood upon twelve calves: three looking toward the North, three looking toward the West, three looking toward the South, and three looking toward the East. The "Sea" was set above them, and all their hindquarters were turned inward. 

Its thickness was a handbreadth <note>original: "παλαιστής" (palaistēs) — the width of a palm, about 3 inches</note>, and its brim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a carved lily blossom. It held three thousand <term>measures</term> <note>original: "μετρητάς" (metrētas) — likely referring to 'baths', a liquid measure of about 8 gallons</note>, and it was completed.

And he made ten smaller washing basins and placed five on the right and five on the left, to wash in them the parts of the burnt offerings; but the "Sea" was for the priests to wash in. 

And he made ten golden lampstands according to their prescribed design and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. And he made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. And he made one hundred golden bowls.

And he made the court of the priests and the Great Court, and doors for the court, and he overlaid their panels with bronze. And he placed the "Sea" at the corner of the house on the right, toward the Southeast.

And Hiram <note>original: "Χειράμ" (Cheiram) — the master craftsman sent from Tyre</note> made the flesh-hooks, the fire-pans, and the grate of the altar, and all its utensils. Thus Hiram finished doing all the work that he was to do for King Solomon in the house of God: the two pillars, and the bowls of the capitals on top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals which were on top of the pillars. And he made four hundred golden bells <note>original: "κώδωνας" (kōdōnas) — though standard biblical texts usually say pomegranates, this manuscript reads "bells"</note> for the two networks, and two rows of pomegranates...

### The Bronze Furnishings and the Golden Sanctuary

...the <unclear>capitals</unclear> <note>original: "κεφαλών" (kephalōn) — the decorative tops of the pillars</note> upon the heads of the pillars; two networks of latticework to be cast upon the top of the pillars, and the ten <term>lavers</term> <note>original: "λουτῆρας" (loutēras) — large bronze basins used for ritual washing</note> which he made, and the lavers he placed upon the <term>bases</term> <note>original: "μεχωνών" (mechonōn) — movable stands for the basins</note>. He also made the one **Sea** <note>A massive bronze basin representing the primordial waters, used by the priests for purification</note> and the twelve calves <note>oxen</note> beneath it, placed under its base.

He fashioned the footbaths, the shovels, the bowls, and the flesh-hooks; and all their vessels Hiram <note>The master craftsman, often called Huram-abi in other versions</note> made and brought to King Solomon for the House of the Lord, made of **pure bronze**. In the plain of the Jordan, the King cast them in the thick clay of the ground, between Succoth and Zeredah. 

And Solomon made all these vessels in such great abundance that the weight of the bronze could not be calculated.

And Solomon made all the vessels for the House of the Lord: the **golden altar** and the tables upon which was the **Bread of Presence** <note>original: "ἄρτοι προθέσεως" (artoi protheseōs) — twelve loaves of holy bread set out before God</note>; the lampstands and the lamps for the light, according to the ordinance, to stand before the <term>Debir</term> <note>original: "λαβείρ" (labeir) — the inner sanctuary or Holy of Holies</note> of pure gold. The tongs, the lamps, the bowls, the incense burners, and the firepans were of pure gold; and the inner door of the house leading to the **Holy of Holies**, and the doors of the main temple, were overlaid with gold.

Thus all the work that Solomon did for the House of the Lord was finished. And Solomon brought in the holy things dedicated by David his father—the silver, the gold, and the vessels—and placed them in the treasury of the House of the Lord.

### The Ark is Brought to the Temple

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the chiefs of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the **Ark of the Covenant of the Lord** from the City of David, which is Zion. And all the men of Israel were assembled before the King at the festival, which is in the seventh month <note>The Feast of Tabernacles or Sukkot</note>.

<column-break/>

And all the elders of Israel came, and all the Levites took up the Ark. And they brought up the Ark, and the **Tabernacle of Testimony**, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tabernacle; the priests and the Levites brought them up.

And King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel, and those who feared God and had gathered with them, were before the Ark, sacrificing oxen and sheep which could not be numbered or counted for their great multitude.

Then the priests brought the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord into its place, into the <term>Debir</term> of the house, into the **Holy of Holies**, beneath the wings of the <term>Cherubim</term>. For the Cherubim spread their wings over the place of the Ark, and the Cherubim overshadowed the Ark and its carrying poles from above. The poles were so long that the ends of the poles could be seen from the holy place in front of the Inner Sanctuary, but they could not be seen from the outside; and they remain there to this day. 

There was nothing in the Ark except the **two tablets** which Moses placed there at Horeb <note>Mount Sinai</note>, where the Lord made a covenant with the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.

And it happened, when the priests came out of the Holy Place—for all the priests present had sanctified themselves, not keeping to their usual divisions—and the Levite singers, including all those of **Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun**, along with their sons and brothers, were clothed in fine linen. Standing at the east end of the altar with cymbals, harps, and lyres, they were joined by one hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets.

And it happened that as one voice, they blew the trumpets and sang, raising a single voice to give thanks and praise to the Lord...

But they shall be his servants, so that they may know the difference between my service and the service of the kingdoms of the earth."

So Shishak king of Egypt went up and took the treasures in the house of the <term>Lord</term> and the treasures in the king's house; he took everything. He even took the gold shields which Solomon <note>original: "Σαλωμων"</note> had made. And King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place, and he appointed over them the keepers of the gate, the commanders of the runners who guarded the king's gate.

And it happened that whenever the king entered the house of the <term>Lord</term>, the guards and the runners would come and take them, and then return them to the guardroom of the runners.

And when he was humbled, the wrath of the <term>Lord</term> turned away from him and did not destroy him completely; for indeed, there were good and pleasing things found in Judah.

And Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the <term>Lord</term> chose out of all the tribes of Israel <note>original: "Ιηλ"</note> to put his name there. And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess. And he did evil, because he did not direct his heart to seek the <term>Lord</term>.

Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, the first and the last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer <note>original: "Αδδω του οραντος"</note>? And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

And Rehoboam died and was buried with his fathers in the City of David <note>original: "Δαδ"</note>. And Abijah his son reigned in his place.

# THE WOE OF THE WEALTHY AND THE VISIONS OF AMOS

Upon the mountain of Samaria, they gathered the firstfruits of the nations and entered in themselves. O house of Israel <note>original: "ΙΗΛ", a shortened form of Israel used by scribes.</note>, pass through, all of you, and see; and go from there to Hamath the Great <note>original: "ΑΜΑΘ ΡΑΒΒΑ", an ancient city in Syria.</note>, and go down from there to Gath of the Philistines—the strongest of all these kingdoms—to see if their borders are greater than your borders.

Those who pray for an evil day, those who draw near and touch false Sabbaths; those who sleep on beds of ivory and live in luxury upon their couches; who eat lambs from the flocks and suckling calves from the midst of the herds; who clap their hands to the sound of musical instruments. They considered these things to be permanent and not fleeting. They drink filtered wine and anoint themselves with the finest oils, and they felt nothing for the crushing of Joseph <note>The "crushing of Joseph" refers to the social and political ruin of the northern tribes of Israel.</note>. 

Therefore, now <margin>Captives</margin> they shall be the first of the captives to go into exile, and the neighing of horses shall be taken away from Ephraim. For the Lord <note>original: "ΚΣ", abbreviation for *Kyrios*.</note> has sworn by himself: "I abhor all the pride of Jacob, and I have hated their lands; I will remove the city along with all who inhabit it." And if there should be ten men left in a single house, they shall die. But a remnant shall be left, and their kinsmen shall take them and try to carry their bones out of the house. And one will say to those presiding over the house: "Is there anyone still with you?" and he will say: "No more." And he will say: "Be silent! For we must not name the name of the Lord <note>original: "ΚΥ", abbreviation for *Kyriou*.</note>." 

For behold, the Lord commands, and he will strike the great house with ruins and the small house with breaches. Will horses run upon rocks? Will they keep silent <column-break/> among the females? <note>This is a difficult passage in the Greek Septuagint; where the Hebrew text describes plowing with oxen, the Greek suggests a loss of natural order or industry.</note> For you have turned judgment into wrath and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness. For behold, O house of Israel, I am raising up a nation against you, and they will afflict you so that you shall not enter into Hamath, even unto the Brook of the West.

And destruction shall rise like a river, and it shall descend like the river of **Egypt** <note>This imagery compares the coming judgment to the rising and falling of the Nile.</note>.
"And it shall be in that day," says the **Lord God** <note>original: "ΚC Ο ΘC", abbreviations for *Kyrios ho Theos*.</note>, "that the sun shall set at midday, and the light shall grow dark upon the earth in the daytime. And I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into a lament. I will bring sackcloth upon every waist and baldness upon every head, and I will make it like the mourning for a beloved son, and those with him like a day of pain."
<margin>I</margin> "Behold, the days are coming," says the **Lord**, "and I will send a famine upon the land—not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the **Lord**. And the waters of the sea shall be shaken; from the north unto the east they shall run about seeking the word of the **Lord**, and they shall not find it."
"In that day, the beautiful virgins and the young men shall faint from thirst—those who swear by the atonement <note>original: "ΙΛΑCΜΟΥ", referring to the idols or cultic objects of Samaria.</note> of **Samaria** and who say, 'As your God lives, O **Dan**!' and 'As your God lives, O **Beer-sheba**!' They shall fall and shall never rise again."
<margin>9:-</margin> I saw the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΝ", abbreviation for *Kyrion* (the Lord in the accusative case).</note> standing upon the altar, and He said: "Smite the altar-hearth, and the gateposts shall be shaken, and I will break them over the heads of all..."

If they hide themselves on the peak of **Carmel**, from there I will search them out and take them; and if they sink out of my sight into the depths of the sea, there I will command the **dragon** <note>original: "ΔΡΑΚΟΝΤΙ", a sea monster or serpent.</note> and it shall bite them.

And the **Lord God Almighty** <note>original: "ΚΣ Ο ΘΣ Ο ΠΑΝΤΟΚΡΑΤΩΡ", the Lord God the Ruler of All.</note> is the one who touches the earth and shakes it, and all who dwell in it shall mourn. By the sword all the sinners of my people shall die, those who say, "Evil shall not draw near or come upon us."

# MICAH

### The Judgment Against Samaria and Jerusalem

And the word of the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΥ", a shortened form of "Κυρίου" (Lord).</note> came to **Micah** of **Moresheth** <note>A town in the lowland of Judah.</note> in the days of **Jotham**, **Ahaz**, and **Hezekiah**, kings of **Judah**, concerning the things he saw regarding **Samaria** and **Jerusalem**. 

Hear these words, O peoples, and let the earth and all who are in it give heed! And the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΣ", shortened form of "Κύριος".</note> shall be a witness among you, the **Lord** from his holy house. For behold, the **Lord** comes forth from his place; he will descend and tread upon the high places of the earth. The mountains shall be shaken beneath him, and the valleys shall melt like wax before a fire, and like water rushing down a steep slope. 

All these things are because of the impiety of **Jacob** and because of the sin of the house of **Israel** <note>original: "ΙΗΛ", shorthand for "Israel".</note>. What is the impiety of **Jacob**? Is it not **Samaria**? And what is the sin of the house of **Judah**? Is it not **Jerusalem** <note>original: "ΙΗΛΜ", shorthand for "Jerusalem".</note>? 

Therefore, I will make **Samaria** like a lodge for the fruit-watchers in a field, and like a planting-place for a vineyard. I will tear down her stones into the abyss, and I will uncover her foundations. All her carved images they shall cut to pieces, and all her earnings <note>original: "ΜΙΣΘΩΜΑΤΑ", referring to the wealth gained through cultic prostitution or idolatry.</note> they shall burn with fire. I will consign all her idols to destruction, because she gathered them from the earnings of harlotry, and from the earnings of harlotry they shall return. 

Because of this, she shall wail and lament; she shall walk naked and barefoot. She shall make a mourning cry like that of **dragons** <note>original: "ΔΡΑΚΟΝΤΩΝ", likely referring to the howling of jackals.</note> and a lamentation like that of the daughters of **sirens** <note>original: "ΣΕΙΡΗΝΩΝ", in this context referring to ostriches, known for their mournful cries.</note>. For her wound has prevailed; it has come even to **Judah**, and it has reached the gate of my people, even to **Jerusalem**. 

You in **Gath**, do not exalt yourselves! You in **Akeim** <note>A town name found in the Greek version, possibly corresponding to Akko or a play on words.</note>, do not rebuild! From the house of laughter, sprinkle yourselves with the dust of your laughter. And she who dwells well in her cities did not come forth—she who dwells in **Sennar** <note>The Greek name used here for a specific location, possibly Zaanan.</note>. Lament for the house neighboring her; 

<column-break/>

a plague of pain shall come upon you from her. Who has begun to bring good things to her that dwells in pain? For evil has come down from the **Lord** to the gates of **Jerusalem**. 

There is a noise of chariots and horsemen, O inhabitant of **Lachish**! She is the leader of sin for the daughter of **Zion**, because in you were found the impieties of **Israel**. Therefore, you shall give forth messengers as far as the inheritance of **Gath**. Vain houses have become as nothing to the kings of **Israel**. 

O inhabitant of **Lachish**, your inheritance shall come to **Ollalam** <note>A Greek transcription of a Hebrew place name, Adullam.</note>; the glory of the daughter of **Zion** shall arrive. Shave your head and cut your hair for your tender children; enlarge your widowhood like an eagle, for they have been taken captive.

### Social Injustice and Divine Woe

<margin>2~</margin> Woe to those who devise toil and work evil upon their beds! As soon as it was day, they carried it out, because they did not lift their hands toward **God** <note>original: "ΘΝ", shorthand for "Θεόν".</note>. They coveted fields and seized orphans; they oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance. 

Therefore, thus says the **Lord**: "Behold, I am devising evil against this tribe, from which you shall not remove your necks; and you shall not walk upright, for the time is evil." 

In that day, a parable shall be taken up against you, and a lamentation shall be sung in melody, saying: "We have become wretched in our wretchedness! The portion of my people has been measured out with a cord, and there was no one to prevent him from returning. Our fields have been divided." 

Because of this, there shall be no one to cast a measuring line by lot for you in the assembly of the **Lord**. Do not weep with tears, nor let them weep for these things; for he will not push away the reproaches of the one who speaks.
