It transitions from a lament over the total breakdown of societal trust (chapter 7) to a concluding prayer of hope, asking God to shepherd His people as He did in the days of the Exodus. The text ends with the book's title and a decorative scribal flourish.</meta>

<margin>7 <note>The number 7 likely marks the beginning of the final chapter.</note> Take heed</margin> **W**oe is me! For I have become as one gathering straw in the harvest and as a gleaning in the vintage, when there is no cluster of grapes to eat the firstfruits.
Woe to my soul! For the godly man has perished from the earth, and there is no one who walks uprightly among men. All are judged in blood; each one oppresses his neighbor. They prepare their hands for oppression.
The prince asks, and the judge has spoken words of peace <note>The Greek text here suggests a corrupt peace or a bribe; the judge speaks kindly while the heart plots.</note> according to the desire of his soul.
And I will take away their goods like a moth devouring, and like one walking upon a rule <note>original: "ΚΑΝΟΝΟϹ" (kanonos). This implies a strict standard or a measuring line of judgment.</note> in the day of your watchtower. Woe! Your vengeance has come; now shall be their weeping.
Do not trust in friends and do not hope in leaders. Guard yourself from your bedfellow, lest you entrust anything to her. For a son dishonors a father, a daughter will rise up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; all the men in his house are enemies.
But as for me, I will look to the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΝ", abbreviation for "Κύριον" (Lord).</note>; I will wait for **God** <note>original: "ΘΩ", abbreviation for "Θεῷ" (God).</note> my savior; my **God** <note>original: "ΘϹ", abbreviation for "Θεός" (God).</note> will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen and I shall rise; for if I sit in the darkness, the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚϹ", abbreviation for "Κύριος" (Lord).</note> shall give me light. I will bear the wrath of the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΥ", Lord's.</note> because I sinned against Him, until He Himself justifies my case. He will execute my judgment and bring me out into the light; I shall see His righteousness.
And my enemy shall see it and shall be covered with shame—she who says to me, "Where is the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚϹ", Lord.</note> your **God** <note>original: "ΘϹ", God.</note>?" My eyes shall look upon her; now she shall be for a trampling, like mire in the streets. A day for the smearing of brick; <note>This unusual phrase in the Greek Septuagint refers to the rebuilding of walls or the plastering of structures.</note> your wiping out is that day.
And that day shall push away your ordinances, and your cities shall come to a leveling and to a partitioning of the Assyrians, and your fortified cities to a partitioning,

from Tyre even to the river Euphrates <note>original: "ΕΥΡΙΑϹ", likely a scribal variant for the Euphrates.</note>, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain. The day exists and the turmoil, and the earth shall be for a desolation together with those inhabiting it, because of the fruits of their practices.
Shepherd your people with your staff, the sheep of your inheritance, those dwelling by themselves in a forest in the midst of Carmel. They shall feed in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old. And according to the days of your departure from Egypt, you shall see marvelous things.
The nations shall see and be put to shame despite all their strength; they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, and their ears shall be made deaf.
They shall lick the dust like serpents dragging themselves along the ground; they shall be confounded in their enclosure. They shall be amazed at the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΩ", Lord.</note> our **God** <note>original: "ΘΩ", God.</note> and shall be afraid of you.
Who is a **God** <note>original: "ΘϹ", God.</note> like you, taking away iniquities and passing over the impieties of the remnant of His inheritance? He has not held His anger as a witness forever, because He is one who desires mercy. He will turn back and have compassion on us; He will sink our iniquities and cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.
You will give truth to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, just as you swore to our fathers in the days of old.

### THE VISION OF OBADIAH

**T**hus says the Lord God to Idumea: I have heard a report from the Lord, and He has sent a message out to the nations: "Arise! And let us rise up against her for war!" **B**ehold, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly dishonored. The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who dwell in the clefts <note>original: "τρωγλαις" (troglies), meaning holes or caverns, referring to the rock-cut architecture of Edom.</note> of the rocks, setting his dwelling on high, saying in his heart: "Who shall bring me down to the ground?" **I**f you should soar like an eagle, and if you should set your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord. # HABAKKUK
# THE PROPHET

How long, Lord <note>original: "ΚΕ" (Kyrie), a shortened sacred form (nomen sacrum) for Lord.</note>, shall I cry out, and you will not hear?
I will shout to you, being wronged, and you will not save.
Why did you show me labors and pains to look upon, toward misery and impiety?
Judgment has occurred against me, and the judge receives <note>The Greek implies the judge accepts bribes or favors, leading to the corruption mentioned in the next line.</note>.
Because of this, the law is dispersed, and judgment is not brought to its end;
For the impious one oppresses the righteous; for this reason, judgment comes forth perverted.
Look, you scoffers, and behold, and wonder marvelously, and be vanished!
For I am working a work in your days which you will not believe, even if someone describes it to you.
For behold, I am raising up against you the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were the people of the Neo-Babylonian Empire who conquered Jerusalem in the early 6th century BCE.</note>, the fighters, the swift and bitter nation, who travel over the breadths of the earth to inherit dwellings not their own.
He is fearsome and illustrious; his judgment shall come from himself, and his capture shall come from himself.
And his horses shall leap swifter than leopards, and they are sharper than the wolves of Arabia.
And his horsemen shall ride out and charge from afar; they shall fly like an eagle eager to eat.
A full destruction shall come upon the impious, standing against their faces; and he shall gather captives like the sand.
And he shall indulge himself among kings, and tyrants are his playthings.
And he shall mock every stronghold; he shall cast up a mound and seize it.
Then his spirit shall change, and he shall pass through and offer propitiation: "This strength belongs to my god."
Are you not from the beginning, Lord <note>original: "ΚΕ" (Kyrie).</note> my God <note>original: "ΘΣ" (Theos), a shortened sacred form.</note>, my Holy One? And we shall not die.

<column-break/>

Lord, you have ordained him for judgment; and he fashioned me to prove his instruction.
Your eye is pure, so as not to see evil, and you will not be able to look upon pains.
Why do you look upon those who despise? Will you remain silent while the impious swallows the righteous?
And will you make men like the fish of the sea, and like the creeping things that have no leader?
He has pulled up the completion <note>The "completion" or "end" here refers to the total catch of people.</note> with a hook, and dragged him in a casting-net, and gathered him in his dragnets.
For this reason, his heart will be glad and will rejoice.
For this reason, he will sacrifice to his casting-net and burn incense to his dragnet, because by them he has fattened his portion and his food is choice.
Therefore, he will cast his casting-net, and he will not spare to kill nations continually.

...of those who dwell in it. **W**hat does a carved image profit, that they have carved it? He fashioned it as a molten image, a false fantasy. For the one who fashioned it trusts in his creation, to make mute idols.

**W**oe to him who says to the wood, "Wake up! Arise!" and to the stone, "Be exalted!" And this itself is a fantasy! This is an overlay of gold and silver, and there is no breath <note>original: "ΠΝΑ" (Pneuma), a shortened form for Spirit or Breath of life.</note> at all in it. But the Lord <note>original: "ΚΣ" (Kyrios).</note> is in his holy temple; let all the earth stand in awe before him.

On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of <term>Darius</term> <note>Darius I, the Great, who ruled the Persian Empire from 522–486 BCE.</note>, the word of the Lord came to Haggai the prophet, saying:
"Thus says the Lord Almighty: Ask the priests for a ruling on the law, saying: If a man takes holy meat in the fold of his garment, and the edge of his garment touches bread, or stew, or wine, or oil, or any food, will it become holy?" And the priests answered and said, "No."
And Haggai said, "If one who is defiled in soul <note>Referring to ritual impurity, usually from contact with a dead body.</note> touches any of these things, will it be defiled?" And the priests answered and said, "It will be defiled."
And Haggai answered and said, "So is this people, and so is this nation before me," says the Lord, "and so are all the works of their hands; and whoever approaches there shall be defiled because of their morning gains; they shall suffer because of their labors, and you hated those who reproved you in the gates.
And now, set it in your hearts from this day and before, even before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord: who were you? When you threw twenty <term>sata</term> <note>A dry measure, approximately 13 liters.</note> of barley into a bin, and there were only ten of barley; and you entered the wine-vat to draw out fifty <term>metretas</term> <note>A liquid measure, roughly 39 liters.</note>, and there were only twenty.
I struck you with parching heat and with wind-blight

**S**et your hearts now from this day and beyond, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, and from the day the temple of the Lord was founded; set it in your hearts whether it shall yet be known upon the threshing floor, and if the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranates, and the olive trees that do not bear fruit—from this day forward I will bless them."

<meta>This page transitions from the prophecies of Haggai, which focused on the physical reconstruction of the Temple, to the Book of Zechariah. Both prophets operated during the second year of King Darius I (520 BCE), but Zechariah’s visions are more apocalyptic and symbolic, focusing on the spiritual restoration of the people and God's role as the "Lord of All."</meta>

### ZECHARIAH I

<margin>/</margin>
**I**N THE EIGHTH MONTH OF THE SECOND YEAR OF <term>DARIUS</term> <note>Darius I, the Great, King of Persia (reigned 522–486 BCE). The date is roughly October/November 520 BCE.</note>, THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME TO ZECHARIAH THE SON OF BERECHIAH, THE SON OF IDDO, THE PROPHET, SAYING:

<margin>/</margin>
"**T**HE LORD WAS ANGRY WITH YOUR FATHERS WITH A GREAT ANGER. AND YOU SHALL SAY TO THEM: THUS SAYS THE <term>LORD ALMIGHTY</term> <note>original: "KC ΠΑΝΤΟΚΡΑΤΩΡ" (Kyrios Pantokrator), literally 'the Lord who holds all things.' In English Bibles, this is often 'Lord of Hosts.'</note>: RETURN TO ME, SAYS THE LORD OF THE POWERS, AND I WILL RETURN TO YOU, SAYS THE LORD ALMIGHTY. AND DO NOT BE LIKE YOUR FATHERS, WHOM THE FORMER PROPHETS ACCUSED, SAYING:

<margin>/</margin>
'**T**HUS SAYS THE LORD ALMIGHTY: TURN AWAY FROM YOUR EVIL WAYS AND FROM YOUR EVIL PRACTICES.' BUT THEY DID NOT PAY ATTENTION TO HEAR ME," SAYS THE LORD.

<margin>/</margin>
"**Y**OUR FATHERS, WHERE ARE THEY? AND THE PROPHETS, SHALL THEY LIVE FOREVER? BUT RECEIVE MY WORDS AND MY STATUTES, AS MANY AS I COMMAND BY MY SPIRIT <note>original: "ΠΝΙ" (Pneuma), meaning Spirit or Breath.</note> TO MY SERVANTS THE PROPHETS, WHICH OVERTOOK YOUR FATHERS."

<margin>/</margin>
**A**ND THEY ANSWERED AND SAID, "JUST AS THE LORD ALMIGHTY DETERMINED TO DO TO US ACCORDING TO OUR WAYS AND ACCORDING TO OUR PRACTICES, SO HE HAS DONE TO US."

<margin>/</margin>
**O**N THE TWENTY-FOURTH DAY OF THE ELEVENTH MONTH—THIS IS THE MONTH OF <term>SHEBAT</term> <note>A month in the Hebrew calendar, roughly January/February.</note>—IN THE SECOND YEAR OF DARIUS, THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME TO ZECHARIAH THE SON OF BERECHIAH, THE SON OF IDDO, THE PROPHET, SAYING:

<margin>/</margin>
**I** HAVE SEEN DURING THE NIGHT, AND BEHOLD, A MAN MOUNTED UPON A RED HORSE, AND HE STOOD IN THE MIDST OF THE TWO SHADOWY MOUNTAINS <note>The Hebrew text of this passage refers to "myrtle trees," but the Greek Septuagint translates the word as "shadowy mountains."</note>. AND BEHIND HIM WERE RED HORSES, AND DAPPLED, AND VARIEGATED, AND WHITE. AND I SAID, "WHAT ARE THESE, LORD?"

<margin>/</margin>
**A**ND THE ANGEL WHO WAS SPEAKING WITHIN ME SAID TO ME, "I WILL SHOW YOU WHAT THESE THINGS ARE." AND THE MAN WHO WAS STANDING IN THE MIDST OF THE MOUNTAINS ANSWERED AND SAID TO ME, "THESE ARE THE ONES WHOM THE LORD HAS SENT TO PATROL THE EARTH."

<column-break/>

<margin>></margin>
AND THEY ANSWERED THE ANGEL OF THE LORD WHO WAS STANDING IN THE MIDST OF THE MOUNTAINS AND SAID, "WE HAVE PATROLLED THE WHOLE EARTH, AND BEHOLD, ALL THE EARTH IS INHABITED AND IS AT REST."

<margin>></margin>
**A**ND THE ANGEL OF THE LORD ANSWERED AND SAID, "LORD ALMIGHTY, HOW LONG WILL YOU NOT HAVE MERCY ON JERUSALEM <note>original: "ΙΗΛΜ" (abbreviation for Ierousalem).</note> AND THE CITIES OF JUDAH, WHICH YOU HAVE OVERLOOKED? THIS IS THE SEVENTIETH YEAR."

<margin>></margin>
**A**ND THE LORD ALMIGHTY ANSWERED THE ANGEL WHO WAS SPEAKING WITHIN ME WITH GOOD WORDS AND COMFORTING SPEECH. AND THE ANGEL WHO WAS SPEAKING WITHIN ME SAID TO ME: "CRY OUT, SAYING, 'THUS SAYS THE LORD ALMIGHTY: I AM JEALOUS FOR JERUSALEM AND FOR ZION WITH A GREAT JEALOUSY. AND I AM VERY ANGRY WITH THE NATIONS THAT JOINED IN THE ATTACK; FOR WHEREAS I WAS ONLY A LITTLE ANGRY, THEY HELPED TO INFLICT EVIL.'"

<margin>/</margin>
"**B**ECAUSE OF THIS, THUS SAYS THE LORD ALMIGHTY: I WILL RETURN TO JERUSALEM WITH COMPASSION, AND MY HOUSE SHALL BE REBUILT IN HER," SAYS THE LORD ALMIGHTY, "AND A MEASURING LINE SHALL YET BE STRETCHED OUT OVER JERUSALEM." AND THE ANGEL WHO WAS SPEAKING WITHIN ME SAID TO ME: "CRY OUT, SAYING, 'THUS SAYS THE LORD ALMIGHTY: CITIES SHALL YET OVERFLOW WITH GOOD THINGS, AND THE LORD SHALL YET HAVE MERCY ON ZION AND SHALL YET CHOOSE JERUSALEM.'"

<margin>/</margin>
**A**ND I LIFTED UP MY EYES AND LOOKED, AND BEHOLD, THERE WERE FOUR HORNS. AND I SAID TO THE ANGEL WHO WAS SPEAKING WITHIN ME, "WHAT ARE THESE, LORD?"

<margin>/</margin>
**A**ND HE SAID TO ME, "THESE ARE THE HORNS THAT SCATTERED JUDAH AND ISRAEL." <note>original: "ΙΗΛ" (abbreviation for Israel).</note> AND THE LORD SHOWED ME FOUR CRAFTSMEN <note>original: "ΤΕΚΤΟΝΑΣ" (tektonas), meaning artisans, builders, or blacksmiths.</note>. AND I SAID, "WHAT ARE THESE COMING TO DO?"

<margin>/</margin>
**A**ND HE SAID TO ME, "THESE ARE THE HORNS THAT SCATTERED JUDAH AND ISRAEL; THEY BROKE THEM, AND NONE OF THEM RAISED HIS HEAD. AND THESE HAVE COME OUT TO SHARPEN THEM <note>The Greek suggests the craftsmen come to sharpen their tools or "sharpen" the horns into submission.</note> IN THEIR HANDS—THESE FOUR HORNS, THE HORNS OF THE NATIONS THAT LIFTED UP THEIR HORN AGAINST THE LAND OF JUDAH TO SCATTER IT."

### ZECHARIAH II

<margin>2.1~</margin>
**A**nd I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a man, and in his hand was a measuring line <note>original: "σχοινίον γεωμετρικόν" (schoinion geōmetrikon), literally a 'geometrical cord' used for surveying land.</note>. And I said to him, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure <term>Jerusalem</term> <note>The Greek text uses the abbreviation "ΙΛΗΜ" for Ierousalēm.</note>, to see what is its width and what is its length."

**A**nd behold, the angel who was speaking with me stood by, and another angel went out to meet him. And he spoke to him, saying, "Run and speak to that young man, saying: 'Jerusalem shall be inhabited as a fruitful place because of the multitude of <term>men</term> <note>The text uses the abbreviation "ΑΝΩΝ" (anthrōpōn).</note> and cattle in her midst. And I will be to her,' says the <term>Lord</term> <note>The text uses the abbreviation "KC" (Kyrios).</note>, 'a wall of fire all around, and I will be for glory in her midst.'"

"**O**h, flee from the land of the north!" says the Lord. "For from the four winds of <term>heaven</term> <note>The text uses the abbreviation "ΟΥΝΟΥ" (ouranou).</note> I will gather you," says the Lord. "Escape to Zion, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon!"

<margin>></margin>For thus says the <term>Lord Almighty</term> <note>original: "KC ΠΑΝΤΟΚΡΑΤΩΡ" (Kyrios Pantokrator), often translated as "Lord of Hosts."</note>: "After the glory, He has sent me to the nations that plundered you; for he who touches you is as one who touches the apple of His eye. For behold, I am bringing my hand upon them, and they shall be plunder for those who served them. And you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me."

"**S**ing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion! For behold, I am coming and I will dwell in your midst," says the Lord. "And many nations shall flee for refuge to the Lord in that day, and they shall be His people, and they shall dwell in your midst. And you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you. And the Lord shall inherit Judah as His portion in the holy land, and He shall still choose Jerusalem."

**L**et all flesh be in awe before the Lord, for He has been raised up from His holy clouds.

For behold the stone which I have set before the face of Jesus; upon that one stone are seven eyes.

### ZECHARIAH V

And I turned and lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a <term>flying sickle</term> <note>original: "δρέπανον πετόμενον" (drepanon petomenon). And I will bring it forth," says the Lord Almighty, "and it shall enter into the house of the thief and into the house of the one who swears falsely by my name; and it shall remain in the midst of his house and shall consume it, even its timber and its stones."

### ZECHARIAH V

...and he said to me: "To build for it a house in the land of Babylon, and to prepare it; and they shall set it there upon its own base."

<margin>6.</margin>And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and I looked, and behold, four chariots coming out from the midst of two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze. In the first chariot were red horses; and in the second chariot, black horses; and in the third chariot, white horses; and in the fourth chariot, dappled gray horses.

And I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my Lord?" And the angel who was speaking with me answered and said, "These are the four winds of heaven; they go forth to stand before the <term>Lord</term> <note>The text uses the abbreviation "ΚΩ" (Kyrio) for the Lord.</note> of all the earth. The chariot in which were the black horses went forth to the land of the north; and the white went forth after them; and the dappled went forth to the land of the south. And if you eat and drink, do you not eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves? Are these not the words which the Lord spoke by the hands of the prophets...'"

### ZECHARIAH VII

<margin>7</margin>...of the former [prophets], when **Jerusalem** was inhabited and prospering, along with her cities round about her, and the hill country and the plain were inhabited?

<margin>7</margin>And the word of the <term>Lord</term> <note>The text uses the Greek abbreviation "ΚΥ" for *Kyriou*, the "Lord."</note> came to **Zechariah**, saying:

"Thus says the **Lord Almighty**: Render just judgment, and show mercy and compassion every man to his brother. And do not oppress the widow, the orphan, the <term>stranger</term> <note>original: "προσήλυτον" (proselyton), referring to a resident alien or convert.</note>, or the poor; and let none of you harbor evil in your hearts against his brother."

But they refused to pay attention; they turned a stubborn back and plugged their ears so as not to hear. And they made their hearts <term>disobedient</term> <note>literally "unyielding" or "stubborn."</note> so as not to hear my law and the words which the **Lord Almighty** had sent by His Spirit through the hands of the former prophets. Therefore, great wrath came from the **Lord Almighty**.

"And it shall come to pass, just as He spoke and they did not hear Him, so they shall cry out and I will not hear," says the **Lord Almighty**. "And I will cast them out among all the nations which they have not known; and the land shall be made desolate behind them, with no one passing through or returning. They have turned a chosen land into a desolation."

<margin>8</margin>And the word of the **Lord Almighty** came, saying:

"Thus says the **Lord Almighty**: I have been jealous for **Jerusalem** and for **Zion** with great jealousy; I have been jealous for her with great wrath."

"Thus says the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "KΣ" (Kyrios).</note>: I will return to **Zion**, and I will dwell in the midst of **Jerusalem**. And **Jerusalem** shall be called a 'True City,' and the mountain of the **Lord Almighty** shall be called a 'Holy Mountain.'"

"Thus says the **Lord Almighty**: Old men and old women shall again sit in the streets of **Jerusalem**, each one holding his staff in his hand because of the greatness of their days <note>A poetic way of describing extreme old age.</note>. "Thus says the **Lord Almighty**: If it should be impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be impossible in my eyes?" says the **Lord Almighty**.

"Thus says the **Lord Almighty**: Behold, I am saving my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west. And I will bring them in, and I will dwell in the midst of **Jerusalem**. "Thus says the **Lord Almighty**: Let your hands be strong, you who hear these words in these days from the mouth of the prophets, from the day that the house of the **Lord Almighty** was founded and the temple was built. For before those days, the wages for <term>men</term> <note>original: "ΑΝΩΝ" (anthropon).</note> brought no profit, and there were no wages for the cattle; and there was no peace from affliction for him who went out or him who came in. "Instead, I will show peace: the vine shall give its fruit, and the earth shall give its produce, and the heaven shall give its dew; and I will cause the remnant of my people to inherit all these things."

**Thus says the Lord:** <note>original: "KS", an abbreviation for "Kyrios" (Lord).</note> Because you have made plans, but not through me, and covenants, but not through my **Spirit**, <note>original: "PNS", for "Pneumatos" (Spirit).</note> to add sin upon sins; you who set out to go down into **Egypt**, but you did not ask me—to be helped by **Pharaoh** and to be sheltered under the shelter of the **Egyptians**. Therefore, thus says the **Lord**, the **Holy One of Israel**: Because you have been disobedient to these words, and you have hoped in a lie, and because you have grumbled and have become confident in this word; therefore this sin shall be to you like a wall falling suddenly when a city has been captured, whose collapse is imminent. And its collapse shall be like the breaking of an earthen vessel, of a fine ceramic, so that one cannot find among them even a shard with which you might take fire, or in which you might scoop a little water.

Thus says the **Lord**, the **Holy One of Israel**: When you return and groan, then you shall be saved, and you shall know where you were when you trusted in vain things. Your strength became vain, and you were not willing to listen. But you said, "We will flee on horses!"—therefore you shall flee. And you said, "We will be on swift mounts!"—therefore those pursuing you shall be swift. A thousand shall flee at the voice of one, and at the voice of five, many shall flee, until you are left like a mast upon a mountain, and like a signal-flag upon a hill.

For a holy people shall dwell in **Zion**, and **Jerusalem** <note>original: "ILHM", for "Ierousalem".</note> has not wept with weeping. ### Isaiah Chapter 49

Behold, these come from afar; some from the north and some from the sea, and others from the land of the Persians. <note>original: "εγγη περσων" (en ge person). A 'Nomen Sacrum' or sacred abbreviation used by early Christian scribes for the word 'God'.</note> has had mercy on His people and has comforted the humble among His people.

But Zion said, "The Lord <note>original: "κσ" (kyrios). A 'Nomen Sacrum' for the word 'Lord'.</note> has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me." Can a woman forget her child, so as not to have mercy on the offspring of her womb? Even if a woman should forget these things, "yet I will not forget you," says the Lord.

Behold, I have painted <note>original: "εζωγραφηκα" (ezographēka). Lift up your eyes round about and see them all; behold, they have gathered and have come to you. "As I live," says the Lord, "you shall clothe yourself with them all as an ornament, and put them on like the jewelry of a bride."

For your desert places and your ruined and fallen places shall now be too narrow for those who dwell in them, and those who swallowed you up shall be far removed from you. For your sons whom you have lost shall say in your ears, "The place is too narrow for me; make a place for me that I may dwell in it."

And you shall say in your heart, "Who has fathered these for me? I was childless and a widow, but who has reared these for me? I was left alone; where were these for me?" 

Thus says the Lord: "Behold, I lift up my hand to the nations, and I will lift up my signal-flag to the islands; and they shall bring your sons in their bosom, and carry your daughters on their shoulders. And kings shall be your foster fathers,

<column-break/>

and their princesses your nurses. They shall bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet; and you shall know that I am the Lord, and you shall not be ashamed."

Shall anyone take spoils from a giant? And if one is taken captive unjustly, shall he be saved? Thus says the Lord: "If one should take a giant captive, he shall take spoils; and he who takes them from a strong man shall be saved. I will judge your cause, and I will rescue your sons. Those who afflict you shall eat their own flesh, and they shall drink their own blood like new wine; and all flesh shall know that I am the Lord who rescued you, and who lays hold of the strength of Jacob."

### Column 1

Therefore I will still plead my case against you, says the Lord <note>original: "κς" (ks), a shortened form of "Kyrios" (Lord)</note>, and with your children’s children I will plead. For pass over to the islands of the Kittim <note>The Kittim refers to the people of Cyprus and the western Mediterranean islands.</note> and see; send to Kedar <note>Kedar refers to the nomadic tribes of the Arabian desert.</note> and consider diligently, and see if such things have happened: if the nations will change their gods, and yet they are not gods. But my people have changed their glory for that from which they shall not profit.

The heaven was amazed at this and shuddered exceedingly, says the Lord. For my people have committed two evils: they have abandoned me, the fountain of living water, and they have dug for themselves broken cisterns that will not be able to hold water. Is Israel a slave or a house-born servant? Why has he become a prey? Lions roared against him and gave forth their voice; they have made his land a desert, and his cities have been torn down so that no one dwells in them. Even the sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes <note>Memphis and Tahpanhes were major Egyptian cities.</note> knew you and mocked you. Did you not do these things to yourself by abandoning me? says the Lord your God <note>original: "κς ο θς σου" (ks o ths sou), abbreviations for "Lord your God"</note>.

And now, what is it to you and the way to Egypt, to drink the water of Geon <note>original: "γηων" (Geon). In the Septuagint, Geon is often used to refer to the Nile River.</note>? And what is it to you and the way to the Assyrians, to drink the water of the rivers? Your apostasy shall discipline you, and your wickedness shall convict you. Know and see that it is a bitter thing for you to abandon me, says the Lord your God; and I have taken no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God. For from of old you have shattered your yoke and torn apart your bonds, and you said, "I will not serve." Instead, I will go upon every high hill and under every shady tree; there I will pour myself out in my fornication.

But I planted you as a fruitful vine, entirely true; how have you turned into bitterness, O strange vine? Though you wash yourself with nitre <note>original: "νιτρω" (nitro), a naturally occurring mineral soda used as a cleaning agent.</note> and multiply soap for yourself, you are still stained in your iniquities before me, says the Lord your God.

How will you say, "I have not been defiled," and "I have not gone after...

### Column 2

...the Baal"? See your ways in the burial ground and know what you have done. Her voice wailed in the evening; she widened her ways. Keep your foot from a rough road and your throat from thirst. But she said, "I will be strong," for she loved strangers and went after them.

Hear now, O women, the word of the Lord, and let your ears receive the words of his mouth; and teach your daughters a lament, and each woman teach her neighbor a dirge. from the streets. And the corpses of the humans <note>original: "ΑΝΩΝ" (ANON), shorthand for *anthropon*</note> shall be as an example upon the face of the field of your land, and like grass behind a reaper, and there shall be no one to gather them.

Do not fear them, for they cannot do evil, and there is no good in them.

->THE WORD THAT CAME FROM THE LORD<-
->TO JEREMIAH, SAYING:<-
**A**rise and go down to the house of the potter, and there you shall hear my words. And I went down to the house of the potter, and behold, he was working at the stones <note>original: "ΛΙΘΩΝ" (lithon), referring to the two horizontal stone discs of a potter’s wheel</note>. And the vessel which he was making in his hands fell; and he made it again into another vessel, as it seemed good in his sight to make it.

**A**nd the word of the Lord <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΥ" (KY), an abbreviation for Kyrios</note> came to me, saying: "Can I not do to you as this potter does, O house of Israel <term>Israel</term> <note>original: "ΙΗΛ" (IEL)</note>? And if that nation should turn from all their evils, I will repent of all the evils which I spoke of doing to them. And at length I will speak against a nation and against a kingdom, to build it up and to plant it. And if they do evil before me, so as not to hear my voice, then I will repent of the good things which I spoke of doing to them."

**A**nd now, speak to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem <term>Jerusalem</term> <note>original: "ΙΗΛΜ" (IELM)</note>: "Behold, I fashion evils against you and I devise a device against you. Let each one turn now from his evil way, and make your practices better."

**A**nd they said, "We will act like men <note>original: "ΑΝΔΡΙΟΥΜΕΘΑ" (andrioumetha), literally "we will behave like men," here implying a stubborn, defiant persistence in their own strength</note>, for we will go after our own perversions, and we will each do what is pleasing to our own evil hearts."

**T**herefore, thus says the Lord <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΣ" (KS)</note>: "Ask now among the nations, who has heard such horrible things as the Virgin of Israel has done so very

<column-break/>

exceedingly? Shall the snow of Lebanon fail from the crags of the rock? Shall water turned aside by a violent wind fail? For my people have forgotten me.

**T**hey have offered incense to vanity, and they shall be weak in their ways. And it came to pass, after Israel was taken captive and Jerusalem was laid waste, Jeremiah sat weeping and composed this lament over Jerusalem and said:

<gloss>1</gloss> <note>The Greek letter 'alpha' (α) serves as the numeral 1, marking the start of the first acrostic poem.</note>
How lonely sits the city that was full of people! She has become like a widow, she who was great among the nations; she who was a princess among the provinces has become a forced laborer.

Bitterly she weeps in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks. There is no one to comfort her among all who loved her. All her friends have dealt treacherously with her; they have become her enemies.

Judah has gone into exile because of her affliction and the greatness of her servitude. She dwells among the nations, but finds no rest. All who pursued her have overtaken her in the midst of her distress.

The roads to Zion mourn because no one comes to the festivals. All her gates are desolate. Her priests groan; her virgins are led away, and she herself is in bitterness.

Her oppressors have become the head, and her enemies prosper; for the Lord <note>original: "KC" (Kyrios)</note> has humbled her for the multitude of her impieties. Her infants have gone into captivity before the face of the oppressor.

And from the daughter of Zion all her splendor has departed. Her princes have become...

<term>Israel</term>: The people and the land of the covenant.

Her watchmen were shaken in the streets; they were defiled with blood, because they were not able to touch their garments <note>original: "ιματιων αυτων" (imatiōn autōn). The image is of people so blood-stained that even their own clothes are ritually unclean.</note>.

# Ezekiel 26–27

...her daughters who are in the field <note>This refers to the smaller satellite villages or suburbs on the mainland surrounding the island city of Tyre.</note> shall fall by the sword, and they shall know that I am the Lord. <note>original: "ΚΣ" — an abbreviation for Kyrios (Lord).</note>
Behold, I am bringing against you, O Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar king of kings of Babylon from the north. He is a king of kings with horses and chariots and a gathering of many nations. He shall slay your daughters in the field with the sword; and he shall set a watch against you and build a wall around you and cast up a rampart against you. He shall direct his siege engines <note>original: "ΒΕΛΟΣΤΑΣΕΙΣ" — specifically refers to stands for catapults or battering rams.</note> and his spears against you; he shall throw down your walls and your towers with his weapons. Because of the multitude of his horses, their dust shall cover you; from the sound of his horsemen and the wheels of his chariots, your walls shall be shaken when he enters your gates as one entering a city from an open field. With the hoofs of his horses they shall trample all your streets; he shall slay your people with the sword and bring the substance of your strength down to the ground. And he shall plunder your power and despoil your wealth; he shall throw down your walls and destroy your desirable houses. Your stones and your wood and your dust he shall cast into the midst of the sea. And he shall put an end to the noise of your musicians, and the sound of your harps <note>original: "ΨΑΛΤΗΡΙΩΝ" — psalteries or stringed instruments.</note> shall no longer be heard in you. # Ezekiel 27

Thus says the Lord God: <note>original: "ἀδωναι κ̅ς̅" — Adonai Kyrios, a Hebrew-Greek hybrid title for God often found in the Septuagint.</note> O Tyre, you have said, "I have clothed myself in my beauty." In the heart of the sea, in the waters, your sons have draped beauty upon you. Cedar from Lebanon was used to build you; the planks for your decks were made of cypress from Lebanon. They were taken to make your mast. They made your oars from the oak of Bashan; <note>original: "σελατίνους ἐκ τῆς Βασανίτιδος" — refers to the region east of the Sea of Galilee, famous for its sturdy trees.</note> they made your sacred shrines out of ivory and groves of wood from the islands of the Chettiein. <note>original: "Χεττιείν" — likely referring to Kittim, or Cyprus.</note> Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt became your couch, to provide you with glory. You were draped in blue and purple from the islands of Elishah, <note>original: "Ἐλεισαί" — likely the coastal regions of North Africa or Southern Europe.</note> and these became your coverings. Your leaders, the inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad, became your rowers. Your wise men, O Tyre, who were within you, these were your ship-pilots. The elders of Byblos <note>original: "Βιβλίων" — also known as Gebal, an ancient Phoenician port.</note> and her wise men were in you; they strengthened your counsel. And all the ships of the sea and their rowers came to you at the far west. Persians and Lydians and Libyans were in your army; your men of war hung shield and helmet within you, and they gave you your glory. The sons of the Arvadians and your own army were upon your walls all around, and guards were in your towers. They hung their quivers upon your harbors all around; these perfected your beauty. The Carthaginians <note>original: "Χαρχηδόνιοι" — the Greek term for the people of Carthage, a great Phoenician colony in North Africa.</note> were your merchants because of the abundance of your great strength; they traded silver, gold, copper, iron, tin, and lead for your merchandise.

<column-break/>

Greece and all the surrounding regions, they themselves were your traders. They traded in the souls of men <note>A somber reference to the slave trade.</note> and bronze vessels as your exchange. From the house of Togarmah <note>original: "Θεργαμὰ" — likely a region in eastern Asia Minor/Armenia.</note> they gave horses, horsemen, and mules for your market. The sons of Rhodes were your merchants; from the islands they increased your trade. You received tusks of ivory and ebony as your payment from those who brought them in. Men were your merchants because of the abundance of your mixed goods; they gave stacte <note>A fragrant perfume or resin.</note> and embroidery from Tarshish, and "mamoth" <note>original: "μαμὼθ" — a difficult term, possibly referring to precious silks or corals.</note> and coral for your market. Judah and the sons of Israel, these were your merchants in the sale of wheat, and myrrh, and cassia; they gave primary honey, oil, and resin into your mixed trade. Damascus was your merchant because of the abundance of all your power, trading wine from Helbon <note>original: "Χεκρὼν" — Helbon was famous for its viticulture.</note> and wool from Miletus. And they brought wine into your market from Uzal; <note>original: "Ἀσὴλ"</note> wrought iron and wheels <note>original: "τροχεια" — potentially gears or pulley systems.</note> and ginger are among your mixed goods. Dedan was your merchant with choice cattle for chariots. Arabia and all the princes of Kedar, these were your merchants who traded with you in lambs, rams, and goats, in which they did business with you. The merchants of Sheba and Raamah, these were your merchants; they traded for your goods with the finest spices, precious stones, and gold. Harran, and Cannae, and Aneis, these were your merchants—Asshur and Chilmad were your traders, bringing trade in blue cloth and purple, and choice treasures bound with ropes in chests of cypress wood.

<margin>13</margin> **A**nd there was a man living in Babylon, and his name was Joakim. **A**nd Joakim was very wealthy, and he had a garden <note>original: "ΠΑΡΑΔΙϹΟϹ" (paradeisos); here meaning a private walled garden or orchard, from which we get the word "paradise."</note> adjoining his house. And the Jews would gather at his home because he was the most honorable of them all.

And two elders from the people were appointed as judges in that year, concerning whom the Sovereign <note>The Lord.</note> had spoken, saying: "Wickedness came forth from Babylon, from elder-judges who seemed to govern the people." These men were constantly at Joakim’s house, and all those who had legal disputes came to them.

**A**nd they perverted their own minds and turned away their eyes so as not to look toward Heaven, nor to remember righteous judgments. And they watched greedily every day to see her.

And the king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet ring of his nobles, so that the matter concerning Daniel might not be changed. And the king went away to his house and slept without dinner, and no food was brought to him, and his sleep fled from him. <insert>And God closed the mouths of the lions, and they did not trouble Daniel.</insert> <note>This sentence appears earlier here than in some other versions of the Bible, emphasizing God's immediate protection.</note>

Then the king rose early at dawn and in haste went to the den of lions. And as he drew near to the den, he cried out with a loud voice: "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God whom you serve continually been able to save you from the mouth of the lions?" And Daniel said to the king: "O King, live forever! My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm me, because before Him <term>uprightness<note>original: "εὐθύτης" (euthytēs)—integrity or moral straightness.</note></term> was found in me; and before you, O King, I have done no wrong." 

Then the king was greatly pleased for him, and he ordered Daniel to be brought out of the den. And Daniel was brought up out of the den, and no <term>injury<note>original: "διαφθορά" (diaphthora)—destruction or physical harm.</note></term> was found in him, because he trusted in his God. And the king spoke, and they brought the men who had <term>accused<note>original: "διαβαλλόντας" (diaballontas)—those who slandered or brought malicious charges.</note></term> Daniel, and they were thrown into the den of lions—they, their children, and their wives. And they had not reached the floor of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones. 

Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, tribes, and languages who dwell in all the earth: "May peace be multiplied to you."

<meta>This page transitions from the final prophetic visions of the Book of Daniel into the narrative additions found in the Septuagint (Greek Old Testament). It contains the stories of "Bel and the Dragon," where Daniel exposes the fraud of the Babylonian priests and destroys a living dragon worshipped as a god, leading to his second ordeal in the lions' den.</meta>

# THE STORY OF BEL AND THE DRAGON #

### THE FRAUD OF THE PRIESTS OF BEL ###

"And seal it with your own ring; and if, when we come in the morning, you do not find everything eaten by Bel, we shall die—or else Daniel, who has lied against us." But they were dismissive <note>original: "ΚΑΤΕΦΡΟΝΟΥΝ" (katephronoun) — they looked down on the threat or felt overconfident.</note>, because they had made a hidden entrance under the table, and they always entered through it to consume the offerings. And it happened that after they went out, the King set out the food for Bel. But Daniel ordered his servants to bring ashes <note>original: "ΤΕΦΡΑΝ" (tephran) — wood ash, used here to reveal footprints.</note>, and they scattered them throughout the whole temple in the presence of the King alone. Then they went out, closed the door, and sealed it with the King's ring, and departed.

But the priests entered during the night according to their custom, with their wives and children, and they ate and drank everything. The King rose early in the morning, and Daniel was with him. The King said, "Are the seals intact, Daniel?" And he said, "They are intact, O King." And it happened that as soon as he opened the doors, the King looked at the table and shouted with a loud voice, "Great are you, O Bel, and there is no deceit in you—not even a little!"

But Daniel laughed and held the King back from entering inside, and said, "Look now at the floor, and perceive whose footprints these are." And the King said, "I see the footprints of men, women, and children!" Then the King was enraged and seized the priests, their wives, and their children; and they showed him the hidden doors through which they used to enter and consume the things on the table. So the King put them to death and delivered Bel into Daniel's power, and he destroyed the idol and its temple.

And there was a great dragon <note>original: "ΔΡΑΚΩΝ" (drakōn) — in this context, likely a large serpent or a mythical beast kept by the Babylonians.</note> in that place.

<column-break/>

### THE DESTRUCTION OF THE DRAGON ###

And the Babylonians worshipped it. And the King said to Daniel, "Will you also say that this one is made of bronze? Look, he lives and eats and drinks! You cannot say that he is not a living god; so worship him."

And Daniel said, "I will worship the Lord my God <note>The Nomina Sacra "ΚΥ ΤΩ ΘΩ" represent "Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ" (Kyriō tō Theō) — the Lord God.</note>, for he is the living God <note>The Nomen Sacrum "ΘC" represents "Θεός" (Theos) — God.</note>. But you, O King, give me permission, and I will kill the dragon without sword or staff." And the King said, "I give it to you."

So Daniel took pitch, fat, and hair, and boiled them together; he made cakes <note>original: "ΜΑΖΑC" (mazas) — barley-cakes or lumps of dough.</note> and threw them into the mouth of the dragon. After eating them, the dragon burst open <note>original: "ΔΙΕΡΡΑΓΗ" (dierragē) — literally "was torn asunder" or "exploded."</note>. And Daniel said, "Behold your objects of worship!"

When the Babylonians heard of it, they were greatly indignant and conspired against the King, saying, "The King has become a Jew! He has destroyed Bel, killed the dragon, and slaughtered the priests!" So they came to the King and said, "Hand Daniel over to us, or else we will kill you and your household!" And the King saw that they were pressuring him greatly, and being forced, he handed Daniel over to them.

### DANIEL IN THE LIONS' DEN ###

They threw him into the lions' den, and he was there for seven days. Now in the den there were seven lions, and they were given two human bodies and two sheep every day; but at that time, these were not given to them, so that they might devour Daniel.

Now the prophet Habakkuk <note>original: "ΑΜΒΑΚΟΥΜ" (Ambakoum) — the prophet Habakkuk is here introduced into the story via divine intervention.</note> was in Judea; he had boiled a stew <note>original: "ΕΨΕΜΑ" (epsema) — a cooked pottage or broth.</note> and crumbled bread into a bowl, and was going into the field to take it to the harvesters. But an angel of the Lord <note>The Nomen Sacrum "ΚΥ" represents "Κυρίου" (Kyriou) — of the Lord.</note> said to Habakkuk, "Take the meal that you have to Babylon, to Daniel!"

# The Book of Esther
## The Dream of Mordecai and the Royal Decree

In the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the Great <note>original: "Αρταξέρξου του Μεγάλου" (Artaxerxou tou Megalou) — While the Hebrew text names the king Ahasuerus (Xerxes I), the Greek translation identifies him as Artaxerxes.</note>, on the first day of the month of Nisan, Mordecai had a dream. He was the son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin. He was a Jewish man living in the city of Susa, a high-ranking official serving in the court of the king. He was among the captives whom Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, had taken into exile from Jerusalem with Jeconiah, the king of Judah.

And this was his dream: Behold, there were voices of noise and thunders, and an earthquake, and a great disturbance upon the earth. And behold, two great dragons came forward, both ready to wrestle. They let out a great cry, and at their cry, every nation prepared for war, to fight against the nation of the righteous.

And behold, it was a day of darkness and gloom, with affliction, necessity, and great disturbance upon the earth. The entire nation of the righteous was troubled, fearing the evils that would come upon them; they prepared to perish and cried out to God.

From their cry, there came as if from a small spring a great river with much water. Light and the sun rose up, and the humble were exalted and they consumed those who were held in glory.

When Mordecai, who had seen this dream and what God intended to do, awoke, he kept the dream in his heart and desired to understand it in every detail until nightfall. And Mordecai was resting in the court with Gabatha and Tharra, the two <term>eunuchs</term> <note>original: "ευνούχων" (eunouchon) — high-ranking palace officials, often in charge of security or the harem.</note> of the king who guarded the court. He heard their schemes and searched out their concerns, and he learned that they were preparing to lay hands upon King Artaxerxes.

<column-break/>

He then informed the king about them. And the king examined the two eunuchs, and when they confessed, they were led away to be executed. The king wrote these events in his records, and Mordecai also wrote concerning these matters. The king then commanded Mordecai to serve in the court and gave him gifts because of this.

But Haman, son of Hammedatha, the <term>Bougaean</term> <note>original: "Βουγαῖος" (Bougaios) — A title of uncertain meaning, possibly a Greek rendering of "Agagite" or a term meaning "bully."</note>, was in high honor before the king, and he sought to harm Mordecai and his people because of what happened to the two eunuchs of the king.

And it happened after these events, in the days of Artaxerxes—this is the Artaxerxes who ruled from India to Ethiopia over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces. In those days, when King Artaxerxes sat upon his throne in the city of Susa, in the third year of his reign, he held a banquet for his friends and the other nations, for the nobles of the Persians and Medes and the rulers of the <term>satraps</term> <note>original: "σατραπών" (satrapon) — provincial governors in the Persian Empire.</note>.

And after this, after he had shown them the wealth of his kingdom and the glory of the abundance of his wealth for one hundred and eighty days—when the days of the drinking feast were completed—the king held a banquet for the nations found in the city for six days in the courtyard of the king’s house.

It was decorated with fine linen and cotton hangings stretched with cords of linen and purple, upon columns of gold and silver, and upon columns of Parian marble. There were cups of gold and silver, and they displayed emeralds and pearls and stones from the island. 

There were various lamps and roses scattered all around. There were cups of gold and silver and a small vessel made of <term>carbuncle</term> <note>original: "άνθρακιον" (anthrakion) — a deep red gemstone, likely a garnet or ruby.</note> set out, worth thirty thousand talents. There was much sweet wine, the kind which the king himself drank. But the drinking was not done according to a set rule <note>original: "ου κατά προκείμενον" (ou kata prokeimenon) — meaning guests were not forced to drink at a specific pace, a departure from some royal customs.</note>.

### BY THE KING’S COMMAND
Many young women were gathered to the city of Susa under the care of Gai <note>original: "ΓΑΙ"—This is Hegai, the king’s eunuch in charge of the harem.</note>.

And he treated her and her attendants well in the women’s quarters.

And when the time came for a young woman to go in to the king, after she had completed the time of a young woman’s preparation—twelve months—for thus the days of treatment were completed: six months being anointed with oil of myrrh, and six months with spices and the purifications of the women.

And they pointed out to Haman that Mordecai was not obeying the king's words. For Mordecai had shown them that he was a Jew. And Haman perceived that Mordecai did not bow down to him.

### THE PLOT OF HAMAN AND THE ROYAL DECREE

And Haman was greatly enraged and plotted to destroy all the Jews <note>original: "ΙΟΥΔΑΙΟΥΣ"—The Greek term for the Jewish people.</note> who were under the kingdom of Artaxerxes. In the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes, he issued a decree <term>original: "ΨΗΦΙΣΜΑ"—A formal resolution or edict.</term> and cast lots for the day and the month, so as to destroy in a single day the race of Mordecai. And the lot fell on the fourteenth day of the month which is Adar <note>Adar is the twelfth month of the Jewish calendar, roughly corresponding to February/March.</note>.

And he spoke to King Artaxerxes, saying, “There is a certain nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom; but their laws are different from all other nations, and they disobey your laws, O King. It is not profitable for the king to tolerate them. If it seems good to the king, let him decree to destroy them, and I will pay into the king’s treasury <note>original: "ΓΑΖΟΦΥΛΑΚΙΟΝ"—The royal storehouse or treasury.</note> ten thousand talents of silver.”

And the king took off his ring and gave it into the hand of Haman, so that he might carry out what was written against the Jews. And the king said to Haman, “Keep the silver, and deal with the nation as you wish.”

And the king’s scribes were called in the first month, on the thirteenth day, and it was written as Haman commanded to the generals and the rulers throughout every province, from India to Ethiopia, one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, and to the rulers of the nations according to their own language, in the name of King Artaxerxes.

And letters were sent by messengers <note>original: "ΒΙΒΛΙΑΦΟΡΩΝ"—Literally "book-bearers" or couriers.</note> throughout the kingdom of Artaxerxes to destroy the race of the Jews in a single day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their possessions. And this is the copy of the letter:

“The Great King Artaxerxes to the rulers of the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia and to those who are subject to them, writes these things: Having become lord over many nations and having mastered the whole world, I have resolved—not being lifted up by the arrogance of power, but conducting myself with greater moderation and

<column-break/>

with gentleness—to settle the lives of my subjects so they are always untroubled, and to make the kingdom peaceful for all people, establishing the longed-for peace.

But when I asked my advisors how this end might be achieved, Haman—who excels among us in wisdom and has shown himself to have unwavering goodwill and steady faithfulness, and who is honored with the second place from the royal thrones—pointed out to us that among all the tribes throughout the world there is mixed a certain hostile people, whose laws are contrary to every nation and who continually disregard the decrees of kings, so that the government which is flawlessly directed by us cannot be established.

Having perceived, therefore, that this nation stands alone in total opposition to every human being, following a strange way of life with foreign laws, and being ill-disposed toward our affairs, performing the worst of evils so that the stability of the kingdom may not be attained;

We have therefore commanded that those indicated to you in the writings of Haman—who is set over our affairs and is our second father—are all to be destroyed, with their wives and children, rooted out by the swords of their enemies without any pity or mercy, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month of Adar of the present year; so that those who were hostile in the past and are so now, may in a single day go down violently into Hades <note>original: "ΑΔΗΝ"—The realm of the dead; the grave.</note>, providing for us for the time to come a stable and tranquil state of affairs. And a copy is to be given to everyone so that it may be known throughout the land and set before all the nations to be ready for this day.”

**Column 1**

Many of those who have been placed in authority and entrusted with the affairs of friends, by the persistent persuasion of those in power, have become partakers of troubles <note>original: "ΠΑΡΑΜΥΘΙΑ" - here suggesting a false comfort or complicity</note> and have surrounded the innocent with irremediable calamities. They deceive the sincere goodwill of their rulers with the lies of the truth <note>meaning they use distorted truths or outright lies to manipulate the sovereign</note>.

It is possible to see this not so much from ancient histories—which we have passed down to you—but by examining what is right at your feet: the unholy deeds accomplished by the empty pride <note>original: "ΓΚΟΝΑΣΙΑ" likely a corruption of *κενοδοξία* (vainglory)</note> of those who hold power with harshness. We must take care for the future so that the kingdom may be provided untroubled for all people, by making use of changes with gentleness, and always judging the matters that come before our eyes with a more reasonable disposition.

For Haman, the son of Hammedatha, a Macedonian <note>original: "ΜΑΚΕΔΩΝ" - The Greek version of Esther identifies Haman as a Macedonian to emphasize his role as a foreign spy or traitor to the Persians</note>—who is in truth an alien to Persian blood and far removed from our kindness—after being welcomed as a guest by us, shared in the benevolence that we have toward every nation to such an extent that he was proclaimed our "Father" and was bowed down to by everyone as the person second only to the royal throne.

But, not bearing his pride, he schemed to deprive us of our authority and our very life. By the convoluted deceptions of his methods, he sought the destruction of our savior and constant benefactor, Mordecai, and the blameless partner of our kingdom, Esther, together with their entire nation. For by these means, he thought to leave us isolated and to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians.

But we find that the Jews, who were delivered to annihilation by this thrice-accursed man <note>original: "ΤΡΙCΑΛΙΤΗΡΙΟΥ"</note>, are not evildoers, but live by the most righteous laws. They are sons of the Most High, Greatest, Living God, who has directed the kingdom for us and for our ancestors in the most excellent state.

For this is the day that God, who is powerful over all, has made for them a time of joy instead of the destruction of the chosen race. Therefore, you also, among your named festivals, celebrate it as a notable day with all feasting, so that both now and hereafter it may be a sign of safety for us and for those Persians who are well-disposed, but a memorial of destruction for those who plot against us.

Every city or country—without exception—which does not act according to these instructions shall be consumed with the spear and fire in our wrath. It shall be made inaccessible not only to men, but also to wild beasts and birds for all time.

And the Jews took it upon themselves, and upon their descendants, and upon all those who joined them, that they would not use these days in any other way, but as a memorial to be celebrated according to their generation, their family, their city, and their country. And these days of the *Phrourai* <note>Purim</note> shall be observed for all time, and the memory of them shall not fail from their generations.

And Queen Esther, daughter of Aminadab, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote all that he had done to confirm the letter concerning the *Phrourai*. And Mordecai and Esther the Queen established this for themselves, regarding their own safety and the plan concerning them. And Esther established it by a word forever, and it was written for a memorial.

<margin>the</margin> For King Artaxerxes <note>historical: Likely representing Xerxes I, though the Greek text uses Artaxerxes</note> imposed a tribute upon his kingdom, both on the mainland and the islands of the sea. As for his strength and his courageous deeds, and the wealth of his kingdom, they are written in the book of the kings of the Persians and Medes as a memorial. And Mordecai succeeded King Artaxerxes; he was great in the kingdom and honored by the Jews and well-loved, for he sought the welfare of his nation.

And Mordecai said: "These things have come from God. For I remember the dream that I saw concerning these matters; for not a word of them has failed. The small spring that became a river, and there was light and sun and much water—this river is Esther, whom the king married and made queen. And the two dragons...

<column-break/>

...are myself and Haman. And the nations are those that gathered together to destroy the name of the Jews. And my nation is Israel, those who cried out to God and were saved. And the Lord <note>original: "KC" – abbreviation for "Kyrios" (Lord)</note> saved His people, and the Lord delivered us from all these evils. And God <note>original: "ΘC" – abbreviation for "Theos" (God)</note> performed signs and great wonders, the likes of which have never happened among the nations. 

For this reason, He made two lots: one for the people of God and one for all the nations. And these lots came to the hour and the time and the day of judgment before God and among all the nations. And God remembered His people and vindicated His inheritance. And these days shall be observed by them in the month of Adar, on the fourteenth and fifteenth of the month, with an assembly and joy and gladness before God throughout all generations forever among His people Israel."

In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra <note>historical: Likely Ptolemy XII and Cleopatra V, roughly 77 BCE, though several royal pairs shared these names</note>, Dositheus, who said he was a priest and a Levite, and Ptolemy his son, brought in the preceding letter regarding the *Phrourai* <note>Purim</note>, which they said was authentic and had been translated by Lysimachus, the son of Ptolemy, who was in Jerusalem.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Book of Tobit, following the conclusion of the Book of Esther. Tobit is a work of Hellenistic Jewish literature, found in the Septuagint but not the Hebrew Bible, which tells the story of a righteous man from the tribe of Naphtali living in exile in Nineveh.</meta>

# THE BOOK OF THE WORDS OF TOBIT, SON OF TOBIEL
### SON OF ANANIEL, SON OF ADUEL, SON OF GABAEL, OF THE SEED OF ASIEL, OF THE TRIBE OF NAPHTALI

Who was taken captive in the days of Enemessaros <note>original: "ΕΝΕΜΕΣΣΑΡΟΥ" – this is the Greek form of the name Shalmaneser V, King of Assyria</note>, king of the Assyrians, from Thisbe, which is to the right of the city strictly called Kedesh of Naphtali in Upper Galilee, above Asher.

I, Tobit, walked in the ways of truth and righteousness all the days of my life, and I performed many acts of charity <note>original: "ΕΛΕΗΜΟΣΥΝΑΣ" (almsgiving/mercy)</note> for my brothers and my nation who went with me into the land of the Assyrians, to Nineveh. And when I was in my own country, in the land of Israel, while I was still young, the entire tribe of my father Naphtali departed from the house of Jerusalem—the city chosen from all the tribes of Israel for all the tribes to offer sacrifice. There, the Temple, the dwelling place of the Most High, had been sanctified and built for all generations forever.

Yet all the tribes that had revolted were sacrificing to the heifer, Baal <note>original: "ΤΗ ΒΑΑΛ ΤΗ ΔΑΜΑΛΕΙ" – referring to the golden calves set up by Jeroboam in the northern kingdom of Israel</note>. And I alone went often to Jerusalem for the festivals, as it is written for all Israel in an eternal decree. Having the firstfruits, the tithes of the produce, and the first shearings of the sheep, I would run to Jerusalem and give them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, for the altar. I gave a tenth of all the produce to the sons of Levi who ministered in Jerusalem. A second tenth I would convert into money and go and spend it in Jerusalem each year. And a third tenth I gave to those to whom it was fitting, just as Deborah, the mother of my father, had commanded me—for I had been left an orphan by my father. And when I became a man, I took Anna as a wife,

<column-break/>

from the seed of our own family, and by her I fathered a son, Tobias. And when I was taken captive to Nineveh, all my brothers and those of my race ate the bread of the Gentiles. But I kept my soul from eating it, because I remembered God with all my soul.

And the Most High gave me grace and favor in the sight of Enemessaros <note>Shalmaneser</note>, and I became his buyer of goods <note>likely a royal purchasing agent or steward</note>. I used to travel into Media, and I deposited with Gabael, the brother of Gabri, at Rages in Media, ten talents of silver.

But when Enemessaros died, his son Sennacherib reigned in his place, and the roads to Media became dangerous, so I could no longer travel there. In the days of Enemessaros, I performed many acts of charity for my brothers: I gave my bread to the hungry and my clothes to the naked; and if I saw any of my race dead and cast out behind the wall of Nineveh, I buried him.

And if Sennacherib killed anyone when he came fleeing from Judea, I buried them secretly—for in his anger he killed many. The bodies were sought by the king, but they were not found. But one of the people of Nineveh went and informed the king about me, that I was burying them, and so I hid myself. When I realized that I was being sought after to be put to death, I became afraid and fled. Then all my property was seized, and nothing was left to me except my wife Anna and my son Tobias.

But not fifty days passed before two of his sons killed him <note>Sennacherib</note>, and they fled into the mountains of Ararat. Then his son Esarhaddon <note>original: "ΣΑΧΕΡΔΟΝΟΣ"</note> reigned in his place. He appointed Achiacharus <note>original: "AXIAXΑΡΟΝ"</note>, the son of my brother Anael, over all the accounts of his kingdom, and he had authority over the entire administration.

# JUDITH

### THE BOOK OF TOBIT
<note>The following text concludes the Book of Tobit, chapter 14:5–15</note>

In it [Jerusalem] shall be built for all the generations of the age, a glorious building, just as the prophets spoke concerning it. And all the nations shall turn truly to fear the Lord God <note>original: "THN," a shortened form of "Theon" (God)</note>, and they shall bury their idols. And all the nations shall bless the Lord <note>original: "KN," a shortened form of "Kyrion" (Lord)</note>, and his people shall give thanks to God <note>original: "THO," a shortened form of "Theō"</note>. And the Lord <note>original: "KS," a shortened form of "Kyrios"</note> shall exalt his people; and all those who love the Lord God in truth and righteousness shall rejoice, showing mercy to our brothers.

And now, my child, depart from Nineveh, because everything the prophet Jonah spoke shall surely come to pass. But as for you, keep the law and the commandments, and be merciful and righteous, so that it may go well with you. And bury me properly, and your mother with me; and do not stay in Nineveh any longer. 

Child, see what Aman <note>In the Book of Tobit, Aman (or Nadin) is the villain who betrayed his uncle</note> did to Achiacharus <note>Tobit’s nephew, also known as Ahikar, a wise courtier</note> who raised him: how from the light he led him into darkness, and what things he repaid him. Yet Achiacharus was saved, while that man received his repayment and went down into the darkness. Manasses <note>The identity of this Manasses is debated; he is cited here as an example of one who escaped death through charity</note> practiced acts of mercy and was saved from the snare of death which they set for him; but Aman fell into the snare and perished. 

And now, children, see what mercy accomplishes, and how righteousness delivers. And as he was saying these things, his soul departed upon his bed. He was one hundred and fifty-eight years old, and they buried him gloriously. And when his mother died, he buried her near his father. 

But Tobias departed with his wife and his sons to Ecbatana, to Raguel his father-in-law. And he grew old with honor, and he buried his parents-in-law gloriously. He inherited their property and that of Tobit his father. He died at the age of one hundred and fifty-eight years <note>The manuscript repeats the age "one hundred fifty and eight" twice in this passage</note> in Ecbatana of Media. Before he died in Media, he heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which Nebuchadnezzar <note>original: "NABOUCHODONOSOR"</note> and Ahasuerus <note>original: "ASYĒROS"</note> had taken captive; and he rejoiced over Nineveh before he died.

### THE BOOK OF JUDITH
<note>This begins the Book of Judith, chapter 1:1–9</note>

In the twelfth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, who reigned over the Assyrians in Nineveh the great city, in the days of Arphaxad, who reigned over the Medes in Ecbatana: 

He [Arphaxad] built walls around Ecbatana of hewn stones three cubits <term>cubit: an ancient unit of length, roughly 18 inches</term> in breadth and six cubits in length. He made the height of the wall seventy cubits and its breadth fifty cubits. He set up its towers at its gates one hundred cubits high, and he laid its foundations sixty cubits wide. He made its gates as gates raised to a height of seventy cubits, and forty cubits wide, for the marching out of his mighty forces and the formations of his infantry.

And in those days, King Nebuchadnezzar made war against Arphaxad in the great plain; this is the plain on the borders of Ragau. And there met him all who inhabited the hill country, and all who inhabited the Euphrates, the Tigris, and the Hydaspes, and the plains of Arioch, king of the Elymaeans. And many nations gathered for the battle-line of the sons of Cheleud.

And Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, sent word to all who inhabited Persia, and to all who inhabited the west: those inhabiting Cilicia, Damascus, Lebanon, and Anti-Lebanon, and all who lived along the coast, and those among the nations of Carmel, Gilead, Upper Galilee, and the great plain of Esdraelon, and all who were in Samaria and its cities, and beyond the Jordan as far as Jerusalem, Chebas, Chalus, and the river of Egypt, and Tahpanhes.

# JUDITH

### THE DEFIANCE OF THE NATIONS
<note>This passage corresponds to Judith 1:9–2:6</note>

...and all the land of Goshen <note>A fertile region in Egypt where the Israelites historically resided</note> as far as the approach to Tanis and Memphis, and all who dwell in Egypt as far as the borders of Ethiopia. And all the inhabitants of the entire land despised the word of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians <note>While history remembers Nebuchadnezzar as a Babylonian king, this text identifies him with the Assyrian capital of Nineveh to emphasize his role as a legendary oppressor</note>. They did not join him in the war, for they were not afraid of him; instead, he seemed to them like but a single man. They sent his messengers back empty-handed and in disgrace. 

Then Nebuchadnezzar was greatly enraged against this entire land. He swore by his throne and his kingdom that he would surely take vengeance on all the territories of Cilicia, Damascus, and Syria, and that he would slaughter with his sword all the inhabitants of the land of Moab, the people of Ammon, all of Judea, and everyone in Egypt as far as the borders of the two seas <note>likely referring to the Mediterranean and the Red Sea</note>.

In the seventeenth year of his reign, he marched his forces against King Arphaxad <note>Identified as the ruler of the Medes</note>. He prevailed in his battle against Arphaxad and overthrew his entire army, all his cavalry, and all his chariots. He took lordship over his cities and reached as far as Ecbatana <note>The capital city of the Medes</note>; he captured its towers, plundered its streets, and turned its former beauty into a cause for shame. He captured Arphaxad in the mountains of Ragau <note>likely the ancient city of Rhagae</note>, struck him down with his javelins, and destroyed him utterly to this day. Then he returned with his spoils—he and his entire mixed multitude of warriors, a very great number—and there he remained, idling and feasting, he and his army, for one hundred and twenty days.

And in the eighteenth year, on the twenty-first day of the first month, a word went forth in the house of Nebuchadnezzar

<column-break/>

king of the Assyrians, that he should take vengeance on all the earth, just as he had spoken. He called together all his servants and all his nobles and laid before them the secret of his counsel; with his own mouth, he determined the full extent of the evil to befall the land. They judged it necessary to destroy all flesh—those who had not obeyed the word of his mouth. 

When he had finished his counsel, Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, called Holofernes, the chief general of his forces, who was second only to himself, and said to him: "Thus says the Great King, the Lord <note>original: "KS," an abbreviation for "Kyrios" (Lord). Here, Nebuchadnezzar claims the divine title for himself</note> of all the earth:

> Behold, you shall go forth from my presence and take with you men who trust in their own strength: one hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers and a multitude of horses with twelve thousand riders. You shall go out against the entire land to the west, because they disobeyed the word of my mouth. You shall command them to prepare 'earth and water' <note>A traditional ancient Near Eastern demand for total surrender, representing the yielding of all resources</note>, for I will go forth in my wrath against them. I will cover the whole face of the earth with the feet of my army, and I will give them over to be plundered. Their wounded shall fill their valleys, and every torrent and river shall be filled to overflowing with their corpses. I will lead them into captivity to the ends of the earth. 

> But you, go out and seize all their borders for me. They shall surrender themselves to you, and you shall keep them for me until the day of their punishment. As for those who remain disobedient, your eye shall not spare them; you shall give them over to slaughter and plunder throughout your entire land. For as I live, and by the power of my kingdom, I have spoken, and I will do these things by my own hand. You shall not transgress even one of the words of your Lord <note>original: "KY," an abbreviation for "Kyriou" (Lord)</note>; rather, you shall strictly carry out everything as I have commanded you. Do not delay in doing these things."

And Holofernes went out from the presence of his lord and called together all the satraps <note>Provincial governors</note>, the generals, and the officers of the Assyrian army, and he numbered...

It introduces the villain Holofernes and establishes Nebuchadnezzar’s claim to divine status as the "Lord of all the earth."</summary>

### THE MOBILIZATION OF HOLOFERNES

His council was completed just as his lord had commanded him. Holofernes <note>The commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army, acting as the king's right hand</note> went out from the presence of his lord and called together all the rulers, the generals, and the officers of the Assyrian <note>original: ΑΣΣΟΥΡ (Assur)</note> military force. He numbered chosen men for the battle line, just as his lord had commanded him, totaling one hundred and twenty thousand infantry and twelve thousand horsemen archers. He organized them in the manner that a vast multitude is prepared for war. He took camels, donkeys, and mules for their baggage—a very great number—and sheep, oxen, and goats without number for their provisions. He also took a great deal of rations for every man, and a very large amount of gold and silver from the royal house.

Then he and his entire force set out on the same road King Nebuchadnezzar had traveled before, to cover the whole face of the earth toward the west with his chariots, his cavalry, and his chosen infantry. A mixed multitude went with them, as numerous as locusts <note>A common ancient metaphor for an army so large it consumes everything in its path</note> or the sand of the earth; their number could not be counted because of their vastness. 

They departed from Nineveh <note>The capital of the Assyrian Empire</note> and traveled for three days to the plain of Bektileth <note>An unidentified location, possibly near the Taurus Mountains</note>. He camped near Bektileth, close to the mountain that is to the left of Upper Cilicia <note>A region in what is now southern Turkey</note>. Taking his entire force—his infantry, cavalry, and baggage train—he departed from there into the hill country. He cut through Phut and Lud <note>Likely referring to groups from Libya and Lydia or similar western territories</note> and plundered all the sons of Rassis and the sons of Ishmael who lived facing the desert to the south of Chelleon. He crossed the Euphrates, passed through Mesopotamia, and demolished all the fortified cities situated along the brook of Abrona, until he reached the sea. He then occupied the borders of Cilicia and 

<column-break/>

cut down all who resisted him. He came to the borders of Japheth <note>Referencing a northern territory</note> toward the south, facing Arabia. He encircled all the Midianites <note>original: ΜΑΔΙΑΜ</note>, burned their tents, and plundered their sheepfolds. He descended into the plain of Damascus during the days of the wheat harvest <note>A strategic time for conquest, as it allowed the army to seize or destroy the year's food supply</note> and burned all their fields; he destroyed their flocks and herds, leveled their cities to the ground, scattered their children, and struck down all their young men with the edge of the sword.

Fear and trembling fell upon all the inhabitants of the coast: those in Sidon and Tyre, those living in Sur and Okina, and everyone dwelling in Jamnia. The inhabitants of Azotus <note>Modern Ashdod</note> and Ashkelon were also terrified of him.

<margin>3.</margin> So they sent messengers to him with peaceful words, saying: "Behold, we, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar the Great King, lie prostrate before you. Use us however it is pleasing to you. Behold, our farmsteads, our entire territory, our wheat fields, our flocks, our herds, and all the folds of our tents lie before you; use them as you wish. Behold, even our cities and those who dwell in them are your slaves. Come and meet us as it seems good in your eyes." 

The men came to Holofernes and reported these words to him. Then he went down to the coast with his army and stationed garrisons in the high cities. He took chosen men from them to serve as allies. They and all the surrounding countryside received him with crowns, dances, and drums. Yet, he demolished all their borders <note>Likely referring to their territorial markers or local shrines</note> and cut down their sacred groves <note>original: ΑΛΣΗ (alsē); these were groves dedicated to local gods, which the Assyrians destroyed to enforce religious conformity</note>. For he had been commanded to destroy all the gods of the land, so that everyone should worship Nebuchadnezzar alone...

<summary>Holofernes mobilizes a massive Assyrian army and begins a scorched-earth campaign across Mesopotamia and Syria, prompting the coastal cities to surrender in terror. The conquest is not only military but religious, as Holofernes begins destroying local shrines to establish Nebuchadnezzar as a god.</summary>
