--- Page 1072 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion of the spiritual utility of the Psalms. While the previous page focused on the harmony of the soul through musical rhythm, this page moves toward the practical application of the Psalms as a mirror for every human emotion and situation, followed by an exhortation on the power of faith using examples from the Epistle to the Hebrews.</meta>

Therefore, let us remind ourselves that from these—as if from the fruits of a **paradise** of benefit for our needs—we may grasp the words that describe the cycle of all human life. In these words, you are able to observe the dispositions of the soul and the movements of our thoughts, and to keep and contain them, so that you do not pray for anything more than these.

For whether there is a need for **repentance** or **confession**, or if **affliction** and **temptation** have overtaken someone, or if one is being persecuted, or if plots have been thrown against one by the "wise," <note>original: "σοφῶν" (sophōn); likely referring to those who use worldly cleverness or rhetoric against the faithful</note> or if one has become sorrowful, or is troubled, or suffers anything like those things mentioned before; or if one sees our prosperity progressing through affliction while the enemy is brought to naught; or if one wishes to praise, give thanks, and bless the **Lord**—he has the teaching of all these things in the **Divine Psalms**.

For let him choose what is said in them concerning each of these situations, and let him recite them as if they were written concerning himself. By identifying with what is written, he offers them up to the **Lord**. Let him not, however, clothe them with the persuasive words of outsiders <note>original: "τοῖς ἔξωθεν πιθανοῖς ῥήμασιν" (tois exōthen pithanois rēmasin); referring to the use of secular, pagan, or sophisticated rhetorical styles</note> in an attempt to be impressive, nor should he try to alter the words or change them at all. Instead, let him speak and sing the things written simply <note>original: "ἀτέχνως" (atechnōs); without artificial craft or worldly artifice</note> and as they are.

This is done so that the holy men who originally ministered these words, recognizing them as their own, might pray along with us. More importantly, it is so that the **Spirit** <term>original: "ΠΝΑ" (Pneuma); the Holy Spirit</term> who spoke in the saints—seeing his own words placed in us which he once gave to them—might assist us. For just as the life of the saints is better than that of others, so too are the words spoken by them better and more powerful than those composed by us, and they are rightly considered more effective.

For in these words they were well-pleasing to **God**, and by speaking these things, as the **Apostle** <note>The author is quoting the Apostle Paul from the Epistle to the Hebrews</note> said: they conquered kingdoms, performed righteousness, and obtained promises.

<column-break/>

They stopped the mouths of lions, quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, and turned to flight the armies of foreigners. Women received their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, not accepting deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection. Others had trial of mockings and scourgings, and even of chains and imprisonment. They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were tempted, and they were slain with the sword. They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, tormented—of whom the world was not worthy. They wandered in deserts and mountains, in dens and caves of the earth.

And all these, having obtained a good testimony through faith, did not receive the promise, for **God** provided something better for us, so that they should not be made perfect without us. <note>This entire paragraph is a direct quotation of Hebrews 11:33-40</note>

For he who decreed through **Moses**... this inscription of John <unclear>and</unclear> to succeed the people and the one appointed as ruler... commanding him to have this **Deuteronomy** <note>original: "Δευτερονόμιον" (Deuteronomion), meaning the "Second Law" or the book of the Bible</note> in his hands... and always to benefit from the commandments in it... looking at the things written in it... <unclear>meditate</unclear> <unclear>upon</unclear> <unclear>the</unclear> <unclear>city</unclear> <unclear>at</unclear> each <unclear>gate</unclear> <unclear>unbound</unclear> <unclear>there</unclear> seeing <unclear>these</unclear> <unclear>separated</unclear> to you <unclear>from</unclear> <unclear>ceasing</unclear> <unclear>throughout</unclear> <unclear>life</unclear> <unclear>of the</unclear>... all those of the wicked... into war... the man himself... and as the voice of **Deuteronomy**... the divine ears of all...

<summary>Athanasius explains that the Psalms serve as a universal mirror for the human soul and should be recited without rhetorical flourishes to maintain their spiritual power. The text then cites the great trials of the biblical heroes of faith from the Book of Hebrews to illustrate the strength gained through such devotion.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spiritual efficacy of the Psalms. Following the previous page’s discussion on using the exact words of Scripture rather than human rhetoric, Athanasius now provides historical and biblical examples—ranging from King Josiah to the apostles—to demonstrate that the words of the Spirit possess an inherent power to repel evil and heal the soul, provided the speaker has sincere faith.</meta>

Column 1

...recalling the **rewards of the Law**—and being further armed with this knowledge—he prevailed over his enemies. And King **Josiah**, when the Book was found and read in the hearing of all, no longer feared his enemies. And if ever the **Ark** containing the tablets of the Law went before them in battle, it was sufficient as a help against all opposing ranks—unless there was some prevailing **sin** or **hypocrisy** among those carrying it. For there is a need for **faith** and a **sincere disposition**, so that the Law may work together with our prayers.

"Therefore," the old man used to say, "I have also heard from wise men that in ancient times, among the Israelites, they used to drive away demons simply by **reading the Scriptures**. For the demons would shrink back from them, being unable to withstand the help given to those who resisted them. And concerning all knowledge, he said it is right for those who desire to be sanctified to set these words aside for themselves. But those who compose **persuasive words** <note>original: "πιθανά ῥήματα" (pithana rēmata); likely referring to worldly or sophisticated rhetoric used in place of scriptural language</note> for themselves from the outside, and use these to adjure demons, are naming themselves rather than the Lord—for they are essentially playing. They offer themselves up to be mocked by the demons, just as the Jewish **sons of Sceva** <note>referring to the account in Acts 19:13-16 where the sons of a Jewish chief priest tried to cast out demons using the name of Jesus without having faith</note> suffered when they attempted to adjure in this manner.

For the demons, hearing such things from people like that, treat them as a joke. But they fear the **words of the Saints** and cannot endure them. For the **Lord** <term>KC</term> <note>original: "Κύριος" (Kyrios); abbreviated in the text as a Nomina Sacra</note> is present within the words of the Scriptures. The demons, unable to bear Him, used to cry out: 'I beg you, do not torment us before the time!' For they were being burned, simply by seeing the **Lord** <term>KN</term> <note>original: "Κύριον" (Kyrion)</note> present. Just as **Paul** commanded the unclean spirits, so too were the demons subject to the **disciples**."

<column-break/>

And in the time of **Elisha** the prophet, the hand of the **Lord** <term>KY</term> <note>original: "Κυρίου" (Kyriou)</note> came upon him, and he prophesied concerning the waters to the three kings when the minstrel played according to his command. So now, if anyone cares for those who are suffering, let him speak these words, and it will rather benefit the one suffering, and he will prove his own faith to be certain and firm. Thus, seeing this faith, **God** <term>ΘΝ</term> <note>original: "Θεόν" (Theon)</note> may provide complete healing to those who are deemed worthy. For the Saint, knowing this, said in the **118th Psalm** <note>Psalm 119 in modern English Bibles, known for its focus on the Law</note>:
<margin>></margin> "I will meditate on your **statutes**;
<margin>></margin> I will not forget your words."
<margin>></margin> And again:
<margin>></margin> "Your statutes were songs to me
<margin>></margin> in the place of my pilgrimage."

<margin>></margin> For in these they gained salvation,
<margin>></margin> saying: "Unless your **Law**
<margin>></margin> had been my meditation,
<margin>></margin> then I would have perished
<margin>></margin> in my humiliation."

Therefore, **Paul** also secured his own disciple in these things,
<margin>></margin> saying: "Meditate on these things;
<margin>></margin> be occupied in them, so that your
progress may be manifest to all." By meditating on these and encountering the **Psalms** with such understanding, you will be able to grasp the meaning in each one, being guided by the **Spirit** <term>ΠΝC</term> <note>original: "Πνεύματος" (Pneumatos)</note>. And you yourself will strive for such a life as the holy, God-inspired men possessed who spoke these things.

**B**lessed is the man who has not
walked in the counsel of the ungodly,
and in the way of sinners
has not stood,
and in the seat of the pestilent <note>original: "λοιμων" (loimōn); often translated as "scornful" or "mockers," though the Greek literally suggests something infectious or plague-like.</note>
has not sat.
But rather, in the law of the Lord <note term="Nomina Sacra">The scribe uses "κ̅υ̅," a shortened form of the word for "Lord" (Kyrios) marked with a line to indicate its sacred status.</note> is
his will, and in
His law he shall meditate
day and night.
And he shall be like the tree
planted beside the outflows
of the waters,
which shall give its fruit in
its season,
and its leaf shall not
fall away;
and all things whatsoever he does
shall be prospered.
Not so the ungodly, not so;
but rather like the dust which 
the wind tosses from the face of the earth.
Because of this, the ungodly shall not stand
in the judgment,
nor sinners in the counsel 
of the righteous.
For the Lord knows the way of the righteous,
and the way of the ungodly shall perish.

### FOR THE END: A PSALM OF DAVID

<margin>36</margin> Do not be provoked by evildoers,
Nor be envious of those who practice lawlessness.
For like grass they shall quickly wither,
And like green herbs they shall quickly fall away.
Hope in the Lord <note>original: 'KN', an abbreviation for 'Kyrie'</note> and do good;
Dwell in the land and you shall be fed by its wealth.
Delight in the Lord, and He will give you the requests of your heart.
Reveal your way to the Lord;
Hope in Him, and He will act.
He will bring forth your righteousness like light,
And your judgment like the noonday.
Be subject to the Lord and plead with Him;
Do not be provoked by the one who prospers in his way,
By the man who practices lawlessness.
Cease from anger and abandon wrath;
Do not be provoked so as to do evil.
For those who do evil shall be destroyed,
But those who wait upon the Lord, they shall inherit the land.
For yet a little while and the sinner shall be no more;
And you shall seek his place and you shall not find it.

<column-break/>

But the meek shall inherit the land,
And they shall delight in the abundance of peace.
The sinner watches the righteous
And gnashes his teeth against him.
But the Lord <note>original: 'KS', an abbreviation for 'Kyrios'</note> shall laugh at him,
For He foresees that his day is coming.
The sinners have drawn the sword;
They have bent their bow
To cast down the poor and needy,
To slaughter the upright in heart.
Let their sword enter into their own heart,
And let their bows be shattered.
A little is better for the righteous
Than the great wealth of sinners.
For the arms of sinners shall be shattered,
But the Lord supports the righteous.
The Lord knows the ways of the blameless,
And their inheritance shall be forever.
They shall not be put to shame in an evil time,
And in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.
For the sinners shall perish;
And the enemies of the Lord, as soon as they are glorified and exalted,
Vanishing like smoke, they have vanished away.
The sinner borrows and will not repay,
But the righteous man is compassionate and gives.
For those who bless Him shall inherit the land,
But those who curse Him shall be destroyed.
A man's steps are directed by the Lord,
And He shall greatly desire his way.
When he falls, he shall not be dashed down,
For the Lord supports his hand.
I have been young and indeed have grown old,
And I have not seen the righteous forsaken,
Nor his offspring seeking <unclear>bread</unclear>.

It emphasizes patience, the temporary nature of evil prosperity, and God's constant support for the blameless.</summary>

->FOR THE END, FOR THE SONS OF KORAH; FOR UNDERSTANDING<-

O God <note>original: 'ΘΣ', shorthand for 'Theos'</note>, we have heard with our ears; our fathers told us of the work which You performed in their days, in the ancient days. Your hand destroyed nations, and You planted them instead; You afflicted peoples and cast them out. For it was not by their own sword that they inherited the land, and their own arm did not save them. But it was Your right hand, and Your arm, and the light of Your countenance, because You were well-pleased with them. 

You Yourself are my King and my God <note>original: 'ΘΣ'</note>, He who commands the salvation of Jacob. Through You we will push down <note>original: 'keratioumen', literally "to gore with a horn," imagery describing a bull defeating its enemies</note> our enemies, and in Your name we will despise those who rise up against us. For I will not hope in my bow, and my sword shall not save me. For You saved us from those who afflict us, and You put to shame those who hate us. In God <note>original: 'ΘΩ', shorthand for 'Theo'</note> we shall be praised all day long, and in Your name we will give thanks forever.

But now You have cast us off and put us to shame, and You, O God <note>original: 'ΘΣ'</note>, do not go forth with our armies. You turned us backward from our enemies, and those who hate us plundered for themselves. You gave us up like sheep for food, and You scattered us among the nations. You sold Your people without price, and there was no profit <note>original: 'alalagmasin', literally referring to the shouting or noise made during a transaction or battle</note> in the sale of them. You made us a reproach to our neighbors,

<column-break/>

a mockery and a derision to those round about us. You made us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples. All day long my disgrace is before me, and the shame of my face has covered me, from the voice of the one reproaching and speaking against me, and from the face of the enemy and the persecutor. 

All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten You, and we have not dealt falsely in Your covenant. Our heart has not turned back, and You have turned our paths away from Your way. For You humbled us in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death covered us. 

If we have forgotten the name of our God <note>original: 'ΘΥ', shorthand for 'Theou'</note>, and if we stretched out our hands to a foreign god <note>original: 'ΘΝ', shorthand for 'Theon'</note>, shall not God <note>original: 'ΘΣ'</note> search these things out? For He knows the secrets of the heart. For for Your sake we are put to death all day long; we were counted as sheep for slaughter.

For our soul has been humbled to the dust; our belly has cleaved to the earth. Arise, Lord <note>original: 'ΚΕ'</note>, and help us, and redeem us for the sake of Your name.

### PRAYER OF MOSES, THE MAN
### OF GOD

<margin>Psalm 89</margin>
<margin>Tone 4</margin>
Lord, you have been our refuge
from generation to generation.
Before the mountains were born, and the earth 
and the world were formed,
even from age to age, you 
are God. <note>original: "θς" (Theos).</note>
Do not turn man away to humiliation;
for you said, "Return, you sons 
of men."
For a thousand years in your eyes, Lord,
are as yesterday which has passed,
and like a watch in the night. 
Their years shall be 
regarded as nothing;
in the morning, let it pass away like grass.

<column-break/>

In the morning, let it bloom and pass away;
in the evening, let it fall, and wither, 
and dry up.
For we have perished in your anger,
and in your wrath we have been troubled.
You have set our iniquities before you;
our span of life in the light 
of your face.
For all our days have failed,
and in your wrath we have fainted;
our years were spent as a spider's web. <note>A poetic Septuagint variant emphasizing the fragility and intricacy of a short life.</note>
The days of our years in themselves 
are seventy years;
but if in strength, 
eighty years;
and the greater part of them is labor and pain.
For a gentleness has come upon us,
and we shall be disciplined.
Who knows the power of your anger?
And can one number your wrath 
from the fear of you?
So make known to me your right hand,
and those whose hearts are 
instructed in wisdom.
Return, O Lord! How long?
And be comforted concerning your servants.
We were filled in the morning with your mercy,
and we exulted and were glad 
in all our days.
We were gladdened in return for the days 
you humbled us,
for the years in which we saw evils.
And look upon your servants,
and upon your works,
and guide their sons.
And let the brightness of the Lord our God 
be upon us;
and the works of our hands,
direct them for us;
yes, the work of our hands,
direct it.

->and under his wings you shall hope;<-

### A PRAISE-SONG TO DAVID FOR THE DAY OF THE SABBATH

It is good to give thanks to the Lord
and to sing psalms to your name, O Most High;
to proclaim your mercy in the morning
and your truth by night,
on a ten-stringed psaltery <note>A stringed instrument similar to a harp.</note> with a song upon the lyre.
For you, Lord, have made me glad by your work,
and in the works of your hands I will exult.

<column-break/>

How your works were magnified, O Lord;
your thoughts were made very deep.
A foolish man shall not know,
and an uncomprehending man shall not understand these things.
When the sinners spring up like grass,
and all who work iniquity look forth—
it is so that they might be destroyed forever and ever.
But you, Lord, are the Most High forever.
For behold, your enemies, Lord, shall perish,
and all who work iniquity shall be scattered.
And my horn <note>A metaphor for strength or royal authority.</note> shall be exalted like that of a unicorn, <note>original: "μονοκέρωτος" (monokerotos). In the Septuagint, this refers to a powerful one-horned animal, often interpreted as a wild ox or rhinoceros.</note>
and my old age shall be anointed with rich oil.
And my eye has looked upon my enemies,
and my ear shall hear of the wicked ones rising up against me.
The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree;
he shall be multiplied like a cedar in Lebanon.
Those who are planted in the house of the Lord
shall flourish in the courts of our God.
They shall still be multiplied in a rich old age,
and they shall be prospering,
to proclaim that the Lord our God is upright,
and there is no unrighteousness in him.

---

the rivers have lifted up their voices;

**He spread a cloud** for a covering for them, and **fire** to give them **light** by night.
They asked, and the **quail** came, and He filled them with the **bread of heaven** <note>original: "ΑΡΤΟΝ ΟΥΡΑΝΟΥ" — referring to the Manna provided in the desert.</note>.
He **split the rock**, and waters flowed; they went through the **waterless places** as rivers.
For He **remembered His holy word**, given to **Abraham His servant**.
And He **brought out His people** with **rejoicing**, and His **chosen ones** with gladness.
And He **gave them the lands** of the nations, and they **inherited the labors** of the peoples,
so that they might **keep His statutes** and seek out **His law**.
**HALLELUJAH** <note>original: "ΑΛΛΗΛΟΥΪΑ" — a transliteration of the Hebrew 'Praise the Lord'.</note>

<margin>Psalm 105</margin> **Give thanks to the Lord**, for He is good; for His **mercy** endures **forever**.
Who will speak of the **mighty acts** of the **Lord**? Who will make all **His praises** heard?
**Blessed** are those who **keep judgment** and do **righteousness** at all times.
**Remember us, O Lord**, in the favor You show Your people; **visit us** with Your **salvation**,
to see the **goodness** of Your **chosen ones**, to be glad in the **gladness** of Your nation, to be **praised** <note>original: "ΕΠΑΙΝΕΙCΘΑΙ" — to glory or boast with pride in God.</note> with Your **inheritance**.
**We have sinned** with our fathers; we have **acted lawlessly**, we have done **injustice**.
Our **fathers in Egypt** did not understand **Your wonders**; they did not **remember the multitude** of Your **mercy**.
And they **rebelled** as they went up by the **Red Sea**.
And **He saved them** for the sake of **His name**.

<column-break/>

To **make known His power**, and He **rebuked the Red Sea**, and it was **dried up**;
and He **led them through the deep** as if through a **wilderness**.
And He **saved them** from the hand of **those who hated them**, and **redeemed them** from the hand of the **enemy**.
The **water covered** those who afflicted them; **not one** of them was left.
And they **believed in His words**, and they **sang His praise**.
They **made haste**, they **forgot His works**; they did not wait for **His counsel**.
And they **lusted** with a **great longing** in the wilderness, and they **tested God** in the waterless land.
And He **gave them their request**; He sent **fullness** <note>original: "ΠΛΗCΜΟΝΗΝ" — satiety or a 'wasting disease' in some translations, but here suggesting a physical filling that led to spiritual sickness.</note> into their **souls**.
And they **provoked Moses** in the camp, and **Aaron**, the **holy one** of the Lord.
The **earth opened** and **swallowed Dathan**, and covered over the **assembly of Abiram** <note>referring to the rebellion against Moses's leadership described in the Book of Numbers.</note>.
And a **fire was kindled** in their assembly; a **flame consumed** the sinners.
And they **made a calf in Horeb** <note>Horeb is the alternative name for Mount Sinai.</note> and **worshiped the carved image**.
And they **exchanged His glory** for the likeness of a **calf that eats grass**.
They **forgot the God who saved them**, who did **great things** in Egypt,
**wonders** in the **land of Ham** <note>The "Land of Ham" is a biblical poetic name for Egypt.</note>, **fearful things** by the **Red Sea**.
And He said He would **destroy them**, had not **Moses His chosen one** stood in the **breach** before Him, to **turn away His wrath**, so He would not destroy them.
And they **despised the desirable land**; they did **not believe His word**, and they **grumbled** in their **tents**.

<meta>This page marks the transition to a new section of the psalter. It contains the entirety of Psalm 107 and the first half of Psalm 108 (following the Septuagint numbering). The text continues the themes of divine sovereignty and the plea for justice against enemies. The handwriting is in the formal uncial style, indicating its use in a significant church codex.</meta>

<margin>Psalm 107:6</margin>

# A PSALM OF DAVID

My heart is ready, O <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΣ", a shortened sacred form of "Theos".</note>,
My heart is ready.
I will sing and play my music in my glory.
Awake, harp and lyre!
I will awake at dawn.
I will give thanks to You among the peoples, O <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΕ", a sacred shortening of "Kyrie".</note>;
And I will sing to You among the nations;
For Your mercy is great, high above the heavens,
And Your truth reaches to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, O <term>God</term>,
And Your glory over all the earth.
That Your beloved ones may be delivered,
Save with Your right hand and answer me.
<term>God</term> has spoken in His holy place:
"I will be exalted and I will divide Shechem,
And the Valley of Succoth <note>original: "ΣΚΗΝΩΝ", literally meaning "tents" or "booths," referring to the region of Succoth.</note>
I will measure out.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine,
And Ephraim is the protection of
my head;
Judah is my king.
Moab is the washpot of my hope;
Over Edom I will stretch out
my shoe;
The Philistines <note>original: "ΑΛΛΟΦΥΛΟΙ", meaning "foreigners," the standard term for Philistines in the Greek Old Testament.</note> have been subjected to me."
Who will lead me into a fortified city?
Or who will guide me as far as
Edom?
Is it not You, O <term>God</term>, who rejected us?
And will You not go out, O <term>God</term>, with
our armies?
Give us help from our affliction,
For the salvation of <term>men</term> <note>original: "ΑΝΩΝ", a sacred shortening of "anthropon".</note> is vain.
In <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΩ", sacred form of "Theos".</note> we shall do valiantly,
And He will bring to nothing those
who afflict us.

# TO THE END, A PSALM OF DAVID

O <term>God</term>, do not pass over my praise
in silence;
For the mouth of the sinner and the mouth
of the deceitful man have opened against me.
They have spoken against me with a deceitful tongue,
And they surrounded me with words of hatred,
And they fought against me without cause.
In return for my love, they slandered me,
But I continued to pray.
And they repaid me with evil
for good,
And hatred in return for my love.

<column-break/>

Appoint a sinner over him,
And let an accuser <note>original: "ΔΙΑΒΟΛΟΣ", meaning an adversary or legal accuser.</note> stand at his right hand.
When he is judged, let him come forth
condemned,
And let his prayer be turned
into sin.
Let his days be
few,
And let another take
his office <note>original: "ΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΗΝ", meaning a position of oversight; famously quoted in the New Testament regarding the replacement of Judas Iscariot.</note>.
Let his sons be
orphans,
And his wife a widow.
Let his sons be tossed about
and moved, and let them beg;
Let them be cast out from their
homesteads.
Let the creditor search out everything
that belongs to him,
And let strangers plunder
the fruits of his labors.
Let there be no one to help him,
Nor let there be anyone who takes pity
on his orphans.
Let his children be
destroyed;
In a single generation let his name
be blotted out.
May the lawlessness
of his fathers be remembered before the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΥ", sacred form of "Kyrios".</note>,
And let the sin of his mother
not be blotted out.
Let them be before the <term>Lord</term>
continually,
And let the memory of him be destroyed
from the earth.
Because he did not remember
to show mercy,
And he persecuted the needy and
poor man,
And the one broken in heart,
to put them to death.
And he loved a curse,
And it shall come to him;
And he did not desire a blessing,
And it shall be far from him.
And he put on a curse like a
garment,
And it entered like water
into his inner parts,
And like oil into
his bones.

# ODE OF MOSES IN EXODUS

Let us sing to the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "KW", an abbreviation for *Kyrio*.</note>, for gloriously has he
been glorified; horse and rider he has cast 
into the sea.
A helper and a protector he has become to me 
unto salvation;
this is my <term>God</term> <note>original: "ThS", abbreviation for *Theos*.</note> and I will glorify him, 
the <term>God</term> of my father and I will exalt him.
The <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "KS", abbreviation for *Kyrios*.</note> shattering wars, the <term>Lord</term>
is his name.
<margin>2</margin> The chariots of Pharaoh and his power 
he has cast into the sea;
the chosen mounted captains 
he drowned in the Red Sea.
With the deep he covered them; 
they sank into the depths like a stone.
<margin>3</margin> Your right hand, O <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "KE", abbreviation for *Kyrie*.</note>, has been glorified in strength;
your right hand, O <term>Lord</term>, has shattered the enemies.
And in the abundance of your glory you crushed 
the adversaries;
you sent forth your wrath and it 
consumed them like stubble.
And through the breath of your anger the water stood apart; 
the waters became thick like a wall, 
the waves became thick in the midst of 
the sea.
The enemy said: "I will pursue and overtake, 
I will divide the spoils, I will satisfy my soul, 
I will kill with my sword, my hand 
shall rule."
You sent forth your <term>spirit</term> <note>original: "PNA", abbreviation for *pneuma*.</note>, the sea 
covered them; 
they sank like lead in the mighty water.
<margin>5</margin> Who is like you among the gods, O <term>Lord</term>? 
Who is like you? Glorified among the saints, 
wonderful in glories, performing wonders.
You stretched out your right hand; the earth 
swallowed them.
In your righteousness, you guided this 
people of yours whom you redeemed; 
by your strength, you have called them into 
your holy resting place.
The nations heard and were angry; 
pangs of sorrow seized those dwelling in 
Philistia.
Then the chiefs of Edom hurried, 
and the rulers of the Moabites—trembling 
seized them; 
all the inhabitants of Canaan 
melted away.
May fear and trembling fall upon them;

<column-break/>

By the greatness of your arm let them 
be turned to stone, until your 
people pass by, O <term>Lord</term>, until 
this people of yours whom you acquired pass by.
Bring them in and plant them 
upon the mountain of your inheritance, 
in your prepared dwelling place 
which you have made, O <term>Lord</term>; 
the sanctuary, O <term>Lord</term>, which your hands prepared.
The <term>Lord</term> reigning for the age and 
unto the age and beyond, 
because the horse of Pharaoh entered with chariots 
and riders into the sea, 
and the <term>Lord</term> brought upon them the water 
of the sea, 
but the sons of Israel walked through dry land 
in the midst of the sea.

# PRAYER OF HEZEKIAH <note>original: ΠΡΟΣΕΥΧΗ ΕΖΕΚΙΟΥ. While titled "Hezekiah," the following text is the Prayer of Habakkuk from the Old Testament.</note>

Were you angry with the rivers, <term>Lord</term>? <note>original: "KE", an abbreviation for *Kyrie*.</note>
Or was your wrath against the rivers?
Or was your surge against the sea?
For you mounted your horses,
and your riding was salvation.
Bending, you bent your bow
against the scepters, says the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "KS", abbreviation for *Kyrios*.</note>.
The earth shall be torn asunder by rivers;
the peoples shall see you and be in labor,
scattering the waters of its passage.
The abyss gave forth its voice,
the height of its imagination.
The sun was lifted up and the moon stood
in its order.
At the light of your arrows they shall go,
at the radiance of the lightning of your weapons.
With a threat you will diminish the earth,
and in wrath you will bring down the nations.
You went forth for the salvation of your people,
to save your anointed ones <note>original: "τους χριστους σου" (tous christous sou). In a Jewish context, this refers to kings or priests; in a Christian context, it was often interpreted as referring to the followers of Christ.</note>.
You cast death upon the heads
of the lawless.
You raised up bonds as far as the neck.
You cut through the heads of the rulers
in an ecstasy.
They shall be shaken by it;
they shall open their bridles,
like a poor man eating in secret.
And you brought your horses
into the sea, troubling the great waters.
I watched and my belly trembled
at the sound of the prayer of my lips;
and trembling entered into my bones,
and my strength was troubled
beneath me.
I will rest in the day of my affliction,
to go up to the people of my sojourn.
For the fig tree shall not bear fruit,
and there shall be no produce on the
vines.
The labor of the olive tree shall fail,
and the fields shall yield no food.
Sheep have failed from the fold,
and there are no oxen at the
mangers. But I will exult in the <term>Lord</term>;
I will rejoice in <term>God</term> <note>original: "THO", abbreviation for *Theo*.</note> my Savior.
The <term>Lord</term> my <term>God</term> is my strength,
and he will set my feet for a
completion.
He brings me up upon the high places,
to be victorious in his song.

I shall leave behind the remaining years.
I said: I shall no longer see the salvation
of <term>God</term> upon the earth;

# THE PRAYER OF MANASSEH

**O** [Lord], who made heaven and earth 
with all their host <note>original: "kosmo." While often translated as "world," in this context it refers to the "host" or "arrangement" of the stars and heavenly powers.</note>;
who bound the sea by the word 
of your command; 
who closed the <term>abyss</term> <note>original: "abysson." In the ancient world, this referred to the primal deep or the subterranean waters.</note> and sealed it 
with your fearful and glorious 
name; 
before whom all things shudder and tremble 
because of the face of your power. 
For the majesty of your glory 
is unbearable, 
and the wrath of your threat 
against sinners is irresistible; 
yet the mercy of your promise 
is immeasurable and unsearchable. 
For you are the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "KE," a shortened form (nomen sacrum) of *Kyrie*.</note> Most High, 
compassionate, long-suffering, 
and very merciful, 
and relenting over the evils of men. 
You then, <term>Lord</term>, the <term>God</term> <note>original: "THS," a shortened form of *Theos*.</note> of the righteous, 
did not appoint repentance for the righteous—
for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, 
who did not sin against you—
but you appointed repentance for me, 
the sinner. 
For I have sinned more than the number 
of the sands of the sea; 
my lawless acts have multiplied, 
and I am not worthy to gaze upon 
and see the height of heaven 
because of the multitude of my injustices. 
I am bent down by many an iron 
chain, 
so that I might not lift my head <note>original: "ananeusai," literally to nod up or look up.</note> because of 
my sins, and there is no relief for me. 
Because I provoked your anger 
and did what was evil before you, 
not doing your will and not keeping 
your commandments <note>original: "prosschocheismata," likely a variant of ordinances or commands.</note>. 
And now I bend the knee of my heart, 
begging for your goodness. 
I have sinned, <term>Lord</term>, I have sinned, 
and I know my lawless acts. 
I ask, begging you: 
Forgive me, <term>Lord</term>, forgive me! 
Do not destroy me along with 
my injustices, 
nor be angry forever and 
store up my sins, 
nor condemn me to the 
lowest parts of the earth.

<column-break/>

**F**or you are the <term>Lord</term>, the <term>God</term> of those who repent, 
and in me you will show 
your goodness; 
for though I am unworthy, you will save me 
according to your great mercy. 
And I will praise you continually 
all the days of my life. 
For all the power of the heavens 
sings your praise, 
and yours is the glory forever. Amen.

# THE PRAYER OF AZARIAH <note>Known as the prayer of one of the three youths in the fiery furnace, from the Greek additions to Daniel 3:26-45.</note>

**B**lessed are you, <term>Lord</term>, the <term>God</term> of our fathers, 
and praised and glorified is 
your name forever. 
For you are righteous in all that 
you have done for us, 
and all your works are true, 
and your ways are straight, 
and all your judgments are true. 
And you have executed true judgments 
in everything you have brought upon us, 
and upon the holy city 
of our ancestors, <term>Israel</term> <note>original: "IHL," abbreviation for *Israel*. While the text says "Israel," the standard version usually refers to the holy city of Jerusalem.</note>. 
For in truth and judgment you brought 
all these things because of our sins. 
For we have sinned and acted lawlessly 
by departing from you, 
and we have sinned in all things and 
did not listen to your commandments, 
nor did we keep them, 
nor did we do them, 
as you commanded us, 
so that it might go well with us. 
And everything you have brought upon us, 
and everything you have done to us, 
you have done in true judgment. 
And you handed us over into the hands of 
lawless enemies, most hateful rebels, 
and to an unjust king, the most wicked 
in all the earth <note>This refers to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, who exiled the Jewish people.</note>. 
And now we cannot open 
our mouths; 
shame and reproach have come 
upon your servants and those 
who worship you. 
Do not hand us over utterly 
for your name's sake, 
and do not break 
your covenant, 
and do not take away your mercy 
from us.

# ♰ JOB ♰

THERE WAS A MAN IN THE LAND OF UZ WHOSE NAME WAS JOB.
AND THAT MAN WAS TRUE,
BLAMELESS, RIGHTEOUS, GOD-FEARING,
ABSTAINING FROM EVERY EVIL
DEED.
AND TO HIM WERE BORN SEVEN SONS AND
THREE DAUGHTERS.
AND HIS LIVESTOCK WERE SEVEN
THOUSAND SHEEP,
THREE THOUSAND CAMELS,
FIVE HUNDRED YOKE OF OXEN,
FIVE HUNDRED FEMALE DONKEYS AT PASTURE,
AND A VERY GREAT HOUSEHOLD.
AND HE HAD GREAT WORKS UPON THE EARTH.
AND THAT MAN WAS NOBLE AMONG THOSE
OF THE RISING SUN. <note>original: ΑΦ ΗΛΙΟΥ ΑΝΑΤΟΛΩΝ; a poetic way to describe the "people of the East."</note>
AND HIS SONS, COMING TOGETHER
WITH ONE ANOTHER,
WOULD MAKE A FEAST EVERY DAY,
TAKING ALONG AT THE SAME TIME THEIR
THREE SISTERS
TO EAT AND DRINK WITH THEM.
AND WHEN THE DAYS
OF THE FEAST WERE FINISHED,
JOB WOULD SEND AND PURIFY THEM,
RISING IN THE MORNING;
HE OFFERED SACRIFICES FOR THEM
ACCORDING TO THEIR NUMBER,
AND ONE CALF FOR A SIN OFFERING FOR
THEIR SOULS.
FOR JOB SAID, "LEST PERHAPS MY SONS
HAVE THOUGHT EVIL IN THEIR HEARTS
AGAINST GOD." <note>original: ΘΝ, an abbreviation of *Theon*; a <term>nomen sacrum</term>.</note>

<summary>Eliphaz challenges Job's righteousness by recounting a terrifying nocturnal vision of a spirit who proclaimed that no mortal is pure before God. He argues that suffering is the result of foolishness or wickedness and urges Job to turn back to the Almighty, who controls the natural world and humbles the crafty.</summary>
<keywords>Eliphaz, Job, vision, spirit, ant-lion, clay houses, divine justice, Septuagint, Greek Uncial</keywords>

### WEALTH UNJUSTLY GATHERED
**Wealth gathered unjustly** shall be vomited out from his belly; a death-angel shall drag him out of his house. He shall suck the venom of dragons, and the tongue of a snake shall slay him. Let him not see the milking of nomads, nor the pastures of honey and butter. He labored for empty and vain things; he provided wealth from which he shall not taste—it is like unchewed, undigested nightshade <note>original: *strychnon*, a bitter or poisonous plant like nightshade, used here to describe wealth that cannot be enjoyed.</note>. 

For he crushed the houses of many weak ones, and he plundered a dwelling but did not establish it. For there is no salvation for him in his possessions, nor shall his good things flourish. Because of this, let him not be exalted; there is nothing left for his food. When he thinks he is already filled, he shall be distressed; every necessity shall come upon him, and every pain <note>The Greek *diastera* suggests a piercing or internal distress.</note>. 

May God send upon him the fury of His wrath; He has let loose pains upon him, and he shall not be saved from the hand of iron <note>A poetic reference to the sword.</note>. A bronze bow shall wound him, and an arrow shall pass through his body. May lightning not walk in his dwelling! Terrors are upon him, and all darkness shall await him. Unquenchable fire shall consume him, and a stranger shall bring evil to his house. 

Let the heaven reveal his iniquities, and let the earth rise up against him. Let destruction drag his house to an end, and let a day of wrath come upon him. This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord <term>ΚΥ</term> <note>original: *KY*, Nomina Sacra for *Kyriou*, "of the Lord."</note>, and the possession of his goods from the Overseer <note>original: *episkopou*, referring to God as the Watcher or Overseer.</note>.

**Hear me, hear my words**, so that this might not be the consolation I receive from you. Bear with me and I will speak, and then do not mock me. For is my complaint against man? And why should I not be angry? Look at me and wonder, placing your hand upon your mouth. For if I remember it, I am troubled, and pains seize my flesh. 

Why do the ungodly live? They have grown old and are in wealth. Their seed is according to their heart's desire, and their children are before their eyes. Their houses prosper, and fear is nowhere; there is no scourge from the Lord <term>ΚΥ</term> <note>original: *KY*, Nomina Sacra for *Kyriou*.</note> upon them. <summary>In these passages from Job 35 and 36, Elihu argues that God is so transcendent that human sin or righteousness does not affect Him personally, yet He remains a just judge who eventually hears the cry of the oppressed and disciplines the wayward. He contrasts the fate of the righteous, who are exalted to thrones, with the hypocrites and ungodly who refuse to learn from divine correction.</summary>

And it is written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord <note>original: KS — a contraction for Kyrios (Lord), a common scribal practice known as Nomina Sacra.</note> raises. This man is interpreted from the Syriac book as dwelling in the land of Uz, on the borders of Idumea <note>The Greek name for the biblical region of Edom.</note> and Arabia. His name was previously Jobab. Having taken an Arabian wife, he fathered a son named Ennon. He was the son of his father Zareth, one of the sons of Esau, and of his mother Bossora, so that he was the fifth generation from Abraham. And these were the kings who reigned in Edom, which country he also ruled: first, Balak the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dennaba. And after Balak, Jobab, who is called Job. And after him, Asom, the governor from the region of Teman. And after him, Adad the son of Barad, who destroyed Midian in the plain of Moab, and the name of his city was Gethaim. And the friends who came to him were Eliphaz, of the sons of Esau, king of the Temanites; Bildad, the tyrant <note>original: tyrannos — in this context, it refers to a local ruler or prince rather than a cruel dictator.</note> of the Shuhites; and Sophar, king of the Minaians.

<column-break/>

## THE PROVERBS OF SOLOMON, SON OF DAVID,
## WHO REIGNED IN ISRAEL.

To know wisdom and instruction, and to perceive words of understanding; to receive the turns of words, and to perceive righteousness, and judgment, and to direct paths; that he might give craftiness to the simple, and to the young child perception and understanding. For by hearing these things, a wise man will become wiser, and a man of understanding will gain direction; he will perceive a parable and a dark saying, the words of the wise and their riddles. The fear of the Lord <note>original: KY — contraction for Kyrios (Lord).</note> is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding belongs to all who practice it; and piety toward God <note>original: THN — contraction for Theon (God).</note> is the beginning of perception; but the ungodly will despise wisdom and instruction.

Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and do not reject the laws of your mother; for you shall receive a crown of graces for your head, and a golden chain around your neck. My son, let not ungodly men lead you astray, nor should you consent if they exhort you, saying: "Come with us, let us share in blood, and let us hide the righteous man in the earth unjustly; let us swallow him alive, as Hades does, and let us remove his memory from the earth; let us seize his costly possessions, and let us fill our houses with spoils. Cast in your lot among us, and let us all possess one common purse." 

Do not go on the road with them, but turn your foot away from their paths; for their feet run toward evil, and they are swift to shed blood. For nets are not spread for birds unjustly; for they, participating in murder, store up evils for themselves; and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.

# The Proverbs of Solomon

### The End of Folly
For the feet of **Folly** lead those who follow her
down into death, even into the grave <note>original: ADHN — Hades, the underworld</note>.
Her steps are not firmly fixed,
for she does not travel the paths of life;
her tracks are slippery and difficult to follow.
Now therefore, my son, listen to me,
and do not make **my words** void.
Keep your way far from her;
do not draw near to the doors of her houses,
lest you give up your life to others
and your livelihood to the unmerciful.
Lest strangers be filled with **your strength**,
and your hard-earned labors enter the houses
of those who are not your own.
In the end, you will regret it,
when the very flesh of your body
is worn away.
Then you will say, “How I hated discipline!
My heart turned away from reproof.
I did not listen to the voice of my teacher,
nor did I lean my ear to those
who instructed me.
I was nearly brought to total ruin
in the midst of the assembly and the congregation.”

### Fidelity and Joy
<margin>all / the</margin> Drink waters from your own vessels,
and from the springs of your own wells.
Let your waters overflow for you
from your own fountain;
let your waters spread throughout
the public squares.
Let them belong to you alone,
and let no stranger share them with you.
Let your fountain of water be your own,
and **rejoice** with the wife
of your youth.
Let her be to you as a lovely doe of friendship
and a graceful foal; let her converse with you.
Let her own fountain lead you and stay with you
at all times;
for by being devoted to her friendship,
you shall be greatly increased.
Do not be captivated by a woman who is not your own,
nor be held in the arms of one
who is a stranger.
For the ways of a man are before
the eyes of God <note>original: THY — Theou</note>.

<column-break/>

And He watches closely
all his paths.
Iniquities ensnare a man,
and each is held fast by the cords
of his own sins.
Such a man dies among the undisciplined;
he is cast out from the abundance
of his own livelihood
<margin>6.~</margin> and perished because of his folly.

### On Debts and Industry
My son, if you become a guarantor for your friend,
you will hand over your hand to an enemy.
For a man’s own lips are a strong snare,
and he is caught by the words of his own mouth.
Do, my son, what I command you
and save yourself;
<margin>con / cerning [friend]</margin> for you have fallen into the hands of evil men
because of your friend.
Do not grow weary,
but go and provoke the friend
for whom you have given security.
Give no sleep to your eyes,
nor let your eyelids slumber,
so that you may be saved like a gazelle from a snare
and like a bird from a trap.

Go to the **ant**, O sluggard!
Observe his ways, be envious of them,
and become wiser than he.
For though he has no field to farm,
no one to compel him,
and no master to rule over him,
he prepares his food in the summer
and makes a great store during the harvest.
<margin>7.~</margin>
Or go to the **bee** <note>This beautiful description of the bee is found in the Greek Septuagint but not in the standard Hebrew Bible.</note>,
and learn how industrious she is,
and how dignified she makes her work.
Her labors are used by kings and commoners
to bring about health;
she is desired and held in honor by everyone.
Though she is weak in physical strength,
she has been brought forward because
she honors **Wisdom**.

How long, O sluggard, will you lie there?
When will you be raised from your sleep?
You sleep a little, you sit a little,
you slumber a little,
and for a little while you fold your arms
across your chest.
Then **Poverty** comes upon you
like an evil traveler.

# The Proverbs of Solomon

### The Wiles of the Seductress
But her feet do not rest in her own house;
for a certain time she roams outside,
and for a time in the squares,
lying in wait at every corner.
Then she caught him and kissed him,
and with a shameless face she spoke to him:
“I have a peace offering;
today I am paying my vows.
Because of this, I came out to meet you;
longing for your presence, I have found you.
I have spread my bed with cords,
and I have laid it with tapestries from Egypt.
I have sprinkled my couch with saffron,
and my house with cinnamon.
Come and let us enjoy friendship <note>The Greek "philia" here suggests an intimate or affectionate bond, often used euphemistically in this context.</note>

come and let us revel in love.
For my husband is not at home;
he has gone on a long journey,
taking a bag of money in his hand;
after many days he will return to his house.”

So she led him astray with much conversation,
and with the snares of her lips she drove him off course.
And he followed her, beguiled <note>original: ΚΕΠΦΩΘΕΙΣ (kepphōtheis) — meaning to be easily deceived or flighty like a 'kepphos' (a type of sea-bird).</note>,

<margin>31:</margin> A courageous woman, who shall find? <note>This begins the famous 'Woman of Valor' poem (Eshet Chayil). In the Greek text, 'andreia' (courageous/brave/manly) is used to describe her strength of character.</note>

### THE WORDS OF THE PREACHER, SON OF DAVID,
### KING OF ISRAEL IN JERUSALEM.

Vanity of vanities, said
the Preacher;
vanity of vanities,
all things are vanity.
What is the profit for a man
in all his toil which he toils
under the sun?
A generation goes, and a generation comes,
but the earth stands forever.
And the sun rises, and the sun sets,
and it hurries to its place.
Rising there, it moves
toward the south,
and circles toward the north.
The wind <note>original: 'pneuma' (πνεῦμα). This word means both "spirit" and "wind." Given the context of sun and sea, it refers here to the atmospheric wind.</note> moves in circling circles,
and the wind returns
upon its circuits.
All the winter-torrents <note>original: 'cheimarroi' (χείμαρροι). Streams that flow primarily during the rainy winter season.</note> move
into the sea,
and yet the sea is not filled;
to the place where the winter-torrents move,
there they return to move
once again.
All words are wearying;
a man will not be able to speak of it.
The eye will not be satisfied
with seeing,
nor will the ear be filled
from hearing.
What is that which has been? That very thing which shall be.
And what is that which has been done? That very thing which 
shall be done.
And there is nothing entirely new
under the sun.
Should anyone speak and say, "See, this is new,"
it has already happened in the ages
that have happened before us.
There is no memory of the first things,
and even for the last things that happen,
there will be no memory of them
among those who will come
at the very end.
I, the Preacher, became
king over Israel in Jerusalem,
and I gave my heart to
seek out
and to observe in wisdom
concerning all things.

<margin>2.</margin> I said in my heart, "Come now, I will
test you with gladness and look upon what is good."
And behold, this also is vanity.
To laughter I said, "It is madness,"

And I searched in my heart

while my heart guided me in wisdom,

I enlarged my works;
I built houses for myself;
I planted vineyards for myself;

and I planted in them every kind of fruit tree.
I made for myself pools of water

I acquired male and female servants,
and home-born slaves were born to me;
and the possession of herds and

beyond all those who were
before me in Jerusalem.

I gathered for myself also 
silver and gold,
and the treasures of kings
and of provinces.
I appointed for myself male and female singers,
and the delights of the sons of mankind:
a male cupbearer and female cupbearers <note>original: 'oinochoon kai oinochoas' (οἰνοχόον καὶ οἰνοχόας). This refers to those who pour wine, but in this context, it often implies the luxuries of a royal court.</note>.
And I became great and increased
beyond all those who were
before me in Jerusalem.
And indeed, my wisdom remained with me.
And whatever my eyes desired,

my labor,
and this was my reward from 
all my labor.
And I looked upon all
my works
which my hands had made,
and upon the labor I had toiled
to perform;
and behold, all was vanity and a 
striving after wind,
and there is no profit under the sun.
And I turned to look at wisdom,
and madness, and folly;
for what man will come after 
the counsel <note>original: 'boulēs' (βουλῆς). The text asks who can follow the king's example or decisions.</note>
of those who have already done it?
And I saw that there is an advantage
for wisdom over folly,
just as the advantage of light
over darkness.
The eyes of the wise man are in his 
head,
but the fool walks in darkness.
And I myself realized that one fate <note>original: 'synantēma' (συνάντημα), literally an "encounter" or "happening."</note>
will happen to them all.
And I said in my heart,
"As the fate of the fool,
so it will happen to me also."
Why then was I excessively wise? I spoke in my heart,
because the fool speaks from his excess;
for this too is vanity.
For there is no remembrance of the wise man
along with the fool forever.

<summary>This page contains the opening reflections of Ecclesiastes, where the author (traditionally Solomon) examines the futility of human wisdom, pleasure, and great works. He concludes that despite his vast wealth and achievements in Jerusalem, everything is "vanity" because both the wise man and the fool share the same ultimate fate.</summary>

# THE WISDOM OF SOLOMON

->**LOVE RIGHTEOUSNESS, YOU WHO JUDGE THE EARTH.**<-
Think of the Lord <note>original: "ΚΥ," a sacred name abbreviation for "Kyriou" (Lord).</note> in goodness,
And seek him in simplicity of heart.
Because he is found by those who do not 
test him;
And he reveals himself to those who do not 
distrust him.
For crooked thoughts separate 
from God <note>original: "ΘΥ," a sacred name abbreviation for "Theou" (God).</note>;
And when his power is tested,
It convicts the foolish.
For into a deceitful soul,
Wisdom shall not enter;
Nor will she dwell in a body
indebted to sin.
For a holy spirit <note>original: "ΠΝΑ," a sacred name abbreviation for "Pneuma" (Spirit).</note> of wisdom will flee 
deceit,
And will withdraw from thoughts 
that are without understanding;
And will be rebuked when 
unrighteousness comes in.
For the spirit of wisdom is a lover of humanity <note>term: "philanthrōpon," literally meaning "lover of mankind," a trait emphasizing God's kindness toward people.</note>;
And will not hold a blasphemer 
guiltless for his lips.
For God <note>original: "ΘΣ," abbreviation for "Theos" (God).</note> is a witness 
of his heart, and a true observer
of his heart,
And a hearer of his tongue.
For the Spirit of the Lord <note>original: "ΠΝΑ ΚΥ," Spirit of the Lord.</note> has filled 
the world;
And that which holds all things together has 
knowledge of every voice.
Therefore, no one who speaks unrighteous 
things will go unnoticed;
Nor will Justice, when she convicts, 
pass him by.
For there shall be an inquiry 
into the counsels of the ungodly;
And the sound of his words shall come to the Lord <note>original: "ΚΝ," abbreviation for "Kyrion" (Lord).</note>
to convict him of his lawless deeds.
For the ear of jealousy hears 
all things;
And the sound of grumbling is not 
hidden.
Beware then of useless 
grumbling;
And refrain your tongue 
from slandering.

<column-break/>

Because a secret word will not go 
for nothing;
And a lying mouth 
destroys the soul.
Do not seek death in the 
error of your life;
And do not bring destruction upon yourselves
by the works of your hands.
For God did not make death;
Neither does he delight in the destruction of the living.
For he created all things so that they might exist;
And the generative forces of the world 
are wholesome;
And there is no poison 
of destruction in them,
Nor is the kingdom of Hades <note>original: "adou," referring to the realm of the dead.</note> upon the earth.
For righteousness is immortal.
But the ungodly, by their hands and 
words, have summoned death;
Thinking him to be a friend, 
they were consumed;
And they made a covenant with him,
Because they are worthy 
to be of his portion.
<margin>2</margin> For they said among themselves, 
reasoning incorrectly:
"Short and sorrowful 
is our life;
And there is no healing at the 
end of a man;
And no one has been known to return from Hades.
Because we were born by chance;
And hereafter we shall be 
as though we had never been.
Because the breath in our nostrils is smoke;
And reason is a spark in the 
beating of our heart.
When it is extinguished, the body 
will turn to ashes,
And the spirit <note>original: "ΠΝΑ," here referring to the breath of life.</note> will be dispersed 
like thin air.
And our name will be 
forgotten in time;
And no one will remember 
our works.
And our life will pass away 
like the traces of a cloud,
And will be scattered like a mist,
Chased by the rays of the sun,
And weighed down 
by its heat."

<summary>This page introduces the Wisdom of Solomon, urging rulers to seek righteousness and warning that Wisdom avoids the deceitful. It also presents the "reasoning of the ungodly," who claim life is short and accidental, leading them to embrace death rather than the immortality of righteousness.</summary>
<keywords>Wisdom of Solomon, righteousness, Spirit of the Lord, justice, immortality, origin of death, Hades, ungodly reasoning, breath of life</keywords>

They no longer keep their lives or their marriages pure;
But one either kills another by lying in wait, or grieves him by adultery.
And all things are a confused mixture: blood and murder, theft and deceit,
Corruption, unfaithfulness, turmoil, perjury,
Confusion of the good, forgetfulness of favors <note>original: "charitos amnestia" — ingratitude for grace or divine gifts.</note>,
Defilement of souls, perversion of birth <note>May refer to sexual perversion or reproductive crimes.</note>,
Disorder in marriage, adultery, and shamelessness.
For the worship of idols that should not even be named
Is the beginning, the cause, and the end of every evil.
For their worshippers either go mad in their festivals, or prophesy lies,
Or live unjustly, or quickly commit perjury.
For since they trust in soulless idols,
They do not expect to be harmed when they swear falsely.
But justice shall pursue them for both reasons:
Because they thought evilly of <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΥ" (Theou)</note> by devoting themselves to idols,
And because they swore unjustly in deceit, despising holiness.
For it is not the power of the things by which they swear,
But the penalty due to those who sin,
That always follows the transgression of the unrighteous.

<margin>15.</margin> But You, our <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘC" (Theos)</note>, are kind and true,
Patient, and governing all things in mercy.
For even if we sin, we are Yours, for we know Your power;
But we will not sin, knowing that we are counted as Yours.

<summary>This passage provides a psychological and political history of idolatry, tracing it back to grieving parents and the cult of personality surrounding kings. It concludes by linking false worship to a total breakdown of social morality and contrasting this chaos with the mercy of the true God.</summary>

# + PROLOGUE +

...having received the righteous as guests, they punished them with terrible labors. 
And they were struck with blindness, just as those others were at the doors of the righteous man <note>A reference to the men of Sodom who were blinded when they tried to attack Lot’s house (Genesis 19:11).</note>, 
when, surrounded by yawning darkness, each one sought the way to his own door. 
For the elements were rearranged among themselves, just as the notes on a harp change the name of the rhythm, yet the sound always remains the same. 
This can be accurately inferred from the sight of what occurred. 
For land creatures were changed into water creatures, and swimming things moved onto the land. 
Fire retained its power in water, forgetting its own nature, and water forgot its quenching nature. 
On the other hand, flames did not wither the flesh of perishable creatures walking among them, 
nor did they melt the ice-like, easily melted kind of ambrosial food <note>This refers to Manna, the "bread from heaven," which was said to look like hoarfrost or ice but provided miraculous nourishment.</note>. 
For in all things, O <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΕ" (Kyrie) — a common abbreviation in sacred texts.</note>, You have magnified Your people and glorified them; 
and You did not overlook them, standing by them in every time and place.

-> THE WISDOM OF SOLOMON <-

<unclear>...</unclear>

<column-break/>

Many great things have been given to us through the Law and the Prophets and the others who followed them, for which it is right to praise Israel for instruction and wisdom. 
Since it is necessary not only for those who read to become knowledgeable themselves, but also for those outside to be able to be helpful to those who love learning, both by speaking and writing; 
my grandfather Jesus, having given himself more and more to the reading of the Law and the Prophets and the other books of our fathers, and having acquired sufficient mastery in them, was himself led to write something of the things pertaining to instruction and wisdom. 
This was so that those who love learning, becoming familiar with these things, might make much more progress by living according to the Law. 

You are invited, therefore, to read with goodwill and attention, and to be indulgent in those places where we may seem to fail in some of the phrases, despite our diligent labor in translation. 
For things spoken in Hebrew <note>original: "ἑβραϊστί"</note> do not have the same force when they are translated into another language. 
And not only these things, but even the Law itself, and the Prophecies, and the rest of the books, have no small difference when they are spoken in their original form. 

For in the thirty-eighth year of King Euergetes <note>Likely Ptolemy VII Euergetes, dating this translator's arrival in Egypt to approximately 132 BCE.</note>, having come to Egypt and stayed there, I found no small copy of instruction <note>original: "ἀφομοίωμα παιδείας" — this likely refers to a version of the book his grandfather had written.</note>. I thought it most necessary that I too should apply some diligence and hard work to translate this book. 
I have applied much sleeplessness and skill during this span of time to bring the book to completion and publish it, also for those living abroad <note>original: "ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ" — literally "in the parish" or "sojourn," referring here to the Jewish community living outside of Judea.</note> who wish to learn and prepare their character to live according to the Law.

<summary>This page concludes the Wisdom of Solomon with a poetic description of nature being "re-tuned" like a harp during the Exodus, followed by the grandson of Jesus son of Sirach explaining why he translated his grandfather's Hebrew wisdom into Greek for the Jewish community in Egypt.</summary>
<keywords>Exodus, Manna, creation, translation, Prologue to Sirach, King Euergetes, Hebrew to Greek, Law and Prophets, Egypt</keywords>

# THE WISDOM OF JESUS SON OF SIRACH

<margin>+</margin>All wisdom is from the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΥ" (Kyriou) — an abbreviated form of 'Lord' used in sacred manuscripts.</note> and is with Him forever.
The sand of the seas and the drops of rain
and the days of eternity—who can count them?
The height of heaven and the breadth of the earth
and the abyss and wisdom—who can trace them out?
Wisdom was created before all things,
and the understanding of prudence from eternity.
To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed?
And who has known her subtleties?
There is one who is wise, greatly to be feared,
seated upon His throne.
The Lord Himself created her;
He saw her and counted her,
and He poured her out upon all His works.
She is with all flesh according to His gift,
and He supplied her to those who love Him.
The fear of the Lord <note>In this context, 'fear' (phobos) refers to a deep, holy reverence and awe rather than terror.</note> is glory and a boast,
and gladness and a crown of rejoicing.
The fear of the Lord will delight the heart,
and will give gladness and joy and long life.
For the one who fears the Lord, it will be well at the end,
and on the day of his death, he will be blessed.
The beginning of wisdom is to fear the Lord,
and she was created together with the faithful in the womb.
She has nested among men as an eternal foundation,
and she will be trusted among their descendants.
The fullness of wisdom is to fear the Lord,
and she intoxicates them with her fruits.
She will fill their whole house with desirable things,
and the storehouses with her produce.
The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord,
making peace and health of healing to flourish.
He saw her and He counted her;
He rained down skill and knowledge of understanding,
and He exalted the glory of those who hold her fast.

<column-break/>

The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord,
and her branches are long life.
An unjust temper will not be able to be justified,
for the tipping of the scale of his temper is his downfall.
A patient man will hold out until the right time,
and afterward, gladness will be repaid to him.
He will hide his words until the right time,
and the lips of many will tell of his understanding.
In the treasures of wisdom is a parable of knowledge,
but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments,
and the Lord will supply her to you.
For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction,
and His delight is faithfulness and gentleness.
Do not be disobedient to the fear of the Lord,
and do not approach Him with a double heart <note>This refers to being "two-faced" or wavering in commitment.</note>.
Do not be a hypocrite in the sight of men,
and pay attention to your lips.
Do not exalt yourself, lest you fall
and bring dishonor upon your soul;
the Lord will reveal your secrets
and will cast you down in the midst of the congregation,
because you did not come with the fear of the Lord,
and your heart was full of deceit.

<margin>2.</margin>My child, if you come forward to serve the Lord,
prepare your soul for trial <note>original: "πειρασμόν" (peirasmon) — meaning testing, trial, or temptation.</note>.

and in the changes of your humiliation, be patient.
For gold is tested in the fire,
and acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.
Trust in Him, and He will help you;
make your ways straight and hope in Him.
You who fear the Lord, wait for His mercy.

# THE WISDOM OF SIRACH

THEN THE CREATOR OF ALL commanded me, 
and He who created me gave rest 
to my tent, and said: 
“Dwell in Jacob, 
and receive your inheritance in Israel.” 
Before the ages, from the beginning, He created me, 
and for all ages I shall not fail. 
In the holy tent I ministered 
before Him, and so in Zion 
I was established. 
In the beloved city likewise He gave me rest, 
and in Jerusalem was my authority. 
And I took root in a glorified people,

# THE WISDOM OF SIRACH
### Chapter 25

...in my heart, 
and the tenth I will speak with my tongue: 
A **man** <note>original: "ΑΝΟΣ" (anthropos) — a shorthand for "human" or "man."</note> who rejoices in his children, 
who lives to see the fall of his enemies. 
**Blessed** is he who lives with a sensible wife, 
and he who has not slipped with his tongue, 
and he who has not served a man unworthy of himself. 
**Blessed** is he who has found prudence, 
and he who speaks into the ears of those who listen. 
How great is he who has found wisdom! 
But there is none above him who fears the **Lord**. <note>original: "KN" (Kyrion) — shorthand for "Lord."</note> 
The fear of the **Lord** <note>original: "KY" (Kyriou) — "of the Lord."</note> surpasses all things; 
to whom can the one who holds it be compared?

Any wound, but not a wound of the **heart**; 
any wickedness, but not the wickedness of a **woman**; 
any affliction, but not the affliction of those who hate; 
any vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies. 
There is no poison worse than the poison of a snake, 
and there is no wrath worse than the wrath of an enemy. 
I would rather dwell with a lion or a dragon 
than dwell with a **wicked woman**. 

The wickedness of a woman changes her appearance 
and darkens her face like a bear. <note>original: "ΩΣ ΑΡΚΟΥ" — some manuscripts read "sackcloth," but "bear" is a common variant in the Greek tradition for this verse.</note> 
Her husband sits down among his neighbors, 
and hearing of her, he sighs bitterly. 
Any malice is small compared to the malice of a woman; 
may the lot of a sinner fall upon her! 

As a sandy ascent is to the feet of the aged, 
so is a talkative woman to a quiet man. 
Do not be ensnared by a woman's beauty, 
and do not desire a woman for her looks. 
There is anger, impudence, and great shame 
when a woman supports her husband. 
A downcast heart, a gloomy face, 
and a wounded heart come from a wicked woman.

<column-break/>

Hanging hands and paralyzed knees 
are caused by her who does not make her husband happy. 
From a woman was the beginning of sin, 
and because of her we all die. <note>A reference to the biblical story of Eve in the Garden of Eden.</note> 
Do not give water an outlet, 
nor a wicked woman freedom of speech. 
If she does not walk according to your hand, 
cut her off from your flesh. <note>A historical idiom for divorce or separation.</note>

### Chapter 26
<margin>26:</margin> **Blessed** is the husband of a good wife; 
the number of his days will be doubled. 
A virtuous woman cheers her husband, 
and he will fulfill his years in peace. 
A good wife is a good portion; 
she will be given to those who fear the **Lord**. 
Whether rich or poor, his heart is glad, 
and at all times his face is cheerful. 

At three things my heart was afraid, 
and at the fourth I was terrified: 
Slander in a city, the gathering of a mob, 
and a false accusation—these are all worse than death. 
But it is a grief of heart and mourning 
when a wife is jealous of another wife, 
and a scourge of the tongue that tells it to everyone. 
A wicked woman is like a swaying ox-yoke; 
he who tries to hold her is like one grasping a scorpion. 
A drunken woman is a cause of great anger; 
she will not even cover her own shame. 

A woman’s harlotry is seen in the lifting of her eyes, 
and she will be known by her eyelids. 
Keep a firm watch over a headstrong daughter, 
lest, finding an opportunity, she takes advantage of it. 
Watch out for her impudent eye, 
and do not be surprised if she sins against you. 
As a thirsty traveler opens his mouth 
and drinks from any water that is near, 
so she will sit before every tent-peg <note>A metaphor for sexual unfaithfulness or lack of discretion.</note> 
and open her quiver to every arrow.

and their insults are a miserable thing to hear.

and he will never find a friend for his soul. 
Love a friend and be faithful to him; 
but if you reveal his secrets, do not pursue him. 
For as a man has lost his enemy, 
so you have lost the friendship of your neighbor. 
And as a bird let out of your hand, 
so you have let your neighbor go, and you will not catch him. 
Do not follow him, for he has gone far away; 
he has escaped like a gazelle from a snare. 
For a wound may be bound up, 
and for an insult there is reconciliation; 
but he who reveals secrets is without hope. 

He who winks with his eye plans evil, 
and no one will draw him away from it. 
In your presence, his mouth is sweet, 
and he will marvel at your words; 
<note>The text breaks off here; the sense continues that he will later twist those same words.</note>

### Chapter 28

<margin>28.</margin> He who seeks vengeance will find vengeance from the **Lord**,
and He will surely keep a record
of his sins.
<margin>A</margin> Forgive your neighbor for the wrong done to you;
and then, when you pray, your own
sins will be forgiven.
Does a man <note>original: "ΑΝΟΣ" (Anthropos) — another nomen sacrum abbreviation for 'man' or 'human.'</note> harbor anger against another man,
and yet seek healing from the **Lord**?
Toward a man like himself he has no mercy,
and yet he prays about his own sins?
He himself, being mere flesh, persists in wrath;
who will make atonement for his sins?
Remember your end and stop
hating;
remember corruption and death, and
abide by the commandments.
Remember the commandments and do not
be angry with your neighbor;
remember the covenant of the **Most High**, and
overlook ignorance.
Abstain from strife, and you will
reduce your sins;
for a hot-tempered man will
kindle strife; and a sinful man
will disturb friends,

and in the midst of those at peace
he will sow slander.
According to the fuel of the fire, so
it will burn;
and according to the intensity of the
strife, it will burn;
according to the strength of the man, his
anger will be;
and according to his wealth, he will increase
his wrath.
A hasty quarrel kindles a fire;
and a hasty fight sheds blood.
If you blow on a spark, it will burn;
and if you spit on it, it will be extinguished;
and both come out of your
**mouth**.
Curse the whisperer and the double-tongued,
for they have destroyed many who were at peace.
A **third tongue** <note>original: "ΓΛΩΣΣΑ ΤΡΙΤΗ" — a Hebrew idiom for slander, referring to the "third" person involved: the speaker, the listener, and the victim.</note> has shaken many,
and scattered them from
nation to nation;
and it has pulled down strong cities,
and overturned the houses of great men.
A third tongue has cast out courageous
women,
and deprived them of the fruits of
their labors.
He who pays attention to it will not find
rest,
nor will he dwell in peace.
The blow of a whip makes a bruise,
but a blow of the tongue breaks bones.
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword,
but not as many as those fallen by the tongue.
**Blessed** is he who is sheltered from it,
who has not passed through its wrath;
who has not pulled its yoke,
and has not been bound by its chains.
For its yoke is a yoke of iron,
and its chains are chains of bronze.
Its death is an evil death,
and **Hades** <note>original: "ΑΔΗΣ" — the realm of the dead; the text suggests death is preferable to the damage caused by slander.</note> is more profitable than it.
It shall not take hold of the godly,
and they will not be burned in its
flame.
Those who forsake the **Lord** will fall
into it;
and it will burn in them and not
be extinguished;
it will be sent against them like a lion.

->On Children<-

<margin>30</margin> **H**e who loves his son will **frequently**
apply the whip to him, <note>original: "ΕΝΔΕΛΕΧΗΣΕΙ ΜΑΣΤΙΓΑΣ" (endeleschesei mastigas). While harsh to modern readers, ancient pedagogy viewed physical discipline as a sign of parental care and investment in a child's character.</note>
so that he may rejoice in his later years.
The one who disciplines his son will **benefit**
from him,
and among his acquaintances he will **boast**
of him.
The one who teaches his son will provoke
**envy** in his enemy,
and in the presence of friends he will
**exult** in him.
**H**is father has died, and yet
it is as if he did not die;
for he has left behind one **like himself**
after him.
In his life he saw him and **rejoiced**,
and at his death he was not grieved.
Against his enemies he left behind an avenger,
and for his friends, one to repay their kindness.
The one who pampers a son will bind up
his **wounds**,
and at every cry his heart will be
**troubled**.
An unbroken horse turns out stubborn,
and a son left to himself turns out headstrong.
**P**amper a child and he will **terrify** you;
play with him and he will bring you grief.
Do not laugh with him, lest you
share in his **sorrow**, and in the end
you set your teeth on edge. <note>original: "ΤΟΜΦΙΑΣΕΙΣ ΤΟΥΣ ΟΔΟΝΤΑΣ" (tomphiaseis tous odontas). A common idiom for experiencing bitter regret or consequences.</note>
Do not give him authority in his youth;
**bruise** his ribs while
he is a child,
lest he become stubborn and disobey you.
Discipline your son and **labor**
over him, so that you do not stumble
over his **shameful** conduct.
A poor man who is healthy and strong
in his vigor is better than a rich man
**afflicted** in his body.
Health and fitness are better than any
**gold**, and a robust body
is better than unmeasured wealth.

<column-break/>

<margin>10</margin> **T**here is no wealth better than
the health of the body,
and there is no **gladness** above
the joy of the heart.
Death is better than a bitter life
or a **lingering** sickness.
Good things poured out upon a
**closed** mouth
are like offerings of food placed
upon a **grave**. <note>The author argues that physical health is the prerequisite for enjoying any of life's pleasures; wealth is useless to a body that cannot function.</note>
**W**hat benefit is an offering to an idol?
For it can neither eat nor smell;
so is the one who is **afflicted** by the Lord—
looking with his eyes and groaning,
just as a **eunuch** embracing
a virgin and groaning. <note>An analogy for the frustration of having something desirable (like food or wealth) but being physically unable to enjoy it.</note>
Do not give your soul over to **sorrow**,
and do not afflict yourself with your own counsel.
Gladness of heart is the life of a man,
and the exultation of a man is long life.
**Love** your own soul and comfort
your heart;
and put sorrow far away from you,
for sorrow has **destroyed** many,
and there is no profit in it.
Envy and anger shorten one's days,
and anxiety brings **old age** before its time.
A cheerful heart is good at mealtimes;
it flourishes under the Lord’s blessing.
Sleeplessness over wealth consumes the flesh,
and the **worry** of it drives away sleep.
Sleeplessness over wealth melts the body.
**Listen** to me, O great ones of the people,
and you leaders of the assembly, give ear:
To a son, a wife, a brother, or a friend,
do not give **authority** over yourself while you live;
and do not give your money to another,
lest you repent and have to **beg** for it.
As long as you live and breath is in you,
do not surrender yourself to any person.
For it is **better** that your children should beg from you
than that you should look to the hands of your sons.
In all your works be **supreme**;
do not allow a stain upon your glory.
At the day of the completion of your life's days,
and at the time of your death, distribute
your **inheritance**.

Remember my sentence <note>original: "κρίμα" (krima), referring to the decree of death common to all humans.</note>, for so shall yours be:
**Yesterday for me, and today for you.**

and be comforted for him as his spirit departs.
The wisdom of a scribe <term>scribe: a "grammateus" was not just a copyist, but a scholar and teacher of the Law</term> comes through the opportunity of leisure,
and he who has little business will become wise.
How can he become wise who holds the plow,
and who glories in the shaft of the goad?
Who drives oxen and is occupied in their labors,

He will set his heart on turning furrows,

and he will struggle with the heat of the furnace.

He will set his heart to finish the glazing,

All these trust in their hands,

memorial,
