### Rom. ii. 26—iii. 31

...will his uncircumcision <note>original: "akrobystiai"; the state of being a non-Jew or Gentile</note> be counted as circumcision? Then he who is physically uncircumcised but keeps the law will judge you who, though having the written code and circumcision, are a law-breaker. For no one is a Jew who is merely one outwardly, nor is circumcision something external and physical. But a Jew is one inwardly; and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. His praise is not from men but from **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou; a "Nomina Sacra" (Sacred Name) abbreviation for God</note>.

<margin>2.</margin>What advantage then has the Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision? Much in every way! To begin with, the Jews were entrusted with the oracles of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note>. What if some were unfaithful? Does their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note>? By no means! Let **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"—Theos</note> be true, though every human being be a liar, as it is written: "So that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged." But if our unrighteousness serves to show the righteousness of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note>, what shall we say? That **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"</note> is unjust to inflict his wrath? (I am speaking in human terms.) By no means! For then how could **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"</note> judge the world? But if through my lie **GOD’S** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note> truthfulness abounds to his glory, why am I still being condemned as a sinner? And why not say—as we are slanderously charged and as some claim we say—"Let us do evil that good may come"? Their condemnation is just.

<margin>3.</margin>What then? Are we any better off? Not at all. For we have already charged that all, both Jews and Greeks, are under sin, as it is written: "None is righteous, no, not one; no one understands; no one seeks for **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΝ"—Theon</note>. All have turned aside; together they have become worthless; no one does good, not even one."

<column-break/>

<margin>>
>
>
>
>
>
>
>
>
></margin> "Their throat is an open grave; they use their tongues to deceive." "The venom of asps <note>A type of venomous snake</note> is under their lips." "Their mouth is full of curses and bitterness." "Their feet are swift to shed blood; ruin and misery are in their paths, and the way of peace they have not known." "There is no fear of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note> before their eyes." <note>The marginal symbols (>) indicate that the scribe is quoting Old Testament scripture, specifically a collection of verses from the Psalms and Isaiah.</note>

Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world may be held accountable to **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theō</note>. For by works of the law no human being <note>original: "pasa sarx"; literally "all flesh"</note> will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note> has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it—the righteousness of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note> through faith in **JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "IΥ ΧΥ"—Iēsou Christou; Sacred Name abbreviations</note> for all who believe. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note>, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in **CHRIST JESUS** <note>original: "ΧΩ IΥ"—Christō Iēsou</note>, whom **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"</note> put forward as a propitiation <note>term: propitiation - an offering that restores a relationship or turns away wrath; historically linked to the 'mercy seat' of the Ark of the Covenant</note> by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show his righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the one who justifies the one who has faith in **JESUS** <note>original: "IΥ"</note>.

Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. Or is **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"</note> the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also, since **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"</note> is one—who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith. Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law.

It features a chain of Old Testament quotations used to demonstrate the universal nature of human fallenness.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Apostle Paul's argument from the end of Chapter 3, transitioning into Chapter 4 and the beginning of Chapter 5. Having established that all have sinned, Paul now uses the historical figure of Abraham to demonstrate that "righteousness" (being right with God) has always been based on trust rather than performing religious rituals or following the Law of Moses.</meta>

### Rom. iv. 1—v. 3

WHAT THEN SHALL WE SAY that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found? For if Abraham was justified <note>original: "edikaiōthē"; to be declared righteous or put in a right relationship with God</note> by works, he has a reason to boast, but not before **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΝ"—Theon; a "Nomina Sacra" (Sacred Name) abbreviation for God</note>. For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theō</note>, and it was credited to him as righteousness." Now to the one who works, the wage is not credited according to grace but according to debt. 
<margin>Γ</margin> But to the one who does not work but believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness. 
<margin>Δ</margin> Just as David also speaks of the blessing of the man <note>original: "ΑΝΟΥ"—anthrōpou; human being</note> to whom **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"—Theos</note> credits righteousness apart from works: "Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man against whom the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚC"—Kyrios</note> will not credit sin." 

Is this blessing then for the circumcised <note>the Jewish people</note> or also for the uncircumcised? For we say that faith was credited to Abraham as righteousness. 
<margin>Ι</margin> How then was it credited? While he was circumcised or uncircumcised? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision! And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe through uncircumcision <note>referring to Gentiles or non-Jews</note>, so that righteousness might be credited to them, and the father of circumcision to those who are not only of the circumcision but also walk in the footsteps of the faith of our father <note>original: "ΠΡC"—patros; father</note> Abraham which he had while uncircumcised. For the promise to Abraham or to his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not through the law but through the righteousness of faith. 
<margin>C</margin> For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith has been made void and the promise has been nullified.

<column-break/>

For the law brings about wrath, but where there is no law, there is no transgression. But he did not waver at the promise of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"</note> through unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"</note>, and being fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to do. <summary>In this passage, Paul argues that Abraham was considered righteous by God because of his faith, long before he was circumcised, making him the spiritual father of both Jews and Gentiles. He concludes that through Jesus’s resurrection, believers are justified and can find peace and hope even in the midst of suffering.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Apostle Paul’s letter to the Romans, picking up mid-sentence from the previous page's discussion on how suffering produces endurance and character. ### Rom. v. 3 — vi. 9

...endurance produces character, and character produces hope. And hope does not put us to shame, because the love of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou; a Sacred Name abbreviation</note> has been poured into our hearts through the **HOLY SPIRIT** <note>original: "ΠΝΣ ΑΓΙΟΥ"—Pneumatos Agiou</note> who has been given to us.

For while we were still weak, at the right time, **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΣ"—Christos</note> died for the ungodly. For rarely will someone die for a righteous person—though perhaps for a good person someone might even dare to die.

<margin>o</margin> But **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΣ"—Theos</note> demonstrates His own love for us in that while we were still sinners, **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΣ"—Christos</note> died for us. Much more then, having now been justified <note>declared righteous or set right</note> by His blood, we shall be saved through Him from the wrath [of God]. For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theō</note> through the death of His **SON** <note>original: "ΥΥ"—Uiou</note>, much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved by His life. And not only this, but we also boast in **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theō</note> through our **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note> **JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "ΙΥ ΧΥ"—Iēsou Christou</note>, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one human being, and death through sin, and so death spread to all humanity because all sinned—for sin was in the world before the law, but sin is not charged to one's account when there is no law. Yet death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those whose sinning was not like the transgression of Adam, who is a <term>type</term> <note>original: "typos"; a person or event in history that foreshadows a future reality</note> of the one who was to come.

But the free gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, much more did the grace of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note> and the gift by the grace of the one man, **JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "ΙΥ ΧΥ"—Iēsou Christou</note>, overflow to the many. And the gift is not like the result of that one man’s sin: The judgment followed one sin and brought condemnation, but the free gift followed many trespasses and brought <term>justification</term> <note>original: "dikaiōma"; a legal verdict of acquittal</note>. For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned...

<column-break/>

...reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, **JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "ΙΥ ΧΥ"—Iēsou Christou</note>.

<margin>7</margin> So then, as through one trespass condemnation came to all people, so also through one righteous act justification of life came to all people.

<margin>7</margin> For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.

<margin>7</margin> Now the law crept in so that the trespass might increase. But where sin increased, grace overflowed all the more, so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through **JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "ΙΥ ΧΥ"—Iēsou Christou</note> our **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note>.

<margin>c</margin> What then shall we say? Should we continue in sin so that grace may increase? By no means! We who died to sin, how can we live in it any longer?

<margin>c</margin> Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into **CHRIST JESUS** <note>original: "ΧΥ ΙΥ"—Christou Iēsou</note> were baptized into His death? We were buried therefore with Him through baptism into death, so that, just as **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΣ"—Christos</note> was raised from the dead through the glory of the **FATHER** <note>original: "ΠΡΣ"—Patros</note>, so we too might walk in newness of life.

<margin>7</margin> For if we have been united with Him in a death like His, we shall certainly also be united with Him in a resurrection like His. We know this: that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be enslaved to sin. For the one who has died has been set free <note>literally "justified" or "acquitted"</note> from sin.

Now if we died with **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΩ"—Christō</note>, we believe that we will also live with Him. For we know that **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΣ"—Christos</note>, being raised from the dead, will never die again; death no longer has mastery over Him.

<summary>This page contains Paul’s pivotal comparison between the "fall" of Adam and the "grace" of Christ, arguing that while one man brought death, one man brings life. It also introduces the theology of baptism as a literal "dying" to one's old life in order to be raised in a new, sin-free existence.</summary>

<margin>1</margin> **PAUL**, an apostle of **JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "ΙΥ ΧΥ"—Iesou Christou; Nomina Sacra abbreviations</note> through the will of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note>, and Sosthenes our brother, to the church of **GOD** that is in Corinth, to those who have been sanctified in **CHRIST JESUS** <note>original: "ΧΩ ΙΥ"—Christo Iesou</note>, called to be saints, together with all those in every place who call upon the name of our **LORD JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "ΚΥ ΗΜΩΝ ΙΥ ΧΥ"—Kyriou Hemon Iesou Christou</note>, both theirs and ours.
<margin>X</margin> Grace to you and peace from **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note> our Father and the **LORD JESUS CHRIST** <note>original: "ΚΥ ΙΥ ΧΥ"—Kyrio Iesou Christo</note>.
<margin>C</margin> I thank my **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theo</note> always concerning you for the grace of **GOD** which was given to you in **CHRIST JESUS**, because in everything you were enriched in him, in every word and all knowledge, even as the testimony of **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΥ"—Christou</note> was confirmed in you, so that you do not lack in any gift <note>original: "χαρίσματι"—charismati; referring to spiritual endowments</note> while you eagerly await the revelation of our **LORD JESUS CHRIST**, who will also confirm you until the end, so that you are blameless in the day of our **LORD JESUS CHRIST**.
<margin>Π</margin> **GOD** <note>original: "ΘC"—Theos</note> is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, **JESUS CHRIST** our **LORD**.
<margin>Γ</margin> Now I exhort you, brothers, through the name of our **LORD JESUS CHRIST**, that you all say the same thing and that there be no divisions <note>original: "σχίσματα"—schismata; from which we get the word 'schism'</note> among you, but that you be knit together in the same mind and in the same purpose. For it was made clear to me concerning you, my brothers, by those of Chloe’s household, that there are rivalries among you. Now I mean this: that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” and “I am of Apollos,” and “I am of Cephas <note>Cephas is the Aramaic name for the apostle Peter.</note>,” and “I am of **CHRIST**.” Is **CHRIST** <note>original: "XC"—Christos</note> divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul? I thank my **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theo</note> that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius, so that no one may say that you were baptized into my name. I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know if I bap-

<column-break/>

tized any other. For **CHRIST** did not send me to baptize but to preach the gospel—not with wisdom of speech <note>original: "σοφία λόγου"—sophia logou; referring to the clever oratory prized in Greek culture</note>, so that the cross of **CHRIST** should not be emptied of its power. For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of **GOD**. For it is written:
<margin>A</margin> “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the discernment of the discerning I will set aside.”
<margin>Π</margin> Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has **GOD** not made foolish the wisdom of the world? For since, in the wisdom of **GOD**, the world through its wisdom did not know **GOD**, it pleased **GOD** through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe. For Jews demand signs and Greeks seek wisdom, but we preach **CHRIST** crucified: a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles, but to those who are called—both Jews and Greeks—**CHRIST** is the power of **GOD** and the wisdom of **GOD**. Because the foolishness of **GOD** is wiser than men <note>original: "ΑΝΩΝ"—anthropon; Nomina Sacra for humans</note>, and the weakness of **GOD** is stronger than men. For consider 
<margin>Γ</margin> your calling, brothers: that not many were wise according to the flesh, not many were powerful, not many were of noble birth. But **GOD** chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and **GOD** chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong. And the low-born things of the world and the despised things **GOD** chose—the things that are not—to bring to nothing the things that are, so that no flesh should boast before **GOD**. But of Him you are in **CHRIST JESUS**, who became wisdom to us from **GOD**, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption.

<margin>brothers</margin> <note>original: "ΔΕ ΑΔΕΛΦΟΙ"—the scribe added "now brothers" in the margin after omitting it from the main line</note>, I have figuratively applied to myself and Apollos for your sakes, so that in us you might learn "not to go beyond what is written," <note>A likely reference to following the scriptures rather than human pride</note> so that no one of you becomes puffed up for one against the other. <meta>This page continues the Apostle Paul’s defense of his apostolic authority and his willingness to sacrifice his personal rights for the sake of the Gospel. Who serves as a soldier at his own expense <note>original: "opsōniois"—referring to a soldier’s pay or rations.</note> at any time? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? But we have not used this authority, but we endure all things so that we may not put any hindrance in the way of the Gospel of **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΥ"—Christou</note>. 
Do you not know that those who perform the holy services eat from the temple? And those who attend to the altar share in the offerings of the altar? So also the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΣ"—Kyrios</note> directed those who proclaim the Gospel to get their living from the Gospel. But I have used none of these things. 
And I have not written these things so that it may be done so in my case; for it would be better for me to die than to let anyone make my boast void. For if I preach the Gospel, I have nothing to boast about, for necessity is laid upon me; for woe is me if I do not preach the Gospel. For if I do this voluntarily, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, I am still entrusted with a stewardship. 
What then is my reward? That in my preaching I may offer the Gospel without charge, so as not to make full use of my authority in the Gospel. For though I am free from all, I have made myself a slave to all, so that I might win more people. And to the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might win Jews; to those under the Law as one under the Law, though not being myself under the Law,

<column-break/>

To the weak I became weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by all means I might save some. I do all things for the sake of the Gospel, so that I may become a fellow-partner in it. 
Do you not know that those who run in a stadium <note>original: "stadiō"—referring to the athletic races, likely the Isthmian Games held near Corinth.</note> all run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may win it. Everyone who competes in the games exercises self-control in all things. They then do it to receive a perishable crown <note>original: "stephanon"—a wreath made of leaves (like laurel or celery) that would eventually wither.</note>, but we an imperishable one. Therefore I run in such a way, as not without aim; I box in such a way, as not beating the air; but I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that, after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified. 
<margin>TO :··</margin> For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea; and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea; and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink. Do not be idolaters, as some of them were; just as it is written: "The people sat down to eat and drink, and stood up to play." <note>Quoting Exodus 32:6 regarding the Golden Calf incident.</note> Nor let us act immorally, as some of them did...

Nor grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the **Destroyer** <note>Referring to the angel of death or divine executioner.</note>. Therefore, let the one who thinks he stands watch out lest he fall. No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to man. But **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΣ"—Theos</note> is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also provide the way out, so that you may be able to endure it. Therefore, my beloved, flee from **idolatry**.

I speak as to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say. The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not a **participation** <term>participation: Greek *koinōnia*, meaning a shared fellowship or communion</term> in the blood of **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΥ"—Christou</note>? The bread which we break, is it not a participation in the body of **CHRIST**? Because there is one bread, we, though many, are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.

Consider **Israel** according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar? What am I saying then? That food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything? No, but that what the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to **GOD**. I do not want you to become participants with demons. You cannot drink the cup of the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note> and the cup of demons; you cannot partake of the table of the **LORD** and the table of demons. Or are we provoking the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΝ"—Kyryion</note> to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?

<column-break/>

All things are lawful, but not all things are beneficial. All things are lawful, but not all things build up. Let no one seek his own good, but that of the other. Eat everything sold in the **meat market** <term>meat market: Greek *makellō*, a loanword from the Latin *macellum*</term> without asking questions for conscience’s sake; for "the earth is the **LORD’S**, and its fullness."

If one of the unbelievers invites you and you wish to go, eat everything set before you without asking questions for conscience’s sake. But if someone says to you, "This is **offered in sacrifice**" <note>original: "ιεροθυτον"—hierothyton, a term meaning "sacred sacrifice," likely used by a pagan host to be polite.</note>, do not eat for the sake of the one who informed you and for conscience’s sake—I mean conscience, not your own, but the other person's. For why is my freedom judged by another’s conscience? If I partake with thankfulness, why am I slandered because of that for which I give thanks?

Whether then you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note>. Give no offense to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of **GOD**, just as I also try to please everyone in everything, not seeking my own advantage but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

<margin>80 : ~ |</margin>
Become **imitators** of me, as I am of **CHRIST**. I praise you because you remember me in everything and maintain the **traditions** <term>traditions: Greek *paradosis*, referring to the oral teachings handed down by the apostles</term> just as I delivered them to you.

<margin>11 ~ |</margin>
But I want you to know that the head of every man is **CHRIST**, and the head of woman is the man, and the head of **CHRIST** is **GOD**. Every man who prays or prophesies with something over his head dishonors his head. And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is one and the same as if she were shaved. For if a woman is not covered, let her also have her hair cut off; but if it is shameful for a woman...

### 1 Corinthians 11:6–12:3

...shorn or shaved is shameful for a woman, let her cover her head.
<margin>Λ</margin> For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, being the **image and glory of GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou. In early manuscripts, sacred names were abbreviated with a line over them, known as Nomina Sacra.</note>; but woman is the glory of man. For man is not from woman, but woman from man. And indeed, man was not created for the woman, but woman for the man. For this reason, the woman ought to have **authority** <term>authority: likely referring to a head covering as a sign of her status or protection</term> on her head, because of the angels.
<margin>Π</margin> Nevertheless, neither is woman independent of man, nor man independent of woman, in the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΩ"—Kyriō</note>. For just as the woman came from the man, so also the man comes through the woman; but all things come from **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note>.
<margin>Κ</margin> Judge for yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theō</note> uncovered? Does not nature itself teach you that if a man wears long hair, it is a dishonor to him? But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, because her hair is given to her in place of a **covering** <note>original: "peribolaiou," meaning a cloak or wrap.</note>.
<margin>Φ</margin> But if anyone intends to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note>.
But in giving these instructions, I do not praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse. For first of all, when you come together as a church, I hear that **divisions** <term>divisions: Greek "schismata," from which we get the word "schism"</term> exist among you, and in part I believe it. For there must also be factions among you, so that those who are **genuine** <note>original: "dokimoi," meaning those who have been tested and approved.</note> may become evident among you.
<margin>Ο</margin> Therefore, when you meet together in the same place, it is not to eat the **LORD’S** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriakon</note> Supper. For each one takes his own supper first in the eating; and one is hungry, while another is drunk. For do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise the church of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note> and humiliate those who have nothing?

<column-break/>

What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this, I do not praise you. For I received from the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note> that which I also delivered to you: that the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΣ"—Kyrios</note> on the night in which he was betrayed took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is for you; do this in **remembrance** <term>remembrance: Greek "anamnēsin," a sacrificial or ritual memorial</term> of me.”
<margin>(</margin> In the same way, he also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me.” For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the **LORD’S** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note> death until he comes.
<margin>(</margin> Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note> unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note>. But let a person examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup. For the one who eats and drinks without **discerning** <note>original: "diakrinōn," meaning to distinguish or judge rightly.</note> the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.
Because of this, many among you are weak and sick, and a number have fallen asleep. But if we judged ourselves rightly, we would not be judged. But when we are judged by the **LORD** <note>original: "ΚΥ"—Kyriou</note>, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned along with the world.
<margin>(</margin> Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another. If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you do not come together for judgment. And the rest I will set in order whenever I come.
<margin>12</margin> Now concerning **spiritual matters** <term>spiritual matters: Greek "pneumatikōn," referring to spiritual gifts or people</term>, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant. You know that when you were pagans, you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led. Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking by the **SPIRIT OF GOD** <note>original: "ΠΝΙ ΘΥ"—Pneumati Theou</note> says, “Jesus is accursed,” and no one can say “**JESUS IS LORD**” <note>original: "ΚΣ ΙΣ"—Kyrios Iēsous</note> except by the **HOLY SPIRIT** <note>original: "ΠΝΙΑΓΙΩ"—Pneumati Agiō</note>.

### 1 Corinthians 12:2–12:21

<unclear>...when you were [Gentiles], you were led toward speechless idols, however you were led astray.</unclear>
Therefore, I make known to you that no one speaking in the **SPIRIT** <note>original: "ΠΝΙ"—Pneumati. An abbreviation for the Holy Spirit.</note> of **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΥ"—Theou</note> says, "Jesus is accursed," and no one can say, "Jesus is **LORD**" <note>original: "ΚΣ"—Kyrios</note> except by the **HOLY SPIRIT** <note>original: "ΠΝΙ ΑΓΙΩ"</note>.
Now there are varieties of **gifts** <term>gifts: "charismata," referring to spiritual endowments or "grace-gifts" given for the benefit of the community</term>, but the same **SPIRIT**; and there are varieties of ministries, and the same **LORD**; and there are varieties of activities, but it is the same **GOD** who works all things in everyone.
To each is given the manifestation of the **SPIRIT** for the common good. To one is given through the **SPIRIT** a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge according to the same **SPIRIT**, to another faith by the same **SPIRIT**, to another **gifts of healing** by the one **SPIRIT**, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the discernment of spirits, to another various kinds of **tongues** <term>tongues: "glōssōn," ecstatic or inspired speech in different languages or heavenly dialects</term>, and to another the interpretation of tongues.
All these are empowered by one and the same **SPIRIT**, distributing to each one individually just as He wills.
For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΡΣ"—Christos</note>. For in one **SPIRIT** we were all baptized into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free—and we were all made to drink of one **SPIRIT**.
For the body does not consist of one member but of many. If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body. And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body. If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
<margin>—</margin> But as it is, **GOD** has arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as He chose. If all were a single member, where would the body be? As it is, there are many members, yet one body. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you,"

<column-break/>

### 1 Corinthians 12:21–13:3

nor again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you." On the contrary, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and those members of the body that we think less honorable we clothe with greater honor, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty, whereas our more presentable parts do not need this. But **GOD** has so composed the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it, so that there may be no **division** <note>original: "schisma," the root of the English word "schism."</note> in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another. If one member suffers, all suffer together; if a member is honored, all rejoice together.
Now you are the body of **CHRIST** <note>original: "ΧΡΥ"—Christou</note> and individually members of it. And **GOD** has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, helping, leadership, and various kinds of tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles? Do all possess gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
But earnestly desire the greater gifts. And I will show you a still more excellent way.
<margin>13.~</margin> If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not **love** <term>love: "agapē," specifically referring to selfless, divine-like love rather than romantic or brotherly affection</term>, I am a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.
And if I have prophetic powers, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
If I give away all my possessions, and if I deliver up my body in order to **boast** <note>original: "kauchēsōmai." Some manuscripts read "that I may be burned," but this ancient uncial likely supports the "boast" reading.</note>, but have not love, I gain nothing.

### 1 Corinthians 13:4 — 14:20

**Love** is patient, **love** is kind; **love** does not envy, **love** does not boast, it is not arrogant, it does not act unbecomingly, it does not seek its own, it is not provoked, it does not keep a record of wrongs, it does not rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices together with the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. **Love** never fails.

But whether there are prophecies, they will be abolished; whether there are **tongues** <term>tongues: "glōssai," referring to ecstatic, inspired, or foreign languages given by the Spirit</term>, they will cease; whether there is knowledge, it will be abolished. For we know in part and we prophesy in part, but when the perfect comes, that which is in part will be abolished.

When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I thought as a child, I reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I abolished the things of the child. For we see now through a mirror in a riddle <note>original: "en ainigmati," often translated as "dimly" or "obscurely," referring to the polished metal mirrors of antiquity which gave an imperfect reflection</note>, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know fully, just as I also have been fully known.

And now remain faith, hope, **love**—these three; but the greatest of these is **love**.

<margin>Chapter 14</margin> Pursue **love**, and desire the spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy. For the one speaking in a **tongue** speaks not to men but to **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theō (abbreviated nomen sacrum)</note>; for no one understands, but in the spirit he speaks mysteries. But the one who prophesies speaks to men for edification and encouragement and consolation.

The one speaking in a **tongue** edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church. Now I want you all to speak in **tongues**, but rather that you may prophesy. Greater is the one who prophesies than the one speaking in **tongues**, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive edification. But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in **tongues**, what will I profit you

<column-break/>

unless I speak to you either in revelation or in knowledge or in prophecy or in teaching? Even lifeless things giving a sound, whether a flute or a harp, if they do not give a distinction in the notes, how will it be known what is played on the flute or the harp? For indeed, if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will prepare for battle?

So also you, through the **tongue**, unless you give an intelligible word, how will what is spoken be known? For you will be speaking into the air. There are, perhaps, so many kinds of languages in the world, and none is without meaning. If then I do not know the power of the language, I will be a barbarian <note>original: "barbaros"—to the Greeks, this referred to anyone who did not speak Greek, whose speech sounded like "bar-bar"</note> to the one speaking, and the one speaking will be a barbarian to me.

So also you, since you are zealots for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound for the edification of the church. Therefore, the one speaking in a **tongue** should pray that he may interpret. For if I pray in a **tongue**, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful. What then is it? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the mind.

Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will the one occupying the place of the outsider <term>outsider: "idiōtou," a person who is unlearned or a layperson without the specific gift of tongues</term> say the "Amen" at your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying? For you indeed give thanks well, but the other is not edified.

I thank **GOD** <note>original: "ΘΩ"—Theō</note> that I speak in **tongues** more than all of you; but in church I want to speak five words with my mind, so that I may also instruct others, rather than ten thousand words in a **tongue**.

Brothers, do not be children in your thinking, but in malice be infants, and in your thinking be mature.

### 1 Corinthians 14:21 — 15:12

In the law it is written: "By people of other tongues and by the lips of others I will speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to me," says the **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΣ"—Kyrios (Lord). # 1 Corinthians 15:12–44

...from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ <note>original: **XC**, abbreviation for *Christos*.</note> has been raised; and if Christ <note>original: **XC**</note> has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith is in vain. 

<margin>-</margin> **W**e are even found to be false witnesses of God <note>original: **ΘΥ**, abbreviation for *Theou* (God).</note>, because we testified against God <note>original: **ΘΥ**</note> that he raised Christ <note>original: **ΧΝ**, abbreviation for *Christon*.</note>, whom he did not raise if it is true that the dead are not raised. For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ <note>original: **XC**</note> has been raised. And if Christ <note>original: **XC**</note> has not been raised, your faith is futile and you are still in your sins. Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ <note>original: **ΧΩ**, abbreviation for *Christō*.</note> have perished. If in this life only we have hoped in Christ <note>original: **ΧΩ**</note>, we are of all people <note>original: **ΑΝΘΝ**, abbreviation for *anthrōpōn* (humans).</note> most to be pitied. But in fact Christ <note>original: **XC**</note> has been raised from the dead, the first fruits <note>term: *aparchē* — the first portion of a harvest, which serves as a pledge for the rest.</note> of those who have fallen asleep. For since death came through a human <note>original: **ΑΝΘΥ**, abbreviation for *anthrōpou*.</note>, the resurrection of the dead has also come through a human <note>original: **ΑΝΘΥ**</note>. For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ <note>original: **ΧΩ**</note> shall all be made alive. But each in his own order: 

<margin>-</margin> **C**hrist <note>original: **XC**</note> the first fruits, then at his coming those who belong to Christ <note>original: **XY**</note>. Then comes the end, when he delivers the kingdom to God <note>original: **ΘΩ**</note> the Father after destroying every rule and every authority and power. For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy to be destroyed is death. For "God has put all things in subjection under his feet." But when it says, "all things are put in subjection," it is plain that he is excepted who put all things in subjection under him. When all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to him who put all things in subjection under him, that God <note>original: **ΘC**, abbreviation for *Theos*.</note> may be all in all. Otherwise, what do people mean by being bap-

<column-break/>

-tized on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized on their behalf? Why are we also in danger every hour? I die every day! That is as certain, brothers, as the boasting in you which I have in Christ <note>original: **ΧΩ**</note> Jesus <note>original: **ΙΥ**, abbreviation for *Iēsou*.</note> our Lord <note>original: **ΚΩ**, abbreviation for *Kyriō*.</note>. If with merely human <note>original: **ΑΝΘ**</note> motives I fought with wild beasts at Ephesus, what do I gain? If the dead are not raised, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." <note>Paul quotes a common skeptical proverb, likely from Isaiah 22:13.</note> Do not be deceived: "Bad company ruins good morals." <note>Paul is quoting the Greek poet Menander here.</note> Wake up from your drunken stupor, as is right, and do not go on sinning. For some have no knowledge of God <note>original: **ΘΥ**</note>. I say this to your shame.

<margin>-</margin> **B**ut someone will ask, "How are the dead raised? With what kind of body do they come?" You foolish person! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies. And as for what you sow, you do not sow the body that is to be, but a bare kernel <note>original: **ΚΟΚΚΟΝ**, *kokkon* — a grain or seed.</note>, perhaps of wheat or of some other grain. But God <note>original: **ΘC**</note> gives it a body as he has chosen, and to each kind of seed its own body. For not all flesh is the same, but there is one kind for humans <note>original: **ΑΝΘΩ**</note>, another for animals, another for birds, and another for fish. There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly is of one kind, and the glory of the earthly is of another. There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for star differs from star in glory.

<margin>-</margin> **S**o is it with the resurrection of the dead. What is sown is perishable; what is raised is imperishable. It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power. It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.

<summary>This page contains Paul's foundational theological argument for the resurrection, using the metaphor of a seed dying to produce a new body. He argues that if Christ was not raised, the Christian faith is meaningless, but his resurrection serves as the "first fruits" for all believers.</summary>

<margin>12</margin> because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, so that I would not be too exalted, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan, so that it might buffet me, so that I would not be too exalted. <note>Paul uses the term "thorn in the flesh" to describe a persistent physical or spiritual trial; scholars have debated its nature for centuries.</note> Concerning this, three times I pleaded with the Lord <note>original: **ΚΝ**, abbreviation for *Kyrion*</note> that it might depart from me. <meta>This page continues the Apostle Paul's letter to the Galatians, picking up in the middle of chapter 3. <summary>This page contains Paul's foundational ethical instructions, contrasting the destructive behaviors of the "flesh" with the virtuous "fruit of the Spirit." He argues that true Christian freedom is found not in legalism or license, but in serving others through love and mutual support.</summary>

<meta>This page marks the transition between two of Paul’s letters. It concludes the Epistle to the Galatians, where Paul adds a personal, handwritten postscript, and begins the Epistle to the Ephesians with a grand, liturgical opening regarding God’s eternal plan.</meta>

### TO THE EPHESIANS

the one sowing to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption; but the one sowing to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life. And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due season we will reap if we do not lose heart. So then, as we have opportunity, let us work good toward all, and especially toward those of the household of faith. See with what large letters I have written to you with my own hand. <note>Paul usually dictated his letters to a scribe but often wrote the final greeting himself in large, bold letters to prove the letter's authenticity.</note> As many as wish to make a good showing in the flesh, these compel you to be circumcised, only so that they might not be persecuted for the cross of Christ. For not even those who are circumcised keep the law themselves, but they wish you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh. But may it never be for me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision is anything nor uncircumcision, but a new creation. And as many as will walk by this rule, peace be upon them and mercy, and upon the Israel of God. From now on, let no one cause me troubles; for I bear the <term>marks</term> <note>original: **στίγματα** (*stigmata*); these were physical scars or brands. Paul likely refers to the scars from his beatings and stonings as proof that he belongs to Jesus, just as a slave might be branded by a master.</note> of Jesus on my body. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

->Eph. 5:1–33<-

<column-break/>

**B**e therefore imitators of **God** <note>original: **ΘΥ**; Nomina Sacra abbreviation for *Theou*.</note> as beloved children, and walk in love, just as **Christ** <note>original: **ΧϹ**; Nomina Sacra abbreviation for *Christos*.</note> also loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to **God** <note>original: **ΘΩ**; abbreviation for *Theō*.</note> for a sweet-smelling aroma.

**B**ut sexual immorality and all impurity or greed, let it not even be named among you, as is proper for <term>saints</term> <note>literally "holy ones," referring to the members of the early Christian community.</note>; and filthiness or foolish talking or crude joking, which are not fitting, but rather thanksgiving. For this you know with certainty, that no sexually immoral or impure or greedy person—who is an idolater—has an inheritance in the kingdom of **Christ** <note>original: **ΧΥ**; abbreviation for *Christou*.</note> and **God** <note>original: **ΘΥ**; abbreviation for *Theou*.</note>.

**L**et no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of **God** <note>original: **ΘΥ**; abbreviation for *Theou*.</note> comes upon the sons of disobedience. Therefore do not be partakers with them. For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the **Lord** <note>original: **ΚΩ**; abbreviation for *Kyriō*.</note>; walk as children of light—for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth—proving what is well-pleasing to the **Lord** <note>original: **ΚΩ**; abbreviation for *Kyriō*.</note>.

**A**nd do not participate in the unfruitful works of darkness, but instead even expose them. For the things done in secret by them are shameful even to mention. But all things being exposed by the light are made visible, for everything that is made visible is light. Therefore it says:
<margin>></margin> "Awake, O sleeper, and arise from the dead, and **Christ** <note>original: **ΧϹ**; abbreviation for *Christos*.</note> will shine upon you."

**L**ook carefully then how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the **Lord** <note>original: **ΚΥ**; abbreviation for *Kyriou*.</note> is.

<column-break/>

<margin>></margin> **A**nd do not get drunk with wine, in which is debauchery, but be filled with the **Spirit** <note>original: **ΠΝΙ**; Nomina Sacra abbreviation for *Pneumati*.</note>, speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the **Lord** <note>original: **ΚΩ**; abbreviation for *Kyriō*.</note>, giving thanks always for all things in the name of our **Lord** <note>original: **ΚΥ**; abbreviation for *Kyriou*.</note> **Jesus Christ** <note>original: **ΙΥ ΧΥ**; abbreviations for *Iēsou Christou*.</note> to **God** <note>original: **ΘΩ**; abbreviation for *Theō*.</note> even the **Father** <note>original: **ΠΡΙ**; abbreviation for *Patri*.</note>, submitting to one another in the fear of **Christ** <note>original: **ΧΥ**; abbreviation for *Christou*.</note>.

<margin>></margin> **W**ives, submit to your own husbands as to the **Lord** <note>original: **ΚΩ**; abbreviation for *Kyriō*.</note>, for the husband is the head of the wife as also **Christ** <note>original: **ΧϹ**; abbreviation for *Christos*.</note> is the head of the church, he himself being the savior of the body. But as the church is subject to **Christ** <note>original: **ΧΩ**; abbreviation for *Christō*.</note>, so also wives should be to their husbands in everything.

<margin>ʘ</margin> **H**usbands, love your wives, just as **Christ** <note>original: **ΧϹ**; abbreviation for *Christos*.</note> also loved the church and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, that he might present the church to himself in splendor, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she might be holy and blameless.

**S**o also husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as also **Christ** <note>original: **ΧϹ**; abbreviation for *Christos*.</note> does the church, because we are members of his body.

<margin>></margin> "For this reason a **man** <note>original: **ΑΝΟϹ**; Nomina Sacra for *anthrōpos*.</note> shall leave his **father** <note>original: **ΠΡΑ**; abbreviation for *patera*.</note> and **mother** <note>original: **ΜΡΑ**; abbreviation for *mētera*.</note> and shall be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh." This mystery is great, but I am speaking regarding **Christ** <note>original: **ΧΝ**; abbreviation for *Christon*.</note> and the church. Nevertheless, each one of you also must love his own wife as himself.

<meta>This page concludes the Epistle to the Ephesians. It transitions from the household codes of Chapter 5—specifically the duties of wives and husbands—into Chapter 6, which covers the duties of children, parents, slaves, and masters. The letter famously concludes with the "Armor of God" metaphor and a personal greeting regarding Tychicus.</meta>

<margin>6</margin>**A**nd the wife, let her fear her husband <note>original: **ΗΔΕΓΥΝΗΙΝΑΦΟΒΗΤΑΙΤΟΝΑΝΔΡΑ**; "fear" here implies deep respect or reverence within the cultural context of the time.</note>.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Epistle to the Philippians. The previous page concluded the Epistle to the Ephesians with instructions on the "Armor of God" and personal greetings. # TO THE PHILIPPIANS

->**PAUL AND TIMOTHY**,<-
servants of **Christ Jesus**, to all the saints in **Christ Jesus** who are in **Philippi**, along with the overseers <note>original: **ΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΙΣ**; traditionally translated as bishops or church leaders</note> and deacons: **Grace** to you and **peace** from **God** our **Father** and the **Lord Jesus Christ**.

I thank my **God** <note>original: **ΘΩ**; Nomina Sacra abbreviation for *Theō*</note> in all my remembrance of you, always in every prayer of mine for you all, making the prayer with joy because of your partnership in the **Gospel** <note>original: **ΕΥΑΓΓΕΛΙΟΝ**; literally "Good News"</note> from the first day until now. I am confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion until the day of **Jesus Christ**. 

Just as it is right for me to think this about you all, because I have you in my heart, both in my imprisonment <note>original: **ΔΕΣΜΟΙΣ**; literally "bonds" or "chains"</note> and in the defense and confirmation of the **Gospel**, you are all partners in grace with me. For **God** is my witness, how I long for you all with the deep affection <note>original: **ΣΠΛΑΓΧΝΟΙΣ**; literally "bowels," used to describe intense, gut-level emotion and compassion</note> of **Christ Jesus**. 

And this I pray, that your love may overflow more and more in knowledge and all discernment, so that you may approve the things that are excellent, in order that you may be pure and blameless for the day of **Christ**, filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through **Jesus Christ** to the glory and praise of **God**.

Now I want you to know, brothers, that the things concerning me have actually turned out for the progress of the **Gospel**, so that my imprisonment for **Christ** has become well known throughout the entire praetorium <note>original: **ΠΡΑΙΤΩΡΙΩ**; refers to the elite Imperial Guard or the governor’s headquarters</note> and to all the rest, and most of the brothers, having become confident in the **Lord** because of my imprisonment, dare all the more fearlessly to speak the word of **God**.

<column-break/>

Some indeed preach **Christ** <note>original: **ΧΝ**; Nomina Sacra abbreviation for *Christon*</note> even from envy and strife, but some also from good will. The former out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the **Gospel**; but the latter proclaim **Christ** out of selfish ambition, not purely, thinking to stir up affliction in my imprisonment. 

What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, **Christ** is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will rejoice, for I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your prayer and the provision of the **Spirit** <note>original: **ΠΝΣ**; Nomina Sacra for *Pneumatos*</note> of **Jesus Christ**, according to my eager expectation and hope that I will be put to shame in nothing, but with all boldness, as always, now also **Christ** will be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.

For to me, to live is **Christ** and to die is gain. But if to live in the flesh means fruitful labor for me, then what I shall choose I do not know. I am hard-pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and be with **Christ**, for that is far better; but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake. And being confident of this, I know that I will remain and continue with you all for your progress and joy in the faith, so that your boasting may overflow in **Christ Jesus** in me through my presence with you again.

Only conduct yourselves <note>original: **ΠΟΛΙΤΕΥΕΣΘΑΙ**; literally "live as a citizen," implying the duties one has to a community or heavenly kingdom</note> worthily of the **Gospel** of **Christ**, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear about your circumstances, that you are standing firm in one spirit, with one soul striving together for the faith of the **Gospel**, and not being frightened in anything by your opponents. This is a sign of destruction to them, but of your salvation, and this from **God**. For it... <note>The text cuts off here at the bottom of the page.</note>

<summary>This page contains the opening of Paul's letter to the Philippians, where he expresses his deep affection for the congregation and explains how his imprisonment has actually helped spread the Gospel. He reflects on his own mortality, famously stating "to live is Christ and to die is gain," before exhorting the Philippians to live worthily of their faith.</summary>
<keywords>Philippians, Paul, Timothy, imprisonment, Gospel, Praetorium, joy, salvation, life and death, citizenship</keywords>

<column-break/>

...and so we will always be with the Lord <note>original: **ΚΩ** (*Kyriō*)</note>. Therefore, <margin>Chapter 5</margin> **e**ncourage <note>The bold **Λ** in the Greek text is the final part of the word *parakaleite*, meaning 'to comfort' or 'encourage'</note> one another with these words. 

Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you. For you yourselves know accurately that the day of the Lord <note>original: **ΚΥ** (*Kyriou*)</note> comes like a thief in the night. When they say, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction comes upon them like labor pains on a woman with child, and they will by no means escape.

**B**ut you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief. For you are all children of light and children of the day. We are not of the night or of darkness. So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us stay alert and be sober. For those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk are drunk at night. But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, **p**utting on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation. For God <note>original: **ΘC** (*Theos*)</note> has not destined us for wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord <note>original: **ΚΥ** (*Kyriou*)</note> Jesus Christ <note>original: **ΙΗ ΧΥ** (*Iēsou Christou*)</note>, who died for us so that whether we are awake or asleep we might live together with Him.

Therefore encourage one another and build one another up, just as you are doing.

**W**e ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labor among you and are over you in the Lord <note>original: **ΚΩ** (*Kyriō*)</note> and admonish you, and to esteem them very highly in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves. And we urge you, brothers, admonish the unruly, encourage the faint-hearted, help the weak, be patient with everyone. See that no one repays evil for evil...

The scribe has concluded the first epistle with a formal "subscription" or colophon indicating its supposed origin, followed by the title and opening of the second epistle. The text uses "Nomina Sacra," which are shortened forms of holy names like God, Jesus, and Spirit, marked by a horizontal bar in the original Greek.</meta>

# TO THE THESSALONIANS II

Paul and Silvanus and Timothy to the church of the Thessalonians in God <note>original: **ΘΩ** (*Theō*)</note> our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ <note>original: **ΚΥ ΙΥ ΧΩ** (*Kyriō Iēsou Christō*)</note>:
Grace to you and peace from God <note>original: **ΘΥ** (*Theou*)</note> our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ <note>original: **ΚΥ ΙΥ ΧΥ** (*Kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou*)</note>.
We ought to thank God <note>original: **ΘΩ** (*Theō*)</note> always for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing abundantly and the love of every one of you all for one another is increasing, so that we ourselves boast about you in the churches of God <note>original: **ΘΥ** (*Theou*)</note> for your perseverance and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions that you endure. This is evidence of the righteous judgment of God <note>original: **ΘΥ** (*Theou*)</note>, so that you may be considered worthy of the kingdom of God <note>original: **ΘΥ** (*Theou*)</note>, for which you are also suffering.
Since it is just for God <note>original: **ΘΩ** (*Theō*)</note> to repay with affliction those who afflict you, and to give relief to you who are afflicted along with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus <note>original: **ΚΥ ΙΥ** (*Kyriou Iēsou*)</note> from heaven with His mighty angels in flaming fire, inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God <note>original: **ΘΝ** (*Theon*)</note> and to those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus <note>original: **ΚΥ ΗΜΩΝ ΙΥ** (*Kyriou hēmōn Iēsou*)</note>. They will suffer the penalty of eternal destruction away from the presence of the Lord <note>original: **ΚΥ** (*Kyriou*)</note> and from the glory of His power, when He comes to be glorified among His saints and to be marveled at among all those who have believed—because our testimony to you was believed—on that day.
To this end we also pray always for you, that our God <note>original: **ΘΣ** (*Theos*)</note> may count you worthy of the calling and fulfill every desire for goodness and work of faith with power, so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ <note>original: **ΚΥ ΗΜΩΝ ΙΥ ΧΥ** (*Kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou*)</note> may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God <note>original: **ΘΥ** (*Theou*)</note> and the Lord Jesus Christ <note>original: **ΚΥ ΙΥ ΧΥ** (*Kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou*)</note>.

And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will consume with the <term>breath of his mouth</term> <note>A metaphor for divine power and judgment</note> and will destroy by the appearance of his coming. And for this reason, God sends them a working of delusion so that they believe the lie, in order that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness.

For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: that if anyone does not want to work, neither

<meta>This page continues the Epistle to the Hebrews. The previous page discussed the "Rest" of God and the failure of the Exodus generation to enter it through unbelief. Since then we have a great **high priest** <note>original: "archierea" — the chief religious official who acted as a mediator between God and the people</note> who has passed through the heavens, **Jesus the Son of God** <note>original: "IN̅ TON YN̅ TOY THY̅" — these are "nomina sacra," or sacred names, which scribes abbreviated with horizontal bars to show reverence</note>, let us hold fast to our **confession** <note>original: "homologias" — our public declaration of faith</note>. For we do not have a high priest who is unable to **sympathize** <note>original: "sympathēsai" — to suffer along with or feel the same pain</note> with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us then approach with confidence the **throne of grace** <note>a metaphor for God's presence, where mercy is given freely</note>, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.

<margin>5:~</margin> For every high priest chosen from among mortals is put in charge of things pertaining to **God** <note>original: "THN̅"</note> on their behalf, to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins. He is able to deal gently with the ignorant and wayward, since he himself is subject to weakness; and because of this he must offer sacrifice for his own sins as well as for those of the people. And one does not take this honor on oneself, but only when called by **God** <note>original: "THY̅"</note>, just as **Aaron** <note>the brother of Moses and the first high priest of Israel</note> was. <meta>This page continues the Epistle to the Hebrews, specifically chapters 6 and 7. The previous page concluded with an encouragement toward hope and the mention of Jesus entering the inner sanctuary as a high priest in the line of Melchizedek. This page provides the biblical-theological justification for why Jesus’s priesthood is superior to the traditional Jewish (Levitical) priesthood by examining the mysterious Old Testament figure Melchizedek.</meta>

...your work and the **love** <note>original: "agapēs"</note> which you demonstrated toward His name, in that you served the **saints** <note>original: "hagiois" — a term used by early Christians to refer to all members of the faith community</note> and continue to serve them. We desire each one of you to show the same diligence toward the full assurance of **hope** until the end, so that you may not become sluggish, but rather imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the **promises**.

For when **God** <note>original: "ΘC" — a "nomen sacrum" or sacred shorthand for 'Theos'</note> made a promise to **Abraham**, since He had no one greater by whom to swear, He swore by Himself, saying: "Surely blessing I will bless you and multiplying I will multiply you." And so, after waiting patiently, Abraham obtained the promise. For humans swear by something greater than themselves, and the **oath** serves as a confirmation that ends all dispute. 

In the same way, **God** <note>original: "ΘC"</note>, desiring even more to show the heirs of the promise the unchangeable nature of His purpose, guaranteed it with an oath. This was so that through two unchangeable things <note>God's word and God's oath</note>, in which it is impossible for **God** <note>original: "ΘΝ" — 'Theon'</note> to lie, we who have taken refuge might have strong encouragement to seize the **hope** set before us. 

We have this hope as an **anchor of the soul** <note>a classic metaphor for spiritual stability</note>, both certain and steadfast, which enters into the inner place behind the **curtain** <note>referring to the 'veil' in the Temple that separated the Holy of Holies, the residence of God's presence, from the rest of the world</note>. There, **Jesus** <note>original: "ΙC" — sacred shorthand for 'Iēsous'</note> has entered as a **forerunner** on our behalf, having become a **high priest** forever according to the order of **Melchizedek**.

For this **Melchizedek**, king of **Salem**, priest of the **Most High God** <note>original: "ΘΥ ΤΟΥ ΥΨΙCΤΟΥ"</note>, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him. To him Abraham also apportioned a **tenth** <note>a tithe, or 10% of the spoils of war</note> of everything. His name is first translated as "**King of Righteousness**," and then also "**King of Salem**," which means...

<column-break/>

..."**King of Peace**." 

He is without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the **Son of God** <note>original: "ΥΙΩ ΤΟΥ ΘΥ"</note>, he remains a priest forever. Consider how great this man was, to whom even **Abraham** the **patriarch** <note>the founding father of the Israelite nation</note> gave a tenth of the choice spoils. 

Now those of the sons of **Levi** who receive the priestly office have a commandment according to the **Law** <note>the Torah, or Mosaic Law</note> to collect tithes from the people—that is, from their own kindred—even though these also are descended from Abraham. But this man <note>Melchizedek</note>, who does not share their genealogy, collected tithes from Abraham and blessed him who had received the promises. It is beyond all dispute that the **lesser** is blessed by the **greater**. 

In the one case, tithes are received by mortal men; but in the other, by one of whom it is testified that he lives on. One might even say that **Levi** himself, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham, for he was still "in the loins" of his ancestor <note>meaning he was a future descendant</note> when Melchizedek met him.

Now if **perfection** <note>meaning full spiritual access to God</note> had been attainable through the **Levitical priesthood** (for under it the people received the Law), what further need would there have been for another priest to arise according to the order of **Melchizedek**, rather than one according to the order of **Aaron**? For when there is a change in the priesthood, there is necessarily a change in the **Law** as well. 

For the one of whom these things are spoken belongs to another **tribe** <note>the tribe of Judah</note>, from which no one has ever served at the **altar**. For it is evident that our **Lord** <note>original: "KC" — sacred shorthand for 'Kyrios'</note> descended from **Judah**, a tribe about which **Moses** said nothing regarding priests. This becomes even more evident if another priest arises in the likeness of **Melchizedek**, who has become a priest not according to a legal requirement concerning physical descent...

->Heb. vi. 10—vii. 16<-

See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking. For if those people did not escape when they refused the one who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we turn away from the one who warns from heaven? At that time, his voice shook the earth; but now he has promised, saying: "Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven." This phrase, "Yet once more," indicates the removal of what is shaken—that is, created things—so that what cannot be shaken may remain.

Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us give thanks, by which we may offer service pleasing to **God** <note>original: "ΘΩ"</note> with reverence and awe; for indeed, our **God** <note>original: "ΘΣ"</note> is a consuming fire.

# First Letter to Timothy

...forever and ever. Amen.
I appeal to you, brothers, bear with this word of exhortation, for I have written to you briefly.
Know that our brother **Timothy** <note>original: "ΤΙΜΟΘΕΟΝ"</note> has been released, with whom I shall see you if he comes shortly.
Greet all your leaders and all the **saints** <term>hagioi: a term used for the members of the early Christian community, meaning "set apart" or "holy ones"</term>. Those from Italy greet you.
**Grace** <note>original: "Η ΧΑΡΙϹ"</note> be with you all. Amen.

---

->To the Hebrews<-
->Written from<-
->Rome<-
<note>This decorative subscription acts as a "colophon" or concluding title, indicating the tradition that the letter was sent from Rome.</note>

<column-break/>

**Paul**, an apostle of **Jesus Christ** <note>original: "ΙΥ ΧΥ" — Nomina Sacra (sacred abbreviations) for "Iēsou Christou"</note> by command of **God** <note>original: "ΘΥ" — Nomina Sacra for "Theou"</note> our **Savior** <note>original: "ϹΡϹ" — Nomina Sacra for "Sōtēros"</note> and **Christ Jesus** our hope. To **Timothy**, a true child in faith. 
Grace, mercy, and peace from **God** the Father and **Christ Jesus** our **Lord** <note>original: "ΚΥ" — Nomina Sacra for "Kyriou"</note>.

As I urged you to remain in **Ephesus** <note>A major Roman city in modern-day Turkey, known for its temple to Artemis and a large early Christian community.</note> while I was going to Macedonia, so that you might command certain ones not to teach different doctrines, nor to give heed to **myths and endless genealogies** <note>Likely referring to speculative legends or family trees used by rival teachers to claim special spiritual authority.</note>, which promote speculations rather than the **stewardship** <term>oikonomia: the administration or plan of a household, here referring to God’s plan of salvation</term> of **God** which is in faith. 

The goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith. Some people, having missed the mark, have turned aside into empty talk, wanting to be teachers of the **Law** <term>nomodidaskaloi: instructors in the Jewish Torah or religious law</term>, though they understand neither what they say nor the things about which they make confident assertions.

But we know that the Law is good if one uses it lawfully, knowing this: that the Law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers and mothers, for murderers, for the sexually immoral, for **sodomites** <term>arsenokoitais: a term derived from the Greek translation of Leviticus, referring to same-sex behavior</term>, for **kidnappers** <term>andrapodistais: literally "slave-traders" or those who steal people to sell them</term>, for liars, for perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to **sound teaching** <term>hygiainousē didaskalia: literally "healthy" or "wholesome" instruction</term>, according to the glorious gospel of the blessed **God** with which I was entrusted.

I give thanks to the one who has strengthened me, **Christ Jesus** our **Lord**, because he considered me faithful, appointing me to ministry—me, who was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man. But I was shown mercy because I acted ignorantly in unbelief. And the grace of our **Lord** overflowed with the faith and love that are in **Christ Jesus**. This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptance: that **Christ Jesus** came into the world to save sinners...

<meta>This page concludes the First Letter to Timothy with a final doxology and a warning against false teachings, followed by a postscript indicating its origin. ### TO TIMOTHY II

...until the appearing <note>original: "ΕΠΙΦΑΝΕΙΑΣ" (epiphaneias) — the visible manifestation or second coming of Christ.</note> of our **Lord Jesus Christ**, which He will reveal in His own time—He who is the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords, who alone possesses immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no human has seen or is able to see; to Him be honor and eternal might, amen.

To those who are rich in this present age, charge them not to be arrogant, nor to set their hope on the uncertainty of wealth, but on **God**, who richly provides us with all things for our enjoyment. Tell them to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous and ready to share, storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of that which is truly life.

O Timothy, guard the deposit <note>original: "ΠΑΡΑΘΗΚΗΝ" (parathēkēn) — a legal term for a trust or something committed to another's "safe-keeping."</note> entrusted to you. Turn away from godless, empty chatter and the opposing arguments of what is falsely called "knowledge" <note>original: "ΓΝΩΣΕΩΣ" (gnōseōs) — likely a reference to early Gnostic tendencies where "secret knowledge" was prized over traditional faith.</note>, which some have professed and, in doing so, have missed the mark concerning the faith.

**Grace** be with you all.

**Paul**, an apostle of **Christ Jesus** by the will of **God**, according to the promise of life that is in **Christ Jesus**, to Timothy, my beloved child:

**Grace**, mercy, and peace from **God** the Father and **Christ Jesus** our **Lord**.

I give thanks to **God**, whom I serve with a clear conscience as my ancestors did, as I constantly remember you in my prayers night and day. Longing to see you, as I recall your tears, so that I may be filled with joy. I am reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded now lives in you as well.

For this reason, I remind you to fan into flame <note>original: "ΑΝΑΖΩΠΥΡΕΙΝ" (anazōpyrein) — literally to "rekindle" or keep a fire burning.</note> the gift of **God** which is in you through the laying on of my hands. For **God** did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power and of love and of self-control.

Therefore, do not be ashamed of the testimony of our **Lord**, nor of me His prisoner, but join with me in suffering for the gospel according to the power of **God**, who saved us and called us with a holy calling—not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and grace. This grace was given to us in **Christ Jesus** before time began, but has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior **Christ Jesus**, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel. For this gospel I was appointed a herald, an apostle, and a teacher of the nations <note>original: "ΕΘΝΩΝ" (ethnōn) — often translated as "Gentiles" or non-Jewish peoples.</note>. For this reason I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed...

And when the thousand years are finished, **Satan** shall be released from his prison, and he will go out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth—**Gog and Magog**—to gather them together for war; their number is like the sand of the sea.
